<p><b>Portugal</b> (<span style="font-size:85%;">Portuguese pronunciation:&#160;</span><span title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)" class="IPA" lang="pt-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Portuguese" title="Help:IPA/Portuguese">[puɾtuˈɣal]</a></span>), officially the <b>Portuguese Republic</b> (<a href="/wiki/Portuguese_language" title="Portuguese language">Portuguese</a>: <i lang="pt">República Portuguesa</i> <span style="font-size:85%;"></span><span title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)" class="IPA" lang="pt-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Portuguese" title="Help:IPA/Portuguese">[ʁɛˈpuβlikɐ puɾtuˈɣezɐ]</a></span>),<sup id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15">&#91;note 3&#93;</a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/Sovereign_state" title="Sovereign state">country</a> located on the <a href="/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula" title="Iberian Peninsula">Iberian Peninsula</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Southwestern_Europe" title="Southwestern Europe">Southwestern</a> <a href="/wiki/Europe" title="Europe">Europe</a>, and whose territory also includes the <a href="/wiki/Macaronesia" title="Macaronesia">macaronesian</a> <a href="/wiki/Archipelago" title="Archipelago">archipelagos</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Azores" title="Azores">Azores</a>, <a href="/wiki/Madeira" title="Madeira">Madeira</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Savage_Islands" title="Savage Islands">Savage Islands</a>. It features <a href="/wiki/Cabo_da_Roca" title="Cabo da Roca">the westernmost point</a> in <a href="/wiki/Continental_Europe" title="Continental Europe">continental Europe</a>, and its Iberian portion is bordered to the west and south by the Atlantic Ocean and to the north and east by <a href="/wiki/Spain" title="Spain">Spain</a>, the sole country to have a <a href="/wiki/Portugal%E2%80%93Spain_border" title="Portugal–Spain border">land border with Portugal</a>. Its archipelagos form two <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_Regions_of_Portugal" title="Autonomous Regions of Portugal">autonomous regions</a> with their own <a href="/wiki/Local_government" title="Local government">regional governments</a>. In the mainland, <a href="/wiki/Alentejo_region" class="mw-redirect" title="Alentejo region">Alentejo region</a> occupies the biggest area but is one of the regions in Europe with a lower population density. <a href="/wiki/Lisbon" title="Lisbon">Lisbon</a> is the <a href="/wiki/Capital_city" title="Capital city">capital</a> and largest city by population, being also the main spot for tourists alongside <a href="/wiki/Porto" title="Porto">Porto</a> and <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a>.
</p><p>One of the oldest countries in Europe, its territory has been continuously settled, invaded and fought over since <a href="/wiki/Prehistoric_Iberia" title="Prehistoric Iberia">prehistoric times</a>. The territory was first inhabited by the <a href="/wiki/Celts" title="Celts">Celtic</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_the_Pre-Roman_peoples_of_the_Iberian_Peninsula" title="List of the Pre-Roman peoples of the Iberian Peninsula">Iberian</a> peoples, such as the <a href="/wiki/Lusitanians" title="Lusitanians">Lusitanians</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Gallaecians" class="mw-redirect" title="Gallaecians">Gallaecians</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Celtici" title="Celtici">Celtici</a>, <a href="/wiki/Turduli" title="Turduli">Turduli</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Conii" class="mw-redirect" title="Conii">Conii</a>. These peoples had some commercial and cultural contact with <a href="/wiki/Phoenicia" title="Phoenicia">Phoenicians</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Greeks" class="mw-redirect" title="Ancient Greeks">ancient Greeks</a> and <a href="/wiki/Carthaginians" class="mw-redirect" title="Carthaginians">Carthaginians</a>. It was later ruled by the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Republic" title="Roman Republic">Romans</a>, followed by the invasions of <a href="/wiki/Germanic_peoples" title="Germanic peoples">Germanic peoples</a> (most prominently, the <a href="/wiki/Suebi" title="Suebi">Suebi</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Visigoths" title="Visigoths">Visigoths</a>) together with the <a href="/wiki/Alans" title="Alans">Alans</a>, and later the <a href="/wiki/Moors" title="Moors">Moors</a>, who were eventually expelled during the <a href="/wiki/Reconquista" title="Reconquista">Reconquista</a>. Founded first as a <a href="/wiki/County_of_Portugal" title="County of Portugal">county</a> within the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Le%C3%B3n" title="Kingdom of León">Kingdom of León</a> in 868, the country officially gained its independence as the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Portugal" title="Kingdom of Portugal">Kingdom of Portugal</a> with the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Zamora" title="Treaty of Zamora">Treaty of Zamora</a> in 1143.<sup id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16">&#91;13&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Portugal made numerous discoveries and maritime explorations outside the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean" class="mw-redirect" title="Mediterranean">Mediterranean</a> and by the 15th and 16th centuries established one of the longest-lived maritime and commercial empires, becoming one of the main economic and political powers of the time.<sup id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17">&#91;14&#93;</a></sup> At the end of the 16th century, Portugal suffered a <a href="/wiki/War_of_the_Portuguese_Succession" title="War of the Portuguese Succession">war for the crown succession</a> with Spain, leading to the <a href="/wiki/Iberian_Union" title="Iberian Union">Iberian Union</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Restoration_War" title="Portuguese Restoration War">Portuguese Restoration War</a> re-instated the <a href="/wiki/House_of_Braganza" title="House of Braganza">House of Braganza</a> in 1640 after a period of substantial loss to Portugal.<sup id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18">&#91;15&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>By the early 19th century, the accumulative crisis, events such as the <a href="/wiki/1755_Lisbon_earthquake" title="1755 Lisbon earthquake">1755 Lisbon earthquake</a>, the country's occupation during the <a href="/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars" title="Napoleonic Wars">Napoleonic Wars</a>, and the resulting <a href="/wiki/Independence_of_Brazil" title="Independence of Brazil">independence of Brazil</a> in 1822 led to a marked decay of <a href="/wiki/Economic_history_of_Portugal" title="Economic history of Portugal">Portugal's prior opulence</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19">&#91;16&#93;</a></sup> This was followed by the <a href="/wiki/Liberal_Wars" title="Liberal Wars">civil war</a> between <a href="/wiki/Liberalism" title="Liberalism">liberal</a> constitutionalists and conservative absolutists over royal succession, which lasted from 1828 to 1834. The <a href="/wiki/5_October_1910_revolution" title="5 October 1910 revolution">1910 revolution</a> deposed Portugal's centuries-old monarchy, and established the democratic but unstable <a href="/wiki/First_Portuguese_Republic" title="First Portuguese Republic">Portuguese First Republic</a>, later being superseded by the <i><a href="/wiki/Estado_Novo_(Portugal)" title="Estado Novo (Portugal)">Estado Novo</a></i> (New State) authoritarian regime. <a href="/wiki/Democracy" title="Democracy">Democracy</a> was restored after the <a href="/wiki/Carnation_Revolution" title="Carnation Revolution">Carnation Revolution</a> (1974), ending the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Colonial_War" title="Portuguese Colonial War">Portuguese Colonial War</a> and eventually losing its remaining colonial possessions.
</p><p>Portugal has left a profound cultural, architectural and linguistic influence <a href="/wiki/Evolution_of_the_Portuguese_Empire" title="Evolution of the Portuguese Empire">across the globe</a>, with a legacy of around 250 million <a href="/wiki/Lusophone" class="mw-redirect" title="Lusophone">Portuguese speakers</a> around the world. It is a <a href="/wiki/Developed_country" title="Developed country">developed country</a> with an <a href="/wiki/IMF_advanced_economy_list" class="mw-redirect" title="IMF advanced economy list">advanced economy</a> which holds the <a href="/wiki/Gold_reserve" title="Gold reserve">14th largest gold reserve</a> at its <a href="/wiki/Bank_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Bank of Portugal">national central bank</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20">&#91;17&#93;</a></sup> has the 8th largest proven reserves of <a href="/wiki/Lithium" title="Lithium">lithium</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21">&#91;18&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23">&#91;20&#93;</a></sup> with the weight of exports representing 49% of its GDP in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24">&#91;21&#93;</a></sup> A member of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a>, the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Schengen_Area" title="Schengen Area">Schengen Area</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">Council of Europe</a> (CoE), Portugal was also one of the founding members of <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Eurozone" title="Eurozone">eurozone</a>, the <a href="/wiki/OECD" title="OECD">OECD</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Community_of_Portuguese_Language_Countries" title="Community of Portuguese Language Countries">Community of Portuguese Language Countries</a>.
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Etymology">Etymology</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Etymology">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h2>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Anta_de_Arca.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Anta_de_Arca.JPG/220px-Anta_de_Arca.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Anta_de_Arca.JPG/330px-Anta_de_Arca.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Anta_de_Arca.JPG/440px-Anta_de_Arca.JPG 2x" data-file-width="3840" data-file-height="2880" /></a><figcaption>Chalcolithic Dolmen <i>Anta da Arca</i></figcaption></figure>
<p>The word <i>Portugal</i> derives from the combined <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Rome" title="Ancient Rome">Roman</a>-<a href="/wiki/Celtic_languages" title="Celtic languages">Celtic</a> place name <a href="/wiki/Portus_Cale" title="Portus Cale">Portus Cale</a>;<sup id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-26">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> a settlement where present-day's conurbation of <a href="/wiki/Porto" title="Porto">Porto</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vila_Nova_de_Gaia" title="Vila Nova de Gaia">Vila Nova de Gaia</a> (or simply, Gaia) stand, along the banks of <a href="/wiki/River_Douro" class="mw-redirect" title="River Douro">River Douro</a> in the north of what is now Portugal. The name of Porto stems from the Latin word for <a href="/wiki/Port" title="Port">port</a> or harbour, <span title="Latin-language text"><i lang="la">portus</i></span>, with the second element <i>Cale</i>’s meaning and precise origin being less clear. The mainstream explanation points to an <a href="/wiki/Ethnonym" title="Ethnonym">ethnonym</a> derived from the <a href="/wiki/Callaeci" class="mw-redirect" title="Callaeci">Callaeci</a> also known as Gallaeci peoples, who occupied the north-west of the Iberian Peninsula.<sup id="cite_ref-academia.edu_27-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-academia.edu-27">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup> The names <i>Cale</i> and <i>Callaici</i> are the origin of today's <i><a href="/wiki/Vila_Nova_de_Gaia" title="Vila Nova de Gaia">Gaia</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Galicia_(Spain)" title="Galicia (Spain)">Galicia</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-ReferenceA_28-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ReferenceA-28">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-auto3_29-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto3-29">&#91;26&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Another theory proposes that <i>Cale</i> or <i>Calle</i> is a derivation of the Celtic word for 'port', like the <a href="/wiki/Irish_language" title="Irish language">Irish</a> <span title="Irish-language text"><i lang="ga">caladh</i></span> or <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Gaelic" title="Scottish Gaelic">Scottish Gaelic</a> <span title="Scottish Gaelic-language text"><i lang="gd">cala</i></span>. These explanations, would require the pre-Roman language of the area to have been a branch of Q-Celtic, which is not generally accepted because the region's pre-Roman language was <a href="/wiki/Gallaecian" class="mw-redirect" title="Gallaecian">Gallaecian</a>. However, scholars like <a href="/wiki/Jean_Markale" title="Jean Markale">Jean Markale</a> and Tranoy propose that the Celtic branches all share the same origin, and placenames such as Cale, Gal, Gaia, <a href="/wiki/Calais" title="Calais">Calais</a>, Galatia, Galicia, <a href="/wiki/Gaelic_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Gaelic language">Gaelic</a>, Gael, <a href="/wiki/Gaul" title="Gaul">Gaul</a> (<a href="/wiki/Latin_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Latin language">Latin</a>: <i lang="la">Gallia</i>),<sup id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30">&#91;27&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Wales" title="Wales">Wales</a>, Cornwall, <a href="/wiki/Wallonia" title="Wallonia">Wallonia</a> and others all stem from one linguistic root.<sup id="cite_ref-ReferenceA_28-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ReferenceA-28">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31">&#91;28&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32">&#91;29&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>A further explanation proposes <i>Gatelo</i> as having been the origin of present-day <a href="/wiki/Braga" title="Braga">Braga</a>, <a href="/wiki/Santiago_de_Compostela" title="Santiago de Compostela">Santiago de Compostela</a>, and consequently the wider regions of Northern Portugal and Galicia.<sup id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup> A different theory has it that <i>Cala</i> was the name of a Celtic goddess (drawing a comparison with the <a href="/wiki/Gaelic_languages" class="mw-redirect" title="Gaelic languages">Gaelic</a> <i><a href="/wiki/Cailleach" title="Cailleach">Cailleach</a></i>, a supernatural hag). Further still, some French scholars believe the name may have come from <span title="Latin-language text"><i lang="la">Portus Gallus</i></span>,<sup id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34">&#91;31&#93;</a></sup> the port of the Gauls or Celts.
</p><p>Around 200 BC, the <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Rome" title="Ancient Rome">Romans</a> took the <a href="/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula" title="Iberian Peninsula">Iberian Peninsula</a> from the Carthaginians during the <a href="/wiki/Second_Punic_War" title="Second Punic War">Second Punic War</a>. In the process they conquered Cale, renaming it <span title="Latin-language text"><i lang="la">Portus Cale</i></span> ('Port of Cale') and incorporating it in the province of <a href="/wiki/Gaelicia" class="mw-redirect" title="Gaelicia">Gaellicia</a> with its capital in <a href="/wiki/Bracara_Augusta" class="mw-redirect" title="Bracara Augusta">Bracara Augusta</a> (modern day <a href="/wiki/Braga" title="Braga">Braga</a>, Portugal). During the <a href="/wiki/Middle_Ages" title="Middle Ages">Middle Ages</a>, the region around Portus Cale became known by the <a href="/wiki/Suebi" title="Suebi">Suebi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Visigoths" title="Visigoths">Visigoths</a> as <i>Portucale</i>. The name <i>Portucale</i> evolved into <i>Portugale</i> during the 7th and 8th centuries, and by the 9th century, that term was used extensively to refer to the region between the rivers <a href="/wiki/Douro" title="Douro">Douro</a> and <a href="/wiki/Minho_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Minho River">Minho</a>. By the 11th and 12th centuries, <i>Portugale</i>, <i>Portugallia</i>, <i>Portvgallo</i> or <i>Portvgalliae</i> was already referred to as <i>Portugal</i>.
</p><p>The 14th-century <a href="/wiki/Middle_French" title="Middle French">Middle French</a> name for the country, <span title="Middle French (ca. 1400-1600)-language text"><i lang="frm">Portingal</i></span>, which added an intrusive /n/ sound through the process of <a href="/wiki/Excrescence_(phonology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Excrescence (phonology)">excrescence</a>, spread to <a href="/wiki/Middle_English" title="Middle English">Middle English</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-OED_35-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OED-35">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup> Middle English variant spellings included <span title="Middle English (1100-1500)-language text"><i lang="enm">Portingall</i></span>, <span title="Middle English (1100-1500)-language text"><i lang="enm">Portingale</i></span>,<sup id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37">&#91;note 4&#93;</a></sup> <span title="Middle English (1100-1500)-language text"><i lang="enm">Portyngale</i></span> and <span title="Middle English (1100-1500)-language text"><i lang="enm">Portingaill</i></span>.<sup id="cite_ref-OED_35-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OED-35">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38">&#91;34&#93;</a></sup> The spelling <span title="Middle English (1100-1500)-language text"><i lang="enm">Portyngale</i></span> is found in Chaucer's Epilogue to <a href="/wiki/The_Nun%27s_Priest%27s_Tale" title="The Nun&#39;s Priest&#39;s Tale">the Nun's Priest's Tale</a>. These variants survive in the <i><a href="/wiki/Torrent_of_Portyngale" title="Torrent of Portyngale">Torrent of Portyngale</a></i>, a Middle English romance composed around 1400, and "<a href="/wiki/Old_Robin_of_Portingale" title="Old Robin of Portingale">Old Robin of Portingale</a>", an English Child ballad. <span title="Scots-language text"><i lang="sco">Portingal</i></span> and variants were also used in <a href="/wiki/Scots_language" title="Scots language">Scots</a><sup id="cite_ref-OED_35-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OED-35">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup> and survive in the <a href="/wiki/Cornish_language" title="Cornish language">Cornish</a> name for the country, <i><a href="https://kw.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portyngal" class="extiw" title="kw:Portyngal">Portyngal</a></i>.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="History">History</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: History">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/History_of_Portugal" title="History of Portugal">History of Portugal</a></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Prehistory">Prehistory</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Prehistory">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Prehistoric_Iberia" title="Prehistoric Iberia">Prehistoric Iberia</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Rock_Art_Foz_Coa_01.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Rock_Art_Foz_Coa_01.jpg/220px-Rock_Art_Foz_Coa_01.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Rock_Art_Foz_Coa_01.jpg/330px-Rock_Art_Foz_Coa_01.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Rock_Art_Foz_Coa_01.jpg/440px-Rock_Art_Foz_Coa_01.jpg 2x" data-file-width="909" data-file-height="682" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Prehistoric_Rock_Art_Sites_in_the_C%C3%B4a_Valley" title="Prehistoric Rock Art Sites in the Côa Valley">Prehistoric Rock Art Sites in the Côa Valley</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The early history of Portugal is shared with the rest of the <a href="/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula" title="Iberian Peninsula">Iberian Peninsula</a> located in south-western Europe. <a href="/wiki/The_name_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="The name of Portugal">The name of Portugal</a> derives from the joined Romano-Celtic name <a href="/wiki/Portus_Cale" title="Portus Cale">Portus Cale</a>. The region was <a href="/wiki/Pre-Roman_peoples_of_the_Iberian_Peninsula" class="mw-redirect" title="Pre-Roman peoples of the Iberian Peninsula">settled</a> by Pre-<a href="/wiki/Celts" title="Celts">Celts</a> and Celts, giving origin to peoples like the <a href="/wiki/Gallaeci" title="Gallaeci">Gallaeci</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lusitanians" title="Lusitanians">Lusitanians</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39">&#91;35&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Celtici" title="Celtici">Celtici</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cynetes" title="Cynetes">Cynetes</a> (also known as <a href="/wiki/Conii" class="mw-redirect" title="Conii">Conii</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40">&#91;36&#93;</a></sup> Some coastal areas were visited by <a href="/wiki/Phoenicians" class="mw-redirect" title="Phoenicians">Phoenicians</a>-<a href="/wiki/Carthaginians" class="mw-redirect" title="Carthaginians">Carthaginians</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Greek" title="Ancient Greek">Ancient Greeks</a>. It was incorporated in the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Republic" title="Roman Republic">Roman Republic</a> dominions as <a href="/wiki/Lusitania" title="Lusitania">Lusitania</a> and part of <a href="/wiki/Gallaecia" title="Gallaecia">Gallaecia</a>, after 45 BC until 298 AD.
</p><p>The region of present-day Portugal was inhabited by <a href="/wiki/Neanderthal" title="Neanderthal">Neanderthals</a> and then by <i><a href="/wiki/Homo_sapiens" class="mw-redirect" title="Homo sapiens">Homo sapiens</a></i>, who roamed the border-less region of the northern Iberian peninsula.<sup id="cite_ref-Birmp1_41-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Birmp1-41">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup> These were subsistence societies and although they did not establish prosperous settlements, they did form organized societies. Neolithic Portugal experimented with domestication of herding animals, the raising of some cereal crops and fluvial or marine fishing.<sup id="cite_ref-Birmp1_41-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Birmp1-41">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Centro_de_Alcalar_2017_-_Monumento_9_-_Entrada_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Centro_de_Alcalar_2017_-_Monumento_9_-_Entrada_%28cropped%29.jpg/220px-Centro_de_Alcalar_2017_-_Monumento_9_-_Entrada_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="161" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Centro_de_Alcalar_2017_-_Monumento_9_-_Entrada_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-Centro_de_Alcalar_2017_-_Monumento_9_-_Entrada_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Centro_de_Alcalar_2017_-_Monumento_9_-_Entrada_%28cropped%29.jpg/440px-Centro_de_Alcalar_2017_-_Monumento_9_-_Entrada_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1819" data-file-height="1334" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Megalithic_Monuments_of_Alcalar" title="Megalithic Monuments of Alcalar">Megalithic Monuments of Alcalar</a>, built in the 3rd millennium BCE</figcaption></figure>
<p>It is believed by some scholars that early in the first millennium BC, several waves of <a href="/wiki/Celts" title="Celts">Celts</a> invaded Portugal from Central Europe and inter-married with the local populations, forming <a href="/wiki/Pre-Roman_peoples_of_the_Iberian_Peninsula" class="mw-redirect" title="Pre-Roman peoples of the Iberian Peninsula">different tribes</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup> Another theory suggests that Celts inhabited western Iberia / Portugal well before any large Celtic migrations from <a href="/wiki/Central_Europe" title="Central Europe">Central Europe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43">&#91;39&#93;</a></sup> In addition, a number of linguists expert in ancient Celtic have presented compelling evidence that the <a href="/wiki/Tartessian_language" title="Tartessian language">Tartessian language</a>, once spoken in parts of SW Spain and SW Portugal, is at least proto-Celtic in structure.<sup id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modern archaeology and research shows a Portuguese root to the <a href="/wiki/Celts" title="Celts">Celts</a> in Portugal and elsewhere.<sup id="cite_ref-45" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-45">&#91;41&#93;</a></sup> During that period and until the Roman invasions, the Castro culture (a variation of the <a href="/wiki/Urnfield_culture" title="Urnfield culture">Urnfield culture</a> also known as <i>Urnenfelderkultur</i>) was prolific in Portugal and modern Galicia.<sup id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-46">&#91;42&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-47" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-47">&#91;43&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-auto3_29-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto3-29">&#91;26&#93;</a></sup> This culture, together with the surviving elements of the Atlantic megalithic culture<sup id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup> and the contributions that come from the more Western Mediterranean cultures, ended up in what has been called the Cultura Castreja or <a href="/wiki/Castro_Culture" class="mw-redirect" title="Castro Culture">Castro Culture</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-49">&#91;45&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-50" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-50">&#91;46&#93;</a></sup> This designation refers to the characteristic Celtic populations called 'dùn', 'dùin' or 'don' in <a href="/wiki/Goidelic_languages" title="Goidelic languages">Gaelic</a> and that the Romans called castrae in their chronicles.<sup id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51">&#91;47&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti">.mw-parser-output .tmulti .multiimageinner{display:flex;flex-direction:column}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .trow{display:flex;flex-direction:row;clear:left;flex-wrap:wrap;width:100%;box-sizing:border-box}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .tsingle{margin:1px;float:left}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .theader{clear:both;font-weight:bold;text-align:center;align-self:center;background-color:transparent;width:100%}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .thumbcaption{background-color:transparent}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .text-align-left{text-align:left}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .text-align-right{text-align:right}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .text-align-center{text-align:center}@media all and (max-width:720px){.mw-parser-output .tmulti .thumbinner{width:100%!important;box-sizing:border-box;max-width:none!important;align-items:center}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .trow{justify-content:center}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .tsingle{float:none!important;max-width:100%!important;box-sizing:border-box;text-align:center}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .tsingle .thumbcaption{text-align:left}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .trow>.thumbcaption{text-align:center}}</style><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:204px;max-width:204px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Citania_briteiros_casa_2.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Citania_briteiros_casa_2.jpg/200px-Citania_briteiros_casa_2.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="150" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Citania_briteiros_casa_2.jpg/300px-Citania_briteiros_casa_2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Citania_briteiros_casa_2.jpg/400px-Citania_briteiros_casa_2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="640" data-file-height="480" /></a></span></div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Ch%C3%A3o_cividade_terroso.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Ch%C3%A3o_cividade_terroso.JPG/200px-Ch%C3%A3o_cividade_terroso.JPG" decoding="async" width="200" height="150" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Ch%C3%A3o_cividade_terroso.JPG/300px-Ch%C3%A3o_cividade_terroso.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Ch%C3%A3o_cividade_terroso.JPG/400px-Ch%C3%A3o_cividade_terroso.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2000" data-file-height="1500" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption">Examples of <a href="/wiki/Castro_culture" title="Castro culture">Castro culture</a> in <a href="/wiki/Northern_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Northern Portugal">Northern Portugal</a> (9th – 1st c. BCE): <a href="/wiki/Cit%C3%A2nia_de_Briteiros" title="Citânia de Briteiros">Citânia de Briteiros</a> (top) and <a href="/wiki/Cividade_de_Terroso" title="Cividade de Terroso">Cividade de Terroso</a> (bottom)</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>Based on the Roman chronicles about the <a href="/wiki/Callaeci" class="mw-redirect" title="Callaeci">Callaeci</a> peoples, along with the <a href="/wiki/Lebor_Gab%C3%A1la_%C3%89renn" title="Lebor Gabála Érenn">Lebor Gabála Érenn</a><sup id="cite_ref-52" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-52">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup> narrations and the interpretation of the abundant archaeological remains throughout the northern half of Portugal and Galicia, it is possible to infer that there was a matriarchal society, with a military and religious aristocracy probably of the feudal type.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (July 2021)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> The figures of maximum authority were the chieftain (chefe tribal), of military type and with authority in his Castro or clan, and the druid, mainly referring to medical and religious functions that could be common to several castros. The Celtic cosmogony remained homogeneous due to the ability of the <a href="/wiki/Druids" class="mw-redirect" title="Druids">druids</a> to meet in councils with the druids of other areas, which ensured the transmission of knowledge and the most significant events.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (July 2021)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>The first documentary references to Castro society are provided by chroniclers of Roman military campaigns such as <a href="/wiki/Strabo" title="Strabo">Strabo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Herodotus" title="Herodotus">Herodotus</a> and <a href="/wiki/Pliny_the_Elder" title="Pliny the Elder">Pliny the Elder</a> among others, about the social organization, and describing the inhabitants of these territories, the <a href="/wiki/Gallaecia" title="Gallaecia">Gallaeci of Northern Portugal</a> as:
</p><p>"A group of barbarians who spend the day fighting and the night eating, drinking and dancing under the moon."
</p><p>There were other similar tribes, and chief among them were the <a href="/wiki/Lusitanians" title="Lusitanians">Lusitanians</a>; the core area of these people lay in inland central Portugal, while numerous other related tribes existed such as the <a href="/wiki/Celtici" title="Celtici">Celtici of Alentejo</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Cynetes" title="Cynetes">Cynetes or Conii of the Algarve</a>. Among the tribes or sub-divisions were the <a href="/wiki/Bracari" title="Bracari">Bracari</a>, <a href="/wiki/Coelerni" title="Coelerni">Coelerni</a>, <a href="/wiki/Equaesi" title="Equaesi">Equaesi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Grovii" title="Grovii">Grovii</a>, <a href="/wiki/Interamici" title="Interamici">Interamici</a>, <a href="/wiki/Leuni" title="Leuni">Leuni</a>, <a href="/wiki/Luanqui" title="Luanqui">Luanqui</a>, <a href="/wiki/Limici" title="Limici">Limici</a>, <a href="/wiki/Narbasi" title="Narbasi">Narbasi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nemetati" title="Nemetati">Nemetati</a>, <a href="/wiki/Paesuri" title="Paesuri">Paesuri</a>, <a href="/wiki/Quaquerni" title="Quaquerni">Quaquerni</a>, <a href="/wiki/Seurbi" title="Seurbi">Seurbi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tamagani" title="Tamagani">Tamagani</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tapoli" title="Tapoli">Tapoli</a>, <a href="/wiki/Turduli" title="Turduli">Turduli</a>, <a href="/wiki/Turduli_Veteres" title="Turduli Veteres">Turduli Veteres</a>, <a href="/wiki/Turduli_Oppidani" title="Turduli Oppidani">Turduli Oppidani</a>, <a href="/wiki/Turodi" title="Turodi">Turodi</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Zoelae" title="Zoelae">Zoelae</a>. A few small, semi-permanent, commercial coastal settlements (such as <a href="/wiki/Tavira_Municipality" class="mw-redirect" title="Tavira Municipality">Tavira</a>) were also founded in the <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a> region by <a href="/wiki/Phoenicians" class="mw-redirect" title="Phoenicians">Phoenicians</a>–<a href="/wiki/Carthaginians" class="mw-redirect" title="Carthaginians">Carthaginians</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Roman_Lusitania_and_Gallaecia">Roman Lusitania and Gallaecia</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Roman Lusitania and Gallaecia">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Lusitania" title="Lusitania">Lusitania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gallaecia" title="Gallaecia">Gallaecia</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Hispania" title="Hispania">Hispania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Evora-RomanTemple_edit.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Evora-RomanTemple_edit.jpg/220px-Evora-RomanTemple_edit.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="163" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Evora-RomanTemple_edit.jpg/330px-Evora-RomanTemple_edit.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Evora-RomanTemple_edit.jpg/440px-Evora-RomanTemple_edit.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3676" data-file-height="2729" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Roman_Temple_of_%C3%89vora" title="Roman Temple of Évora">Roman Temple of Évora</a>, in the <a href="/wiki/Alentejo" title="Alentejo">Alentejo</a>, is one of the best-preserved <a href="/wiki/Roman_civilization" class="mw-redirect" title="Roman civilization">Roman</a>-built structures in the country.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Romans first invaded the Iberian Peninsula in 219 BC. The Carthaginians, Rome's adversary in the <a href="/wiki/Punic_Wars" title="Punic Wars">Punic Wars</a>, were expelled from their coastal colonies. During the last days of <a href="/wiki/Julius_Caesar" title="Julius Caesar">Julius Caesar</a>, almost the entire peninsula was annexed to the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Republic" title="Roman Republic">Roman Republic</a>.
</p><p>The Roman conquest of what is now part of Portugal took almost two hundred years and took many lives of young soldiers and the lives of those who were sentenced to a certain death in the slave mines when not sold as slaves to other parts of the empire. Roman occupation suffered a severe setback in 155 BC, when a <a href="/wiki/Lusitanian_War" title="Lusitanian War">rebellion</a> began in the north. The <a href="/wiki/Lusitanians" title="Lusitanians">Lusitanians</a> and other native tribes, under the leadership of <a href="/wiki/Viriathus" title="Viriathus">Viriathus</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-53" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-53">&#91;49&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-54">&#91;50&#93;</a></sup> wrested control of all of western Iberia.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Torre_de_Centum_Cellas.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Torre_de_Centum_Cellas.jpg/170px-Torre_de_Centum_Cellas.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="227" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Torre_de_Centum_Cellas.jpg/255px-Torre_de_Centum_Cellas.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Torre_de_Centum_Cellas.jpg/340px-Torre_de_Centum_Cellas.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2736" data-file-height="3648" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Centum_Cellas" title="Centum Cellas">Centum Cellas</a>, in the <a href="/wiki/Beira_(Portugal)" title="Beira (Portugal)">Beira region</a>, is a Roman <i><a href="/wiki/Villa_rustica" title="Villa rustica">villa rustica</a></i> from the 1st century CE.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Rome sent numerous legions and its best generals to Lusitania to quell the rebellion, but to no avail – the Lusitanians kept conquering territory. The Roman leaders decided to change their strategy. They bribed Viriathus's allies to kill him. In 139 BC, <a href="/wiki/Viriathus" title="Viriathus">Viriathus</a> was assassinated and <a href="/wiki/Tautalus" title="Tautalus">Tautalus</a> became leader of the Lusitanians.
</p><p>Rome installed a colonial regime. The complete Romanization of Lusitania only took place in the <a href="/wiki/Visigothic" class="mw-redirect" title="Visigothic">Visigothic</a> era.
</p><p>In 27 BC, Lusitania gained the status of <a href="/wiki/Roman_province" title="Roman province">Roman province</a>. Later, a northern province of Lusitania was formed, known as <a href="/wiki/Gallaecia" title="Gallaecia">Gallaecia</a>, with capital in Bracara Augusta, today's <a href="/wiki/Braga" title="Braga">Braga</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55">&#91;51&#93;</a></sup>
There are still many ruins of castros (<a href="/wiki/Hill_forts" class="mw-redirect" title="Hill forts">hill forts</a>) throughout modern Portugal and remains of the <a href="/wiki/Castro_culture" title="Castro culture">Castro culture</a>.
Some urban remains are quite large, like <a href="/wiki/Con%C3%ADmbriga" title="Conímbriga">Conímbriga</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mir%C3%B3briga" title="Miróbriga">Mirobriga</a>. The former, beyond being one of the largest <a href="/wiki/Roman_Empire" title="Roman Empire">Roman</a> settlements in Portugal, is also classified as a <a href="/wiki/Monuments_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Monuments of Portugal">National Monument</a>. Conímbriga lies 16 kilometres (10 miles) from <a href="/wiki/Coimbra" title="Coimbra">Coimbra</a>, which in turn was the ancient <i><a href="/wiki/Aeminium" title="Aeminium">Aeminium</a></i>. The site also has a museum that displays objects found by archaeologists during their excavations.
</p><p>Several works of engineering, such as baths, temples, bridges, roads, circuses, theatres and laymen's homes are preserved throughout the country. Coins, some coined in Lusitanian land, as well as numerous pieces of ceramics, were also found. Contemporary historians include <a href="/wiki/Paulus_Orosius" class="mw-redirect" title="Paulus Orosius">Paulus Orosius</a> (c. 375–418)<sup id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-56">&#91;52&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Hydatius" title="Hydatius">Hydatius</a> (c. 400–469), bishop of <a href="/wiki/Aquae_Flaviae" title="Aquae Flaviae">Aquae Flaviae</a>, who reported on the final years of the Roman rule and arrival of the <a href="/wiki/Germanic_peoples" title="Germanic peoples">Germanic tribes</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Germanic_kingdoms:_Suebi_and_Visigoths">Germanic kingdoms: Suebi and Visigoths</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Germanic kingdoms: Suebi and Visigoths">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Reino_suevo.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Reino_suevo.svg/220px-Reino_suevo.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="253" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Reino_suevo.svg/330px-Reino_suevo.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Reino_suevo.svg/440px-Reino_suevo.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="475" data-file-height="546" /></a><figcaption>Map of the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_the_Suebi" title="Kingdom of the Suebi">Kingdom of the Suebi</a> in the 5th and 6th centuries</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Iberia_560.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Iberia_560.svg/220px-Iberia_560.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="181" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Iberia_560.svg/330px-Iberia_560.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Iberia_560.svg/440px-Iberia_560.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="924" data-file-height="762" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Visigothic_kingdom" class="mw-redirect" title="Visigothic kingdom">Visigothic kingdom</a> in Iberia <span title="circa">c.</span><span style="white-space:nowrap;">&#8201;560</span></figcaption></figure>
<p>In the early 5th century, <a href="/wiki/Germanic_peoples" title="Germanic peoples">Germanic tribes</a>, namely the <a href="/wiki/Suebi" title="Suebi">Suebi</a><sup id="cite_ref-auto4_57-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto4-57">&#91;53&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/Vandals" title="Vandals">Vandals</a> (<a href="/wiki/Silingi" title="Silingi">Silingi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Hasdingi" title="Hasdingi">Hasdingi</a>) together with their allies, the <a href="/wiki/Sarmatian" class="mw-redirect" title="Sarmatian">Sarmatians</a> and <a href="/wiki/Alans" title="Alans">Alans</a> invaded the <a href="/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula" title="Iberian Peninsula">Iberian Peninsula</a> where they would form their kingdom. The <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_the_Suebi" title="Kingdom of the Suebi">Kingdom of the Suebi</a><sup id="cite_ref-auto5_58-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto5-58">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup> was the Germanic post-Roman kingdom, established in the former Roman provinces of <a href="/wiki/Gallaecia" title="Gallaecia">Gallaecia</a>-<a href="/wiki/Lusitania" title="Lusitania">Lusitania</a>. 5th-century vestiges of <a href="/wiki/Alans" title="Alans">Alan</a> settlements were found in <a href="/wiki/Alenquer_Municipality,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Alenquer Municipality, Portugal">Alenquer</a> (from old Germanic <i>Alan kerk</i>, <i>temple of the Alans</i>), <a href="/wiki/Coimbra" title="Coimbra">Coimbra</a> and Lisbon.<sup id="cite_ref-59" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-59">&#91;55&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>About 410 and during the 6th century it became a formally declared <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_the_Suebi" title="Kingdom of the Suebi">Kingdom of the Suebi</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-auto5_58-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto5-58">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-auto4_57-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto4-57">&#91;53&#93;</a></sup> where king <a href="/wiki/Hermeric" title="Hermeric">Hermeric</a> made a peace treaty with the Gallaecians before passing his domains to <a href="/wiki/Rechila" title="Rechila">Rechila</a>, his son. In 448 Rechila died, leaving the state in expansion to <a href="/wiki/Rechiar" title="Rechiar">Rechiar</a>.
After the defeat against the Visigoths, the Suebian kingdom was divided, with Frantan and Aguiulfo ruling simultaneously. Both reigned from 456 to 457, the year in which Maldras (457–459) reunified the kingdom. He was assassinated after a failed Roman-Visigothic conspiracy.
Although the conspiracy did not achieve its true purposes, the Suebian Kingdom was again divided between two kings:
<a href="/wiki/Frumar" title="Frumar">Frumar</a> (Frumario 459–463) and <a href="/wiki/Remismund" title="Remismund">Remismund</a> (Remismundo, son of <a href="/wiki/Maldras" title="Maldras">Maldras</a>) (459–469) who would re-reunify his father's kingdom in 463. He would be forced to adopt <a href="/wiki/Arianism" title="Arianism">Arianism</a> in 465 due to the Visigoth influence.
By 500, the <a href="/wiki/Visigothic_Kingdom" title="Visigothic Kingdom">Visigothic Kingdom</a> had been installed in Iberia, it was based in <a href="/wiki/Toledo,_Spain" title="Toledo, Spain">Toledo</a> and advancing westwards. They became a threat to the Suebian rule.
After the death of Remismund in 469 a dark period set in, where virtually all written texts and accounts disappear. This period lasted until 550. The only thing known about this period is that <a href="/wiki/Theodemund" title="Theodemund">Theodemund</a> (Teodemundo) most probably ruled the Suebians.
The dark period ended with the reign of Karriarico (550–559) who reinstalled <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church" title="Catholic Church">Catholic Christianity</a> in 550. He was succeeded by <a href="/wiki/Theodemir_(Suebian_king)" title="Theodemir (Suebian king)">Theodemar</a> (559–570) during whose reign the 1st Council of Braga (561) was held.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ariamirogaliza.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Ariamirogaliza.jpg/220px-Ariamirogaliza.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="176" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Ariamirogaliza.jpg/330px-Ariamirogaliza.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/66/Ariamirogaliza.jpg 2x" data-file-width="394" data-file-height="316" /></a><figcaption>Illustrated depiction of the <a href="/wiki/First_Council_of_Braga" title="First Council of Braga">First Council of Braga</a> of 561 CE</figcaption></figure>
<p>The councils represented an advance in the organization of the territory (paroeciam suevorum (Suebian parish) and the <a href="/wiki/Christianization" title="Christianization">Christianization</a> of the pagan population (<i><a href="/wiki/De_correctione_rusticorum" title="De correctione rusticorum">De correctione rusticorum</a></i>) under the auspices of <a href="/wiki/Saint_Martin_of_Braga" class="mw-redirect" title="Saint Martin of Braga">Saint Martin of Braga</a> (São Martinho de Braga).<sup id="cite_ref-books.google.co.uk_60-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-books.google.co.uk-60">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>After the death of Teodomiro, <a href="/wiki/Miro_(Suebian_king)" title="Miro (Suebian king)">Miro</a> (570–583) was his successor. During his reign, the 2nd Council of Braga (572) was held.
The Visigothic civil war began in 577. Miro intervened. Later in 583 he also organized an unsuccessful expedition to reconquer Seville. During the return from this failed operation Miro died.
</p><p>In the Suebian Kingdom many internal struggles continued to take place. <a href="/wiki/Eborico" class="mw-redirect" title="Eborico">Eborico</a> (Eurico, 583–584) was dethroned by <a href="/wiki/Andeca" class="mw-redirect" title="Andeca">Andeca</a> (Audeca 584–585), who failed to prevent the Visigothic invasion led by <a href="/wiki/Liuvigild" title="Liuvigild">Leovigildo</a>. The Visigothic invasion, completed in 585, turned the once rich and fertile kingdom of the Suebi into the sixth province of the Gothic kingdom.<sup id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-61">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup>
<a href="/wiki/Leovigild" class="mw-redirect" title="Leovigild">Leovigild</a> was crowned King of Gallaecia, Hispania and <a href="/wiki/Gallia_Narbonensis" title="Gallia Narbonensis">Gallia Narbonensis</a>.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cvp-00791-109v.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Cvp-00791-109v.jpg/170px-Cvp-00791-109v.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="223" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Cvp-00791-109v.jpg/255px-Cvp-00791-109v.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Cvp-00791-109v.jpg/340px-Cvp-00791-109v.jpg 2x" data-file-width="390" data-file-height="512" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_the_Suebi" title="Kingdom of the Suebi">Suebi King</a> <a href="/wiki/Miro_(Suebian_king)" title="Miro (Suebian king)">Miro</a> and St. <a href="/wiki/Martin_of_Braga" title="Martin of Braga">Martin of Braga</a>; <span title="circa">c.</span><span style="white-space:nowrap;">&#8201;1145</span></figcaption></figure>
<p>For the next 300 years and by the year 700, the entire Iberian Peninsula was ruled by the <a href="/wiki/Visigoths" title="Visigoths">Visigoths</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-62">&#91;58&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-63">&#91;59&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-64">&#91;60&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-65">&#91;61&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-66" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-66">&#91;62&#93;</a></sup> Under the Visigoths, Gallaecia was a well-defined space governed by a doge of its own. Doges at this time were related to the monarchy and acted as princes in all matters. Both 'governors' <a href="/wiki/Wamba_(king)" title="Wamba (king)">Wamba</a> and <a href="/wiki/Wittiza" title="Wittiza">Wittiza</a> (Vitiza) acted as doge (they would later become kings in Toledo). These two became known as the 'vitizians', who headquartered in the northwest and called on the Arab invaders from the South to be their allies in the struggle for power in 711. King <a href="/wiki/Roderic" title="Roderic">Roderic</a> (Rodrigo) was killed while opposing this invasion, thus becoming the last Visigothic king of Iberia. From the various Germanic groups who settled in western Iberia, the <a href="/wiki/Suebi" title="Suebi">Suebi</a> left the strongest lasting cultural legacy in what is today Portugal, Galicia and western fringes of Asturias.<sup id="cite_ref-67" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-67">&#91;63&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68">&#91;64&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-69" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-69">&#91;65&#93;</a></sup>
According to Dan Stanislawski, the Portuguese way of living in regions North of the Tagus is mostly inherited from the Suebi, in which small farms prevail, distinct from the large properties of Southern Portugal.
Bracara Augusta, the modern city of <a href="/wiki/Braga" title="Braga">Braga</a> and former capital of <a href="/wiki/Gallaecia" title="Gallaecia">Gallaecia</a>, became the capital of the Suebi.<sup id="cite_ref-books.google.co.uk_60-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-books.google.co.uk-60">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup> Apart from cultural and some linguistic traces, the Suebians left the highest Germanic genetic contribution of the Iberian Peninsula in Portugal and Galicia.<sup id="cite_ref-70" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-70">&#91;66&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Self-published_sources" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability"><span title="The material near this tag may rely on a self-published source. (November 2020)">self-published source?</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> <a href="/wiki/Paulus_Orosius" class="mw-redirect" title="Paulus Orosius">Orosius</a>, at that time resident in Hispania, shows a rather pacific initial settlement, the newcomers working their lands<sup id="cite_ref-71" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-71">&#91;67&#93;</a></sup> or serving as bodyguards of the locals.<sup id="cite_ref-72" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-72">&#91;68&#93;</a></sup>
Another Germanic group that accompanied the Suebi and settled in Gallaecia were the <a href="/wiki/Buri_(Germanic_tribe)" class="mw-redirect" title="Buri (Germanic tribe)">Buri</a>. They settled in the region between the rivers <i><a href="/wiki/C%C3%A1vado_River" title="Cávado River">Cávado</a></i> and <i>Homem</i>, in the area known as <a href="/wiki/Terras_de_Bouro" title="Terras de Bouro">Terras de Bouro</a> (Lands of the Buri).<sup id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-73">&#91;69&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Islamic_period_and_the_Reconquista">Islamic period and the Reconquista</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Islamic period and the Reconquista">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Al_Andalus_-_2.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Al_Andalus_-_2.png/260px-Al_Andalus_-_2.png" decoding="async" width="260" height="193" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Al_Andalus_-_2.png/390px-Al_Andalus_-_2.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Al_Andalus_-_2.png/520px-Al_Andalus_-_2.png 2x" data-file-width="670" data-file-height="497" /></a><figcaption>The Caliphate of Cordoba in the early 10th century</figcaption></figure>
<p>Today's continental Portugal, along with most of modern Spain, was part of <a href="/wiki/Al-Andalus" title="Al-Andalus">al-Andalus</a> between 726 and 1249, following the <a href="/wiki/Umayyad_Caliphate" title="Umayyad Caliphate">Umayyad Caliphate</a> conquest of the <a href="/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula" title="Iberian Peninsula">Iberian Peninsula</a>. This rule lasted from some decades in the North to five centuries in the South.<sup id="cite_ref-Britannica_74-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Britannica-74">&#91;70&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>After defeating the <a href="/wiki/Visigoths" title="Visigoths">Visigoths</a> in only a few months, the Umayyad Caliphate started expanding rapidly in the peninsula. Beginning in 726, the land that is now Portugal became part of the vast Umayyad Caliphate's empire of <a href="/wiki/Damascus" title="Damascus">Damascus</a>, which stretched from the <a href="/wiki/Indus" class="mw-redirect" title="Indus">Indus</a> river in the Indian sub-continent up to the South of France, until its collapse in 750. That year the west of the empire gained its independence under <a href="/wiki/Abd-ar-Rahman_I" class="mw-redirect" title="Abd-ar-Rahman I">Abd-ar-Rahman I</a> with the establishment of the <a href="/wiki/Emirate_of_C%C3%B3rdoba" title="Emirate of Córdoba">Emirate of Córdoba</a>. After almost two centuries, the Emirate became the <a href="/wiki/Caliphate_of_C%C3%B3rdoba" title="Caliphate of Córdoba">Caliphate of Córdoba</a> in 929, until its dissolution a century later in 1031 into no less than 23 small kingdoms, called <a href="/wiki/Taifa" title="Taifa">Taifa</a> kingdoms.<sup id="cite_ref-Britannica_74-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Britannica-74">&#91;70&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Portugal_DSC04496_-_MERTOLA_(34025572830).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Portugal_DSC04496_-_MERTOLA_%2834025572830%29.jpg/220px-Portugal_DSC04496_-_MERTOLA_%2834025572830%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Portugal_DSC04496_-_MERTOLA_%2834025572830%29.jpg/330px-Portugal_DSC04496_-_MERTOLA_%2834025572830%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Portugal_DSC04496_-_MERTOLA_%2834025572830%29.jpg/440px-Portugal_DSC04496_-_MERTOLA_%2834025572830%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2000" data-file-height="1333" /></a><figcaption>Statue of <a href="/wiki/Abu-l-Qasim_Ahmad_ibn_al-Husayn_ibn_Qasi" title="Abu-l-Qasim Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Qasi">Ibn Qasi</a> outside the <a href="/wiki/Castle_of_M%C3%A9rtola" class="mw-redirect" title="Castle of Mértola">Castle of Mértola</a>, in the <a href="/wiki/Alentejo" title="Alentejo">Alentejo</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The governors of the taifas each proclaimed themselves <a href="/wiki/Emir" title="Emir">Emir</a> of their provinces and established diplomatic relations with the Christian kingdoms of the north. Most of present-day Portugal fell into the hands of the <a href="/wiki/Taifa_of_Badajoz" title="Taifa of Badajoz">Taifa of Badajoz</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Aftasid_Dynasty" class="mw-redirect" title="Aftasid Dynasty">Aftasid Dynasty</a>, and after a short spell of an ephemeral <a href="/wiki/Taifa_of_Lisbon" title="Taifa of Lisbon">Taifa of Lisbon</a> in 1022, fell under the dominion of the <a href="/wiki/Taifa_of_Seville" title="Taifa of Seville">Taifa of Seville</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Abbadids" class="mw-redirect" title="Abbadids">Abbadids</a> poets. The Taifa period ended with the conquest of the <a href="/wiki/Almoravids" class="mw-redirect" title="Almoravids">Almoravids</a> who came from <a href="/wiki/Morocco" title="Morocco">Morocco</a> in 1086 winning a decisive victory at the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Sagrajas" title="Battle of Sagrajas">Battle of Sagrajas</a>, followed a century later in 1147, after the second period of Taifa, by the <a href="/wiki/Almohads" class="mw-redirect" title="Almohads">Almohads</a>, also from <a href="/wiki/Marrakesh" title="Marrakesh">Marrakesh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-75" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-75">&#91;71&#93;</a></sup>
Al-Andaluz was divided into different districts called <i>Kura</i>. <a href="/wiki/Gharb_Al-Andalus" class="mw-redirect" title="Gharb Al-Andalus">Gharb Al-Andalus</a> at its largest consisted of ten kuras,<sup id="cite_ref-A._R._Disney,_p.55_76-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-A._R._Disney,_p.55-76">&#91;72&#93;</a></sup> each with a distinct capital and governor. The main cities of the period in Portugal were in the southern half of the country: <a href="/wiki/Beja_(Portugal)" class="mw-redirect" title="Beja (Portugal)">Beja</a>, <a href="/wiki/Silves_Municipality,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Silves Municipality, Portugal">Silves</a>, <a href="/wiki/Alc%C3%A1cer_do_Sal" title="Alcácer do Sal">Alcácer do Sal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Santar%C3%A9m,_Portugal" title="Santarém, Portugal">Santarém</a> and <a href="/wiki/Lisbon" title="Lisbon">Lisbon</a>.
The Muslim population of the region consisted mainly of native Iberian converts to <a href="/wiki/Islam" title="Islam">Islam</a> (the so-called <i><a href="/wiki/Muwallad" class="mw-redirect" title="Muwallad">Muwallad</a></i> or <i>Muladi</i>) and <a href="/wiki/Arabs" title="Arabs">Arabs</a>. The Arabs were principally noblemen from <a href="/wiki/Syria" title="Syria">Syria</a> and <a href="/wiki/Yemen" title="Yemen">Yemen</a>; and though few in numbers, they constituted the elite of the population. The <a href="/wiki/Berbers" title="Berbers">Berbers</a> were originally from the <a href="/wiki/Rif" title="Rif">Rif</a> and <a href="/wiki/Atlas_mountains" class="mw-redirect" title="Atlas mountains">Atlas mountains</a> region of North Africa and were nomads.<sup id="cite_ref-Britannica_74-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Britannica-74">&#91;70&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="County_of_Portugal">County of Portugal</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=7" title="Edit section: County of Portugal">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/County_of_Portugal" title="County of Portugal">County of Portugal</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Porto_April_2019-18.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Porto_April_2019-18.jpg/180px-Porto_April_2019-18.jpg" decoding="async" width="180" height="288" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Porto_April_2019-18.jpg/270px-Porto_April_2019-18.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Porto_April_2019-18.jpg/360px-Porto_April_2019-18.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4342" data-file-height="6951" /></a><figcaption>A statue of Count <a href="/wiki/V%C3%ADmara_Peres" title="Vímara Peres">Vímara Peres</a>, first <a href="/wiki/County_of_Portugal" title="County of Portugal">Count of Portugal</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>An Asturian Visigothic noble named <a href="/wiki/Pelagius_of_Asturias" title="Pelagius of Asturias">Pelagius of Asturias</a> in 718 was elected leader<sup id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77">&#91;73&#93;</a></sup> by many of the ousted <a href="/wiki/Visigoth" class="mw-redirect" title="Visigoth">Visigoth</a> nobles. Pelagius called for the remnant of the Christian Visigothic armies to rebel against the Moors and regroup in the unconquered northern Asturian highlands, better known today as the <a href="/wiki/Cantabrian_Mountains" title="Cantabrian Mountains">Cantabrian Mountains</a>, in what is today the small mountain region in north-western Spain, adjacent to the <a href="/wiki/Bay_of_Biscay" title="Bay of Biscay">Bay of Biscay</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-V._Livermore,_1969_pp._32-33_78-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-V._Livermore,_1969_pp._32-33-78">&#91;74&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Pelagius' plan was to use the Cantabrian mountains as a place of refuge and protection from the invading Moors. He then aimed to regroup the Iberian Peninsula's Christian armies and use the Cantabrian mountains as a springboard from which to regain their lands. In the process, after defeating the Moors in the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Covadonga" title="Battle of Covadonga">Battle of Covadonga</a> in 722, Pelagius was proclaimed king, thus founding the Christian <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Asturias" title="Kingdom of Asturias">Kingdom of Asturias</a> and starting the war of Christian reconquest known in <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_language" title="Portuguese language">Portuguese</a> as the <i><a href="/wiki/Reconquista" title="Reconquista">Reconquista Cristã</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-V._Livermore,_1969_pp._32-33_78-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-V._Livermore,_1969_pp._32-33-78">&#91;74&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>At the end of the 9th century, the region of Portugal, between the rivers Minho and Douro, was reconquered from the Moors by the nobleman and knight <a href="/wiki/V%C3%ADmara_Peres" title="Vímara Peres">Vímara Peres</a> on the orders of King <a href="/wiki/Alfonso_III_of_Asturias" title="Alfonso III of Asturias">Alfonso III of Asturias</a>. Finding that the region had previously had two major cities – <a href="/wiki/Portus_Cale" title="Portus Cale">Portus Cale</a> in the coast and <a href="/wiki/Braga" title="Braga">Braga</a> in the interior, with many towns that were now deserted – he decided to repopulate and rebuild them with Portuguese and Galician refugees and other Christians.<sup id="cite_ref-QuidNovi_79-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-QuidNovi-79">&#91;75&#93;</a></sup>
Apart from the Arabs from the South, the coastal regions in the North were also attacked by <a href="/wiki/Normans" title="Normans">Norman</a> and <a href="/wiki/Viking" class="mw-redirect" title="Viking">Viking</a><sup id="cite_ref-80" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80">&#91;76&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup> raiders mainly from 844. The last great invasion, through the <a href="/wiki/Minho_(river)" title="Minho (river)">Minho (river)</a>, ended with the defeat of <a href="/wiki/Olaf_II_Haraldsson" class="mw-redirect" title="Olaf II Haraldsson">Olaf II Haraldsson</a> in 1014 against the Galician nobility who also stopped further advances into the County of Portugal.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Henri_de_Bourgogne_re%C3%A7oit_l%27investiture_du_comt%C3%A9_de_Portugal,_1094_(Claude_Jacquand,_dit_Claudius;_1841).png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Henri_de_Bourgogne_re%C3%A7oit_l%27investiture_du_comt%C3%A9_de_Portugal%2C_1094_%28Claude_Jacquand%2C_dit_Claudius%3B_1841%29.png/220px-Henri_de_Bourgogne_re%C3%A7oit_l%27investiture_du_comt%C3%A9_de_Portugal%2C_1094_%28Claude_Jacquand%2C_dit_Claudius%3B_1841%29.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="202" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Henri_de_Bourgogne_re%C3%A7oit_l%27investiture_du_comt%C3%A9_de_Portugal%2C_1094_%28Claude_Jacquand%2C_dit_Claudius%3B_1841%29.png/330px-Henri_de_Bourgogne_re%C3%A7oit_l%27investiture_du_comt%C3%A9_de_Portugal%2C_1094_%28Claude_Jacquand%2C_dit_Claudius%3B_1841%29.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Henri_de_Bourgogne_re%C3%A7oit_l%27investiture_du_comt%C3%A9_de_Portugal%2C_1094_%28Claude_Jacquand%2C_dit_Claudius%3B_1841%29.png/440px-Henri_de_Bourgogne_re%C3%A7oit_l%27investiture_du_comt%C3%A9_de_Portugal%2C_1094_%28Claude_Jacquand%2C_dit_Claudius%3B_1841%29.png 2x" data-file-width="1234" data-file-height="1135" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Alfonso_VI_of_Le%C3%B3n" class="mw-redirect" title="Alfonso VI of León">Alfonso VI of León</a> investing <a href="/wiki/Henry,_Count_of_Portugal" title="Henry, Count of Portugal">Henry, Count of Portugal</a>, in 1093</figcaption></figure>
<p>Count Vímara Peres<sup id="cite_ref-82" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-82">&#91;78&#93;</a></sup> organized the region he had reconquered, and elevated it to the status of <a href="/wiki/County" title="County">County</a>, naming it the <a href="/wiki/County_of_Portugal" title="County of Portugal">County of Portugal</a> after the region's major port city – <i>Portus Cale</i> or modern <a href="/wiki/Porto" title="Porto">Porto</a>. One of the first cities Vimara Peres founded at this time is Vimaranes, known today as <a href="/wiki/Guimar%C3%A3es" title="Guimarães">Guimarães</a> – the "birthplace of the Portuguese nation" or the "cradle city" (Cidade Berço in Portuguese).<sup id="cite_ref-QuidNovi_79-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-QuidNovi-79">&#91;75&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>After annexing the County of Portugal into one of the several counties that made up the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Asturias" title="Kingdom of Asturias">Kingdom of Asturias</a>, King <a href="/wiki/Alfonso_III_of_Asturias" title="Alfonso III of Asturias">Alfonso III of Asturias</a> knighted Vímara Peres, in 868, as the First Count of Portus Cale (Portugal). The region became known as <i>Portucale</i>, <i>Portugale</i>, and simultaneously <i>Portugália</i> – the <a href="/wiki/County_of_Portugal" title="County of Portugal">County of Portugal</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-QuidNovi_79-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-QuidNovi-79">&#91;75&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Later the Kingdom of Asturias was divided into a number of Christian Kingdoms in Northern Iberia due to dynastic divisions of inheritance among the king's offspring. With the forced abdication of <a href="/wiki/Alfonso_III_of_Asturias" title="Alfonso III of Asturias">Alfonso III "the Great" of Asturias</a> by his sons in 910, the Kingdom of Asturias split into three separate kingdoms. The three kingdoms were eventually reunited in 924 under the crown of <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Le%C3%B3n" title="Kingdom of León">León</a>.
</p><p>In 1093, <a href="/wiki/Alfonso_VI_of_Le%C3%B3n" class="mw-redirect" title="Alfonso VI of León">Alfonso VI of León</a> bestowed the county to <a href="/wiki/Henry,_Count_of_Portugal" title="Henry, Count of Portugal">Henry of Burgundy</a> and married him to his illegitimate daughter, <a href="/wiki/Teresa_of_Le%C3%B3n,_Countess_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Teresa of León, Countess of Portugal">Teresa of León</a>, for his role in reconquering the land from Moors. Henry based his newly formed county in Bracara Augusta (modern <a href="/wiki/Braga" title="Braga">Braga</a>), capital city of the ancient Roman province, and also previous capital of several kingdoms over the first millennia.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Independence_and_Afonsine_era">Independence and Afonsine era</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=8" title="Edit section: Independence and Afonsine era">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Portugal_in_the_Middle_Ages" title="Portugal in the Middle Ages">Portugal in the Middle Ages</a> and <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_House_of_Burgundy" title="Portuguese House of Burgundy">Portuguese House of Burgundy</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tleft"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:204px;max-width:204px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:BatalhaOurique.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/BatalhaOurique.jpg/200px-BatalhaOurique.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="118" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/BatalhaOurique.jpg/300px-BatalhaOurique.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/BatalhaOurique.jpg/400px-BatalhaOurique.jpg 2x" data-file-width="460" data-file-height="271" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption">The <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Ourique" title="Battle of Ourique">Battle of Ourique</a>, 1139</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Siege_of_Lisbon_by_Roque_Gameiro.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Siege_of_Lisbon_by_Roque_Gameiro.jpg/200px-Siege_of_Lisbon_by_Roque_Gameiro.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="131" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Siege_of_Lisbon_by_Roque_Gameiro.jpg/300px-Siege_of_Lisbon_by_Roque_Gameiro.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Siege_of_Lisbon_by_Roque_Gameiro.jpg/400px-Siege_of_Lisbon_by_Roque_Gameiro.jpg 2x" data-file-width="972" data-file-height="639" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption">The <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Lisbon" title="Siege of Lisbon">siege of Lisbon</a>, 1147</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>On 24 June 1128, the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_S%C3%A3o_Mamede" title="Battle of São Mamede">Battle of São Mamede</a> occurred near <a href="/wiki/Guimar%C3%A3es" title="Guimarães">Guimarães</a>. <a href="/wiki/Afonso_I_of_Portugal" title="Afonso I of Portugal">Afonso Henriques</a>, Count of Portugal, defeated his mother <a href="/wiki/Teresa,_Countess_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Teresa, Countess of Portugal">Countess Teresa</a> and her lover <a href="/wiki/Fern%C3%A3o_Peres_de_Trava" class="mw-redirect" title="Fernão Peres de Trava">Fernão Peres de Trava</a>, thereby establishing himself as sole leader. Afonso then turned his arms against the Moors in the south.
</p><p>Afonso's campaigns were successful and, on 25 July 1139, he obtained an overwhelming victory in the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Ourique" title="Battle of Ourique">Battle of Ourique</a>, and straight after was unanimously proclaimed <a href="/wiki/King_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="King of Portugal">King of Portugal</a> by his soldiers. This is traditionally taken as the occasion when the County of Portugal, as a fief of the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Le%C3%B3n" title="Kingdom of León">Kingdom of León</a>, was transformed into the independent <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Portugal" title="Kingdom of Portugal">Kingdom of Portugal</a>.
</p><p>Afonso then established the first of the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Cortes" title="Portuguese Cortes">Portuguese Cortes</a> at <a href="/wiki/Lamego" title="Lamego">Lamego</a>, where he was crowned by the Archbishop of Braga, though the validity of the Cortes of Lamego has been disputed and called a myth created during the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Restoration_War" title="Portuguese Restoration War">Portuguese Restoration War</a>. Afonso was recognized in 1143 by King <a href="/wiki/Alfonso_VII_of_Le%C3%B3n" class="mw-redirect" title="Alfonso VII of León">Alfonso VII of León</a>, and in 1179 by <a href="/wiki/Pope_Alexander_III" title="Pope Alexander III">Pope Alexander III</a>.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Afonso_I_Henriques_de_Portugal.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Afonso_I_Henriques_de_Portugal.jpg/170px-Afonso_I_Henriques_de_Portugal.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="310" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Afonso_I_Henriques_de_Portugal.jpg/255px-Afonso_I_Henriques_de_Portugal.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/ca/Afonso_I_Henriques_de_Portugal.jpg 2x" data-file-width="328" data-file-height="598" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Afonso_Henriques" class="mw-redirect" title="Afonso Henriques">Afonso Henriques</a> was the last <a href="/wiki/Count_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Count of Portugal">Count of Portugal</a> and the first <a href="/wiki/List_of_Portuguese_monarchs" title="List of Portuguese monarchs">King of Portugal</a> after winning the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Ourique" title="Battle of Ourique">Battle of Ourique</a> in 1139.</figcaption></figure>
<p>During the <a href="/wiki/Reconquista" title="Reconquista">Reconquista</a> period, Christians reconquered the Iberian Peninsula from <a href="/wiki/Moors" title="Moors">Moorish</a> domination. Afonso Henriques and his successors, aided by military <a href="/wiki/Christian_monasticism" title="Christian monasticism">monastic orders</a>, pushed southward to drive out the Moors. At this time, Portugal covered about half of its present area. In 1249, the Reconquista ended with the capture of the <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a> and complete expulsion of the last Moorish settlements on the southern coast, giving Portugal its present-day borders, with minor exceptions.
</p><p>In one of these situations of conflict with the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Castile" title="Kingdom of Castile">kingdom of Castile</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dinis_I_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Dinis I of Portugal">Dinis I of Portugal</a> signed with the king <a href="/wiki/Fernando_IV_of_Castile" class="mw-redirect" title="Fernando IV of Castile">Fernando IV of Castile</a> (who was represented, when a minor, by his mother the queen <a href="/wiki/Maria_de_Molina" class="mw-redirect" title="Maria de Molina">Maria de Molina</a>) the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Alca%C3%B1ices_(1297)" class="mw-redirect" title="Treaty of Alcañices (1297)">Treaty of Alcañices (1297)</a>, which stipulated that Portugal abolished agreed treaties against the kingdom of Castile for supporting the infant <a href="/wiki/Juan_de_Castilla" title="Juan de Castilla">Juan de Castilla</a>. This treaty established among other things the border demarcation between the kingdom of Portugal and the kingdom of Leon, where the disputed town of <a href="/wiki/Olivenza" title="Olivenza">Olivenza</a> was included.
</p><p>The reigns of <a href="/wiki/Denis_I_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Denis I of Portugal">Dinis I</a> (Denis I), <a href="/wiki/Afonso_IV_of_Portugal" title="Afonso IV of Portugal">Afonso IV</a> (Alphons IV), and <a href="/wiki/Peter_I_of_Portugal" title="Peter I of Portugal">Pedro I</a> (Peter I) for the most part saw peace with the Christian kingdoms of Iberia.
</p><p>In 1348 and 1349 Portugal, like the rest of Europe, was devastated by the <a href="/wiki/Black_Death" title="Black Death">Black Death</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup> In 1373, Portugal made an <a href="/wiki/Anglo-Portuguese_Alliance" title="Anglo-Portuguese Alliance">alliance with England</a>, which is one of the oldest standing alliances in the world. Over time, this went far beyond geo-political and military cooperation (protecting both nations' interests in Africa, the Americas and Asia against French, Spanish and Dutch rivals) and maintained strong trade and cultural ties between the two old European allies. In the <a href="/wiki/Oporto" class="mw-redirect" title="Oporto">Oporto</a> region, in particular, there is visible English influence to this day.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Joanine_era_and_Age_of_Discoveries">Joanine era and Age of Discoveries</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=9" title="Edit section: Joanine era and Age of Discoveries">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
