<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_(081).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%28081%29.jpg/220px-Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%28081%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="131" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%28081%29.jpg/330px-Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%28081%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%28081%29.jpg/440px-Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%28081%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="521" data-file-height="310" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon" title="Treaty of Lisbon">Treaty of Lisbon</a> was signed in 2007, when Portugal held the presidency for the <a href="/wiki/European_Council" title="European Council">European Council</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>On 26 March 1995, Portugal started to implement <a href="/wiki/Schengen_Area" title="Schengen Area">Schengen Area</a> rules, eliminating border controls with other Schengen members while simultaneously strengthening border controls with non-member states. In 1996 the country was a co-founder of the <a href="/wiki/Community_of_Portuguese_Language_Countries" title="Community of Portuguese Language Countries">Community of Portuguese Language Countries</a> (CPLP) headquartered in Lisbon. In 1996, <a href="/wiki/Jorge_Sampaio" title="Jorge Sampaio">Jorge Sampaio</a> became president. He won <a href="/wiki/2001_Portuguese_presidential_election" title="2001 Portuguese presidential election">re-election</a> in January 2001. <a href="/wiki/Expo_%2798" title="Expo &#39;98">Expo '98</a> took place in Portugal and in 1999 it was one of the founding countries of the <a href="/wiki/Euro" title="Euro">euro</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Eurozone" title="Eurozone">eurozone</a>. On 5 July 2004, <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Manuel_Barroso" title="José Manuel Barroso">José Manuel Barroso</a>, then <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Portugal" title="Prime Minister of Portugal">Prime Minister of Portugal</a>, was nominated <a href="/wiki/President_of_the_European_Commission" title="President of the European Commission">President of the European Commission</a>, the most powerful office in the European Union. On 1 December 2009, the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon" title="Treaty of Lisbon">Treaty of Lisbon</a> entered into force, after it had been signed by the European Union member states on 13 December 2007 in the <a href="/wiki/Jer%C3%B3nimos_Monastery" title="Jerónimos Monastery">Jerónimos Monastery</a>, in Lisbon, enhancing the efficiency and democratic legitimacy of the Union and improving the coherence of its action. Ireland was the only EU state to hold a democratic referendum on the Lisbon Treaty. It was initially rejected by voters in 2008.
</p><p>Economic disruption and an unsustainable growth in <a href="/wiki/Government_debt" title="Government debt">government debt</a> during the <a href="/wiki/Financial_crisis_of_2007%E2%80%932008" class="mw-redirect" title="Financial crisis of 2007–2008">financial crisis of 2007–2008</a> led the country to negotiate in 2011 with the IMF and the European Union, through the <a href="/wiki/European_Financial_Stability_Mechanism" class="mw-redirect" title="European Financial Stability Mechanism">European Financial Stability Mechanism</a> (EFSM) and the <a href="/wiki/European_Financial_Stability_Facility" title="European Financial Stability Facility">European Financial Stability Facility</a> (EFSF), a loan to help the country stabilize its finances.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Geography">Geography</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=16" title="Edit section: Geography">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Portugal" title="Geography of Portugal">Geography of Portugal</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Portugal_topographic_map-pt.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Portugal_topographic_map-pt.png/220px-Portugal_topographic_map-pt.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="389" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Portugal_topographic_map-pt.png/330px-Portugal_topographic_map-pt.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Portugal_topographic_map-pt.png/440px-Portugal_topographic_map-pt.png 2x" data-file-width="1738" data-file-height="3070" /></a><figcaption>Topography and administration</figcaption></figure>
<p>Portugal occupies an area on the <a href="/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula" title="Iberian Peninsula">Iberian Peninsula</a> (referred to as <i>the continent</i> by most Portuguese) and two archipelagos in the Atlantic Ocean: <a href="/wiki/Madeira" title="Madeira">Madeira</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Azores" title="Azores">Azores</a>. It lies between latitudes <a href="/wiki/30th_parallel_north" title="30th parallel north">30°</a> and <a href="/wiki/42nd_parallel_north" title="42nd parallel north">42° N</a>, and longitudes <a href="/wiki/32nd_meridian_west" title="32nd meridian west">32°</a> and <a href="/wiki/6th_meridian_west" title="6th meridian west">6° W</a>.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Continental_Portugal" title="Continental Portugal">Mainland Portugal</a> is split by its main river, the <a href="/wiki/Tagus" title="Tagus">Tagus</a>, that flows from Spain and disgorges in the <a href="/wiki/Tagus_Estuary_Natural_Reserve" title="Tagus Estuary Natural Reserve">Tagus Estuary</a> at Lisbon, before escaping into the Atlantic. The northern landscape is mountainous towards the interior with several plateaus indented by river valleys, whereas the south, including the <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Alentejo" title="Alentejo">Alentejo</a> regions, is characterized by rolling plains.<sup id="cite_ref-106" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-106">&#91;102&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Portugal's highest peak is the similarly named <a href="/wiki/Mount_Pico" title="Mount Pico">Mount Pico</a> on the island of <a href="/wiki/Pico_Island" title="Pico Island">Pico</a> in the Azores. This ancient volcano, with a height of 2,351&#160;m (7,713&#160;ft) is an iconic symbol of the Azores. <a href="/wiki/Serra_da_Estrela" title="Serra da Estrela">Serra da Estrela</a> on the mainland (the summit being 1,991&#160;m (6,532&#160;ft) above sea level) is an important seasonal attraction for skiers and winter sports enthusiasts.
</p><p>The archipelagos of Madeira and the Azores are scattered within the Atlantic Ocean: the Azores straddling the <a href="/wiki/Mid-Atlantic_Ridge" title="Mid-Atlantic Ridge">Mid-Atlantic Ridge</a> on a tectonic triple junction, and Madeira along a range formed by <a href="/wiki/Plate_tectonics" title="Plate tectonics">in-plate</a> <a href="/wiki/Hotspot_(geology)" title="Hotspot (geology)">hotspot</a> geology. Geologically, these islands were formed by volcanic and seismic events. The last terrestrial volcanic eruption occurred in 1957–58 (<a href="/wiki/Capelinhos" title="Capelinhos">Capelinhos</a>) and minor earthquakes occur sporadically, usually of low intensity.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone_of_Portugal" title="Exclusive economic zone of Portugal">The exclusive economic zone</a>, a sea zone over which the Portuguese have special rights in exploration and use of marine resources, covers an area of 1,727,408&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (666,956&#160;sq&#160;mi). This is the 3rd largest <a href="/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone" title="Exclusive economic zone">exclusive economic zone</a> of the European Union and the 20th largest in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-107">&#91;103&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Climate">Climate</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=17" title="Edit section: Climate">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Climate_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Climate of Portugal">Climate of Portugal</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Portugal_K%C3%B6ppen.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Portugal_K%C3%B6ppen.svg/200px-Portugal_K%C3%B6ppen.svg.png" decoding="async" width="200" height="445" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Portugal_K%C3%B6ppen.svg/300px-Portugal_K%C3%B6ppen.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Portugal_K%C3%B6ppen.svg/400px-Portugal_K%C3%B6ppen.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="765" data-file-height="1701" /></a><figcaption>Köppen climate classification map of continental Portugal</figcaption></figure>
<p>Portugal is mainly characterized by a <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_climate" title="Mediterranean climate">Mediterranean climate</a> (<i>Csa</i> in the South, central interior, and the <a href="/wiki/Douro" title="Douro">Douro</a> river valley; <i>Csb</i> in the North, Central west and <a href="/wiki/Southwest_Alentejo_and_Vicentine_Coast_Natural_Park" title="Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park">Vicentine Coast)</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-108">&#91;104&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Oceanic_climate" title="Oceanic climate">temperate maritime climate</a> (Cfb) in the mainland north-western highlands and mountains, and in some high altitude zones of the Azorean islands; a <a href="/wiki/Semi-arid_climate" title="Semi-arid climate">semi-arid climate</a> in certain parts of the <a href="/wiki/Beja_District" title="Beja District">Beja District</a> far south (<i>BSk</i>) and in <a href="/wiki/Porto_Santo_Island" title="Porto Santo Island">Porto Santo Island</a> (BSh), a <a href="/wiki/BWh" class="mw-redirect" title="BWh">warm desert climate</a> (BWh) in the <a href="/wiki/Savage_Islands" title="Savage Islands">Selvagens Islands</a> and a <a href="/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate" title="Humid subtropical climate">humid subtropical climate</a> in the western <a href="/wiki/Azores" title="Azores">Azores</a> (Cfa), according to the <a href="/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification" title="Köppen climate classification">Köppen-Geiger Climate Classification</a>. It is one of the warmest countries in Europe: the annual average temperature in <a href="/wiki/Mainland_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Mainland Portugal">mainland Portugal</a> varies from 10–12&#160;°C (50.0–53.6&#160;°F) in the mountainous interior north to 16–18&#160;°C (60.8–64.4&#160;°F) in the south and on the <a href="/wiki/Guadiana" title="Guadiana">Guadiana</a> <a href="/wiki/River_basin" class="mw-redirect" title="River basin">river basin</a>. There are however, variations from the highlands to the lowlands: Spanish biologist Salvador Rivas Martinez presents several different bioclimatic zones for Portugal.<sup id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-109">&#91;105&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a>, separated from the <a href="/wiki/Alentejo" title="Alentejo">Alentejo</a> region by mountains reaching up to 900 metres (3,000&#160;ft) in <a href="/wiki/F%C3%B3ia_(mountain)" title="Fóia (mountain)">Alto da Fóia</a>, has a climate similar to that of the southern coastal areas of Spain or Southwest Australia.
</p><p>Annual average rainfall in the mainland varies from just over 3,200&#160;mm (126.0&#160;in) on the <a href="/wiki/Peneda-Ger%C3%AAs_National_Park" title="Peneda-Gerês National Park">Peneda-Gerês National Park</a> to less than 500&#160;mm (19.7&#160;in) in southern parts of <a href="/wiki/Alentejo" title="Alentejo">Alentejo</a>. <a href="/wiki/Mount_Pico" title="Mount Pico">Mount Pico</a> is recognized as receiving the largest annual rainfall (over 6,250&#160;mm (246.1&#160;in) per year) in Portugal, according to <i><a href="/wiki/Instituto_Portugu%C3%AAs_do_Mar_e_da_Atmosfera" title="Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera">Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera</a></i>.
</p><p>In some areas, such as the Guadiana basin, annual diurnal average temperatures can be as high as 26&#160;°C (79&#160;°F), and summer's highest temperatures are routinely over 40&#160;°C (104&#160;°F). The record high of 47.4&#160;°C (117.3&#160;°F) was recorded in <a href="/wiki/Amareleja" title="Amareleja">Amareleja</a>, although this might not be the hottest spot in summer, according to satellite readings.<sup id="cite_ref-110" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-110">&#91;106&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-111">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Praia_da_Marinha_(2012-09-27),_by_Klugschnacker_in_Wikipedia_(86).JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Praia_da_Marinha_%282012-09-27%29%2C_by_Klugschnacker_in_Wikipedia_%2886%29.JPG/170px-Praia_da_Marinha_%282012-09-27%29%2C_by_Klugschnacker_in_Wikipedia_%2886%29.JPG" decoding="async" width="170" height="256" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Praia_da_Marinha_%282012-09-27%29%2C_by_Klugschnacker_in_Wikipedia_%2886%29.JPG/255px-Praia_da_Marinha_%282012-09-27%29%2C_by_Klugschnacker_in_Wikipedia_%2886%29.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Praia_da_Marinha_%282012-09-27%29%2C_by_Klugschnacker_in_Wikipedia_%2886%29.JPG/340px-Praia_da_Marinha_%282012-09-27%29%2C_by_Klugschnacker_in_Wikipedia_%2886%29.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2848" data-file-height="4288" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Praia_da_Marinha" title="Praia da Marinha">Marinha Beach</a> in <a href="/wiki/Lagoa,_Algarve" class="mw-redirect" title="Lagoa, Algarve">Lagoa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a> is considered by the <a href="/wiki/Michelin_Guide" title="Michelin Guide">Michelin Guide</a> as one of the 10 most beautiful beaches in Europe and as one of the 100 most beautiful beaches in the world.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Snowfalls occur regularly in the winter in the interior North and Centre of the country in districts such as <a href="/wiki/Guarda_District" title="Guarda District">Guarda</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bragan%C3%A7a_District" title="Bragança District">Bragança</a>, <a href="/wiki/Viseu_District" title="Viseu District">Viseu</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vila_Real_District" title="Vila Real District">Vila Real</a>, particularly on the mountains. In winter, temperatures may drop below −10.0&#160;°C (14.0&#160;°F), particularly in <a href="/wiki/Serra_da_Estrela" title="Serra da Estrela">Serra da Estrela</a>, <a href="/wiki/Serra_do_Ger%C3%AAs" class="mw-redirect" title="Serra do Gerês">Serra do Gerês</a>, <a href="/wiki/Serra_do_Mar%C3%A3o" title="Serra do Marão">Serra do Marão</a> and <a href="/wiki/Montesinho_Natural_Park" title="Montesinho Natural Park">Serra de Montesinho</a>. In these places snow can fall any time from October to May. In the South of the country snowfalls are rare but still occur in the highest elevations. While the official absolute minimum by <a href="/wiki/Instituto_Portugu%C3%AAs_do_Mar_e_da_Atmosfera" title="Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera">IPMA</a> is −16.0&#160;°C (3.2&#160;°F) in <a href="/wiki/Penhas_da_Sa%C3%BAde" title="Penhas da Saúde">Penhas da Saúde</a> and <a href="/wiki/Miranda_do_Douro" title="Miranda do Douro">Miranda do Douro</a>, lower temperatures have been recorded, such as −17.5&#160;°C (0.5&#160;°F) by <a href="/wiki/Bragan%C3%A7a,_Portugal" title="Bragança, Portugal">Bragança</a> Polytechnic Institute in the outskirts of the city in 1983, and below −20.0&#160;°C (−4.0&#160;°F) in Serra da Estrela.
</p><p>Continental Portugal receives around 2,300 to 3,200 hours of sunshine a year, an average of 4–6&#160;hours in winter and 10–12&#160;hours in the summer, with higher values in the south-east, south-west and the Algarve coast and lower in the north-west. Insolation values are lower in the archipelagos, with around 1,600 hours in the humid <a href="/wiki/Flores_Island_(Azores)" title="Flores Island (Azores)">Flores Island</a> and around 2,300 hours in the island of Madeira and Porto Santo. Insolation in the <a href="/wiki/Selvagens" class="mw-redirect" title="Selvagens">Selvagens</a> is thought to be higher due to weaker <a href="/wiki/Orographic_lift" title="Orographic lift">orographic lift</a> and their relative proximity to the <a href="/wiki/Sahara_Desert" class="mw-redirect" title="Sahara Desert">Sahara Desert</a>.
</p><p>Portugal's central west and southwest coasts have an extreme ocean <a href="/wiki/Seasonal_lag" title="Seasonal lag">seasonal lag</a>, sea temperatures are warmer in October than in July and are their coldest in March.
The average <a href="/wiki/Sea_surface_temperature" title="Sea surface temperature">sea surface temperature</a> on the west coast of mainland Portugal varies from 14–16&#160;°C (57.2–60.8&#160;°F) in January−March to 19–21&#160;°C (66.2–69.8&#160;°F) in August−October while on the south coast it ranges from 16&#160;°C (60.8&#160;°F) in January−March and rises in the summer to about 22–23&#160;°C (71.6–73.4&#160;°F), occasionally reaching 26&#160;°C (78.8&#160;°F).<sup id="cite_ref-112" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-112">&#91;108&#93;</a></sup> In the Azores, around 16&#160;°C (60.8&#160;°F) in February−April to 22–24&#160;°C (71.6–75.2&#160;°F) in July−September,<sup id="cite_ref-113" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-113">&#91;109&#93;</a></sup> and in Madeira, around 18&#160;°C (64.4&#160;°F) in February−April to 23–24&#160;°C (73.4–75.2&#160;°F) in August−October.<sup id="cite_ref-114" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-114">&#91;110&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Both the archipelagos of the Azores and Madeira have a subtropical climate, although variations between islands exist, making weather predictions very difficult (owing to rough topography). The Madeira and Azorean archipelagos have a narrower temperature range, with annual average temperatures exceeding 20&#160;°C (68&#160;°F) in some parts of the coast (according to the Portuguese Meteorological Institute). Some islands in Azores do have drier months in the summer. Consequently, the islands of the Azores have been identified as having a <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_climate" title="Mediterranean climate">Mediterranean climate</a> (both <i>Csa</i> and <i>Csb</i> types), while some islands (such as <a href="/wiki/Flores_Island_(Azores)" title="Flores Island (Azores)">Flores</a> or <a href="/wiki/Corvo_Island" title="Corvo Island">Corvo</a>) are classified as <a href="/wiki/Humid_subtropical" class="mw-redirect" title="Humid subtropical">Humid subtropical</a> (<i>Cfa</i>), transitioning into an <a href="/wiki/Oceanic_climate" title="Oceanic climate">Oceanic climate</a> (<i>Cfb</i>) at higher altitudes, according to Köppen-Geiger classification.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Porto_Santo_Island" title="Porto Santo Island">Porto Santo Island</a> in Madeira has a warm semi-arid climate (<i>BSh</i>). The <a href="/wiki/Savage_Islands" title="Savage Islands">Savage Islands</a>, which are part of the regional territory of Madeira and a nature reserve are unique in being classified as a desert climate (<i>BWh</i>) with an annual average rainfall of approximately 150&#160;mm (5.9&#160;in). The sea surface temperature in these islands varies from 18.5&#160;°C (65.3&#160;°F) in winter to 23–24&#160;°C (73.4–75.2&#160;°F) in the summer occasionally reaching 25&#160;°C (77.0&#160;°F).<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (March 2017)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Biodiversity">Biodiversity</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=18" title="Edit section: Biodiversity">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1097763485"><table class="box-Split plainlinks metadata ambox ambox-move" role="presentation"><tbody><tr><td class="mbox-image"><div class="mbox-image-div"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Split-arrows.svg/50px-Split-arrows.svg.png" decoding="async" width="50" height="17" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Split-arrows.svg/75px-Split-arrows.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Split-arrows.svg/100px-Split-arrows.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="60" data-file-height="20" /></span></span></div></td><td class="mbox-text"><div class="mbox-text-span">It has been suggested that  this section should be <b><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Splitting" title="Wikipedia:Splitting">split</a></b> into a new article titled <i><a href="/wiki/Biodiversity_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Biodiversity of Portugal">Biodiversity of Portugal</a></i>. (<a href="/wiki/Talk:Portugal" title="Talk:Portugal">discuss</a>)  <span class="date-container"><i>(<span class="date">November 2021</span>)</i></span></div></td></tr></tbody></table>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Dreaming_of_snow_(318977965).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Dreaming_of_snow_%28318977965%29.jpg/200px-Dreaming_of_snow_%28318977965%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="200" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Dreaming_of_snow_%28318977965%29.jpg/300px-Dreaming_of_snow_%28318977965%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Dreaming_of_snow_%28318977965%29.jpg/400px-Dreaming_of_snow_%28318977965%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1970" data-file-height="1970" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Peneda-Ger%C3%AAs_National_Park" title="Peneda-Gerês National Park">Peneda-Gerês National Park</a> is the only nationally designated park in Portugal, owing to the rarity and significance of its environment.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Portugal is located on the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Basin" title="Mediterranean Basin">Mediterranean Basin</a>, the third most diverse hotspot of flora in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-florestas_115-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-florestas-115">&#91;111&#93;</a></sup> Due to its geographical and climatic context - between the Atlantic and Mediterranean - Portugal has a high level of biodiversity on land and at sea. It is home to six terrestrial ecoregions: <a href="/wiki/Azores_temperate_mixed_forests" title="Azores temperate mixed forests">Azores temperate mixed forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cantabrian_mixed_forests" title="Cantabrian mixed forests">Cantabrian mixed forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Madeira_evergreen_forests" title="Madeira evergreen forests">Madeira evergreen forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Iberian_sclerophyllous_and_semi-deciduous_forests" title="Iberian sclerophyllous and semi-deciduous forests">Iberian sclerophyllous and semi-deciduous forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Northwest_Iberian_montane_forests" title="Northwest Iberian montane forests">Northwest Iberian montane forests</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Southwest_Iberian_Mediterranean_sclerophyllous_and_mixed_forests" title="Southwest Iberian Mediterranean sclerophyllous and mixed forests">Southwest Iberian Mediterranean sclerophyllous and mixed forests</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-DinersteinOlson2017_116-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-116">&#91;112&#93;</a></sup> Over 22% of its land area is included in the <a href="/wiki/Natura_2000" title="Natura 2000">Natura 2000</a> network, including 62 special conservation areas and 88 types of protected landscape natural habitats.<sup id="cite_ref-dre_117-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dre-117">&#91;113&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-florestas_115-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-florestas-115">&#91;111&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Eucalyptus" title="Eucalyptus">Eucalyptus</a> (non-native, commercial plantations), <a href="/wiki/Cork_oak" class="mw-redirect" title="Cork oak">cork oak</a> and <a href="/wiki/Maritime_pine" class="mw-redirect" title="Maritime pine">maritime pine</a> together make up 71% of the total forested area of continental Portugal, followed by the <a href="/wiki/Quercus_rotundifolia" title="Quercus rotundifolia">holm oak</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Stone_pine" title="Stone pine">stone pine</a>, the other oak trees (<i><a href="/wiki/Q._robur" class="mw-redirect" title="Q. robur">Q. robur</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Quercus_faginea" title="Quercus faginea">Q. faginea</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Quercus_pyrenaica" title="Quercus pyrenaica">Q. pyrenaica</a></i>) and the <a href="/wiki/Sweet_chestnut" class="mw-redirect" title="Sweet chestnut">sweet chestnut</a>, respectively.<sup id="cite_ref-118" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-118">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup> In Madeira, <a href="/wiki/Laurisilva" class="mw-redirect" title="Laurisilva">laurisilva</a> (recognized as a <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_Site" title="World Heritage Site">World Heritage Site</a>) dominates the landscape, especially on the northern slope. The predominant species in this forest include <i><a href="/wiki/Laurus_novocanariensis" title="Laurus novocanariensis">Laurus novocanariensis</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Apollonias_barbujana" title="Apollonias barbujana">Apollonias barbujana</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Ocotea_foetens" title="Ocotea foetens">Ocotea foetens</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Persea_indica" title="Persea indica">Persea indica</a></i>. Before human occupation the Azores were also rich in dense laurisilva forests, today these native forests are undermined by the introduced <i><a href="/wiki/Pittosporum_undulatum" title="Pittosporum undulatum">Pittosporum undulatum</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Cryptomeria_japonica" class="mw-redirect" title="Cryptomeria japonica">Cryptomeria japonica</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-119" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-119">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-120" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-120">&#91;116&#93;</a></sup> There have been several projects aimed to recover the Laurisilva present in the Azores.<sup id="cite_ref-121" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-121">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup> Remnants of these laurisilva forests are also present in continental Portugal with its few living testimonies <i><a href="/wiki/Laurus_nobilis" title="Laurus nobilis">Laurus nobilis</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Prunus_lusitanica" title="Prunus lusitanica">Prunus lusitanica</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Arbutus_unedo" title="Arbutus unedo">Arbutus unedo</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Myrica_faya" title="Myrica faya">Myrica faya</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Rhododendron_ponticum" title="Rhododendron ponticum">Rhododendron ponticum</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>These geographical and climatic conditions facilitate the introduction of exotic species that later turn to be invasive and destructive to the native habitats. Around 20% of the total number of extant species in continental Portugal are <a href="/wiki/Introduced_species" title="Introduced species">exotic</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-123" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-123">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup> In Madeira, around 36%<sup id="cite_ref-124" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-124">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup> and in the Azores, around 70% species are exotic.<sup id="cite_ref-125" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-125">&#91;121&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-invasoras_126-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-invasoras-126">&#91;122&#93;</a></sup> Due to this, Portugal was placed 168th globally out of 172 countries on the <a href="/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index" title="Forest Landscape Integrity Index">Forest Landscape Integrity Index</a> in 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-FLII-Supplementary_127-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-127">&#91;123&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Chameleo.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Chameleo.jpg/220px-Chameleo.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Chameleo.jpg/330px-Chameleo.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Chameleo.jpg/440px-Chameleo.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3456" data-file-height="2304" /></a><figcaption>Chameleo from <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Portugal is the second country in Europe with the highest number of threatened animal and plant species (488 as of 2020).<sup id="cite_ref-128" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-128">&#91;124&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-129" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-129">&#91;125&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Portugal as a whole is an important stopover for migratory bird species: the southern <a href="/wiki/Marsh" title="Marsh">marshes</a> of the eastern <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a> (<a href="/wiki/Ria_Formosa" title="Ria Formosa">Ria Formosa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Castro_Marim_and_Vila_Real_de_Santo_Ant%C3%B3nio_Marsh_Natural_Reserve" title="Castro Marim and Vila Real de Santo António Marsh Natural Reserve">Castro Marim</a>) and the Lisbon Region (<a href="/wiki/Tagus_Estuary_Natural_Reserve" title="Tagus Estuary Natural Reserve">Tagus Estuary</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sado_Estuary_Natural_Reserve" title="Sado Estuary Natural Reserve">Sado Estuary</a>) hosting various aquatic bird species, the <a href="/wiki/Bonelli%27s_eagle" title="Bonelli&#39;s eagle">Bonelli's eagle</a> and <a href="/wiki/Egyptian_vulture" title="Egyptian vulture">Egyptian vulture</a> on the northern valleys of the <a href="/wiki/Douro_International_Natural_Park" title="Douro International Natural Park">Douro International</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Black_stork" title="Black stork">black stork</a> and <a href="/wiki/Griffon_vulture" class="mw-redirect" title="Griffon vulture">griffon vulture</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Tagus_International_Natural_Park" title="Tagus International Natural Park">Tagus International</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Seabird" title="Seabird">seabird</a> sanctuaries of the <a href="/wiki/Savage_Islands" title="Savage Islands">Savage Islands</a> and <a href="/wiki/Berlengas" title="Berlengas">Berlengas</a> and the highlands of <a href="/wiki/Madeira_Island" title="Madeira Island">Madeira</a> and <a href="/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Miguel_Island" title="São Miguel Island">São Miguel</a> all represent the great diversity of wild avian species (around 450 in continental Portugal), not only migratory but also endemic (e.g. <a href="/wiki/Trocaz_pigeon" title="Trocaz pigeon">trocaz pigeon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Azores_bullfinch" title="Azores bullfinch">Azores bullfinch</a>) or exotic (<a href="/wiki/Crested_myna" title="Crested myna">crested myna</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pin-tailed_whydah" title="Pin-tailed whydah">pin-tailed whydah</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-130" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-130">&#91;126&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-131" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-131">&#91;127&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The large mammalian species of Portugal (the <a href="/wiki/European_fallow_deer" title="European fallow deer">fallow deer</a>, <a href="/wiki/Red_deer" title="Red deer">red deer</a>, <a href="/wiki/Roe_deer" title="Roe deer">roe deer</a>, <a href="/wiki/Iberian_ibex" title="Iberian ibex">Iberian ibex</a>, <a href="/wiki/Wild_boar" title="Wild boar">wild boar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Red_fox" title="Red fox">red fox</a>, <a href="/wiki/Iberian_wolf" title="Iberian wolf">Iberian wolf</a> and <a href="/wiki/Iberian_lynx" title="Iberian lynx">Iberian lynx</a>) were once widespread throughout the country, but intense hunting, habitat degradation and growing pressure from agriculture and livestock reduced population numbers on a large scale in the 19th and early 20th century, others, such as the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_ibex" title="Portuguese ibex">Portuguese ibex</a> were even led to extinction. Today, these animals are re-expanding their native range.<sup id="cite_ref-132" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-132">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-mammals_133-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mammals-133">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup> Smaller mammals include the <a href="/wiki/Red_squirrel" title="Red squirrel">red squirrel</a>, <a href="/wiki/European_badger" title="European badger">European badger</a>, <a href="/wiki/Eurasian_otter" title="Eurasian otter">Eurasian otter</a>, <a href="/wiki/Egyptian_mongoose" title="Egyptian mongoose">Egyptian mongoose</a>, <a href="/wiki/Granada_hare" title="Granada hare">Granada hare</a>, <a href="/wiki/European_rabbit" title="European rabbit">European rabbit</a>, <a href="/wiki/Common_genet" title="Common genet">common genet</a>, <a href="/wiki/European_wildcat" title="European wildcat">European wildcat</a>, among others.<sup id="cite_ref-mammals_133-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mammals-133">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Due to their isolated location, the volcanic islands of the <a href="/wiki/Azores" title="Azores">Azores</a>, <a href="/wiki/Madeira" title="Madeira">Madeira</a> and <a href="/wiki/Salvages" class="mw-redirect" title="Salvages">Salvages</a>, part of <a href="/wiki/Macaronesia" title="Macaronesia">Macaronesia</a>, have many endemic species that have evolved independently from their European, African and occasionally American relatives.
</p><p>The Portuguese west coast is part of the four major Eastern Boundary <a href="/wiki/Upwelling" title="Upwelling">Upwelling</a> Systems of the ocean. This seasonal upwelling system typically seen during the summer months brings cooler, nutrient rich water up to the sea surface promoting <a href="/wiki/Phytoplankton" title="Phytoplankton">phytoplankton</a> growth, <a href="/wiki/Zooplankton" title="Zooplankton">zooplankton</a> development and the subsequent rich diversity in <a href="/wiki/Pelagic_fish" title="Pelagic fish">pelagic fish</a> and other <a href="/wiki/Marine_invertebrates" title="Marine invertebrates">marine invertebrates</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-134" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-134">&#91;130&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Portugal_EEZ.PNG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Portugal_EEZ.PNG/350px-Portugal_EEZ.PNG" decoding="async" width="350" height="275" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e6/Portugal_EEZ.PNG 1.5x" data-file-width="501" data-file-height="394" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone_of_Portugal" title="Exclusive economic zone of Portugal">Exclusive economic zone of Portugal</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>This, adding to its large <a href="/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone_of_Portugal" title="Exclusive economic zone of Portugal">EEZ</a> makes Portugal one of the largest per capita fish-consumers in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135">&#91;131&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Sardine" title="Sardine">Sardines</a> (<i><a href="/wiki/Sardina_pilchardus" class="mw-redirect" title="Sardina pilchardus">Sardina pilchardus</a></i>) and <a href="/wiki/Horse_mackerel" title="Horse mackerel">horse mackerel</a> (<i><a href="/wiki/Trachurus_trachurus" class="mw-redirect" title="Trachurus trachurus">Trachurus trachurus</a></i>) are collected in the thousands every year.<sup id="cite_ref-136" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-136">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup> while <a href="/wiki/Blue_whiting" title="Blue whiting">blue whiting</a>, <a href="/wiki/Monkfish" class="mw-redirect" title="Monkfish">monkfish</a>, <a href="/wiki/Atlantic_cod" title="Atlantic cod">Atlantic cod</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cephalopod" title="Cephalopod">cephalopods</a>, <a href="/wiki/Skate_(fish)" title="Skate (fish)">skates</a> or any other form of <a href="/wiki/Seafood" title="Seafood">seafood</a> are <a href="/wiki/Artisanal_fishing" title="Artisanal fishing">traditionally fished</a> in the local coastal villages.<sup id="cite_ref-137" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-137">&#91;133&#93;</a></sup> This upwelling also allows Portugal to have <a href="/wiki/Kelp_forests" class="mw-redirect" title="Kelp forests">kelp forests</a> which are otherwise very uncommon or non-existent on the Mediterranean.<sup id="cite_ref-138" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-138">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>73% of the <a href="/wiki/Freshwater_fish" title="Freshwater fish">freshwater fish</a> occurring in the <a href="/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula" title="Iberian Peninsula">Iberian Peninsula</a> are endemic, the largest out of any region in Europe.<sup id="cite_ref-139" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-139">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup> Many of these endemic species are concentrated in bodies of water of the central western region (<a href="/wiki/Achondrostoma_occidentale" title="Achondrostoma occidentale">one exclusively endemic</a>), these and other bodies of water throughout the Peninsula are mostly temporary and prone to drought every year, placing most of these species under <a href="/wiki/Threatened" class="mw-redirect" title="Threatened">Threatened</a> status.<sup id="cite_ref-140" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-140">&#91;136&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Around 24<sup id="cite_ref-barreiros_141-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-barreiros-141">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup> to 28<sup id="cite_ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup> species of <a href="/wiki/Cetacean" class="mw-redirect" title="Cetacean">cetacean</a> roam through the Azores, making it one of four places in the world where most species of this infraorder occur.<sup id="cite_ref-barreiros_141-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-barreiros-141">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup> Starting in the mid-19th century and ceasing in 1984, <a href="/wiki/Whaling" title="Whaling">whaling</a> (especially of <a href="/wiki/Sperm_whale" title="Sperm whale">sperm whale</a>) heavily exploited this diversity. Beginning in the early 90s, <a href="/wiki/Whale_watching" title="Whale watching">whale watching</a> quickly grew to popularity and is now one of the main economic activities in the Portuguese archipelago.<sup id="cite_ref-143" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-143">&#91;139&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-144" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-144">&#91;140&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Some <a href="/wiki/Protected_areas_of_Portugal" title="Protected areas of Portugal">protected areas in Portugal</a> other than the ones previously mentioned include: the <a href="/wiki/Serras_de_Aire_e_Candeeiros_Natural_Park" title="Serras de Aire e Candeeiros Natural Park">Serras de Aire e Candeeiros</a> with its limestone formations, paleontological history and great diversity in <a href="/wiki/Bats" class="mw-redirect" title="Bats">bats</a> and <a href="/wiki/Orchid" title="Orchid">orchids</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Southwest_Alentejo_and_Vicentine_Coast_Natural_Park" title="Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park">Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park</a> with its well preserved, wild coastline.<sup id="cite_ref-146" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-146">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Montesinho_Natural_Park" title="Montesinho Natural Park">Montesinho Natural Park</a> which hosts some of the only populations of <a href="/wiki/Iberian_wolf" title="Iberian wolf">Iberian wolf</a> and recent sightings of <a href="/wiki/Iberian_brown_bear" class="mw-redirect" title="Iberian brown bear">Iberian brown bear</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-147" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-147">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup> which had been considered extinct in the country; among other species.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Government_and_politics">Government and politics</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=19" title="Edit section: Government and politics">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Portugal" title="Government of Portugal">Government of Portugal</a> and <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Portugal" title="Politics of Portugal">Politics of Portugal</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:298px;max-width:298px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:147px;max-width:147px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa_(Web_Summit).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa_%28Web_Summit%29.jpg/145px-Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa_%28Web_Summit%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="145" height="217" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa_%28Web_Summit%29.jpg/218px-Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa_%28Web_Summit%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa_%28Web_Summit%29.jpg/290px-Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa_%28Web_Summit%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2667" data-file-height="4000" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center"><a href="/wiki/Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa" title="Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa">Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa</a><br /><span style="font-size:85%;"><a href="/wiki/President_of_Portugal" title="President of Portugal">President of Portugal</a><br />since 2016</span></div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:147px;max-width:147px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa-_2017_-_Web_Summit_-_24778904437.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa-_2017_-_Web_Summit_-_24778904437.jpg/145px-Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa-_2017_-_Web_Summit_-_24778904437.jpg" decoding="async" width="145" height="217" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa-_2017_-_Web_Summit_-_24778904437.jpg/218px-Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa-_2017_-_Web_Summit_-_24778904437.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa-_2017_-_Web_Summit_-_24778904437.jpg/290px-Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa-_2017_-_Web_Summit_-_24778904437.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2667" data-file-height="4000" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center"><a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa" title="António Costa">António Costa</a><br /><span style="font-size:85%;"><a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Portugal" title="Prime Minister of Portugal">Prime Minister of Portugal</a><br />since 2015</span></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>Portugal has been a <a href="/wiki/Semi-presidential_system" class="mw-redirect" title="Semi-presidential system">semi-presidential</a> <a href="/wiki/Representative_democracy" title="Representative democracy">representative democratic</a> <a href="/wiki/Republic" title="Republic">republic</a> since the ratification of the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Constitution_of_1976" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Constitution of 1976">Constitution of 1976</a>, with <a href="/wiki/Lisbon" title="Lisbon">Lisbon</a>, the nation's largest city, as its capital.<sup id="cite_ref-148" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-148">&#91;144&#93;</a></sup> The Constitution grants the division or separation of powers among four <a href="/w/index.php?title=Sovereignty_body_(Portugal)&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Sovereignty body (Portugal) (page does not exist)">"sovereignty bodies"</a><span class="noprint" style="font-size:85%; font-style: normal;">&#160;&#91;<a href="https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%93rg%C3%A3o_de_soberania_(Portugal)" class="extiw" title="pt:Órgão de soberania (Portugal)">pt</a>&#93;</span>: the <a href="/wiki/President_of_Portugal" title="President of Portugal">President of the Republic</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Portugal" title="Government of Portugal">Government</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_parliament" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese parliament">Assembly of the Republic</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Judiciary_of_Portugal" title="Judiciary of Portugal">Courts</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-constitution_149-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-constitution-149">&#91;145&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The President, who is elected to a five-year term, has an executive role: the current President is <a href="/wiki/Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa" title="Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa">Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa</a>. The Assembly of the Republic is a single chamber parliament composed of a maximum of 230 deputies elected for a four-year term. The Government is headed by the <a href="/wiki/List_of_Prime_Ministers_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="List of Prime Ministers of Portugal">Prime Minister</a> (currently <a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa" title="António Costa">António Costa</a>) and includes Ministers and Secretaries of State. The <a href="/wiki/Courts" class="mw-redirect" title="Courts">Courts</a> are organized into several levels, among the judicial, administrative and fiscal branches. The <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Supreme_Court" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Supreme Court">Supreme Courts</a> are institutions of last resort/appeal. A thirteen-member <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Constitutional_Court" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Constitutional Court">Constitutional Court</a> oversees the constitutionality of the laws.
</p><p>Portugal operates a multi-party system of competitive legislatures/local administrative governments at the national, regional and local levels. The Assembly of the Republic, Regional Assemblies and local municipalities and parishes, are dominated by two political parties, the <a href="/wiki/Socialist_Party_(Portugal)" title="Socialist Party (Portugal)">Socialist Party</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Social_Democratic_Party_(Portugal)" title="Social Democratic Party (Portugal)">Social Democratic Party</a>, in addition to <a href="/wiki/Chega_(political_party)" title="Chega (political party)">Enough</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Liberal_Initiative_(Portugal)" class="mw-redirect" title="Liberal Initiative (Portugal)">Liberal Initiative</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Unitary_Democratic_Coalition" title="Unitary Democratic Coalition">Unitary Democratic Coalition</a> (<a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Communist_Party" title="Portuguese Communist Party">Portuguese Communist Party</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ecologist_Party_%22The_Greens%22" title="Ecologist Party &quot;The Greens&quot;">Ecologist Party "The Greens"</a>) and the <a href="/wiki/Left_Bloc_(Portugal)" title="Left Bloc (Portugal)">Left Bloc</a>, which garner between 5 and 15% of the vote regularly.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Presidency_of_the_Republic">Presidency of the Republic</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=20" title="Edit section: Presidency of the Republic">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/President_of_Portugal" title="President of Portugal">President of Portugal</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Portugal" title="List of presidents of Portugal">List of presidents of Portugal</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Lisbon,_Bel%C3%A9m_Palace.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Lisbon%2C_Bel%C3%A9m_Palace.JPG/220px-Lisbon%2C_Bel%C3%A9m_Palace.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Lisbon%2C_Bel%C3%A9m_Palace.JPG/330px-Lisbon%2C_Bel%C3%A9m_Palace.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Lisbon%2C_Bel%C3%A9m_Palace.JPG/440px-Lisbon%2C_Bel%C3%A9m_Palace.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2764" data-file-height="1843" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Bel%C3%A9m_Palace" title="Belém Palace">Belém Palace</a> serves as the official residence and workplace of the <a href="/wiki/President_of_Portugal" title="President of Portugal">President of the Republic</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Head of State of Portugal is the <a href="/wiki/President_of_Portugal" title="President of Portugal">President of the Republic</a>, elected to a five-year term by direct, <a href="/wiki/Universal_suffrage" title="Universal suffrage">universal suffrage</a>. Presidential powers include the appointment of the Prime Minister and the other members of the Government (where the President takes into account the results of legislative elections); dismissing the Prime Minister; dissolving the Assembly of the Republic (to call early elections); <a href="/wiki/Veto" title="Veto">vetoing</a> legislation (which may be overridden by the Assembly); and declaring a state of war or siege. The President has also supervisory and <a href="/wiki/Reserve_power" title="Reserve power">reserve powers</a> and is the <i><a href="/wiki/Ex_officio" class="mw-redirect" title="Ex officio">ex officio</a></i> Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces.
</p><p>The President is advised on issues of importance by the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Council_of_State" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Council of State">Council of State</a>, which is composed of six senior civilian officers, any former Presidents elected under the 1976 Constitution, five members chosen by the Assembly, and five selected by the president.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Government">Government</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=21" title="Edit section: Government">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Portugal" title="Government of Portugal">Government of Portugal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Portugal" title="Prime Minister of Portugal">Prime Minister of Portugal</a>, and <a href="/wiki/List_of_Prime_Ministers_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="List of Prime Ministers of Portugal">List of Prime Ministers of Portugal</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Lisboa_April_2014-15a.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Lisboa_April_2014-15a.jpg/250px-Lisboa_April_2014-15a.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="90" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Lisboa_April_2014-15a.jpg/375px-Lisboa_April_2014-15a.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Lisboa_April_2014-15a.jpg/500px-Lisboa_April_2014-15a.jpg 2x" data-file-width="12707" data-file-height="4585" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Pra%C3%A7a_do_Com%C3%A9rcio" title="Praça do Comércio">Praça do Comércio</a> houses multiple ministries of the <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Portugal" title="Government of Portugal">Government of Portugal</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Government is headed by the presidentially appointed <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Portugal" title="Prime Minister of Portugal">Prime Minister</a>, also including one or more Deputy Prime Ministers, Ministers, Secretaries of State and Under-Secretaries of State.
</p><p>The Government is both the organ of sovereignty that conducts the general politics of the country and the superior body of the public administration.
</p><p>It has essentially Executive powers, but has also limited legislative powers. The Government can legislate about its own organization, about areas covered by legislative authorizations conceded by the Assembly of the Republic and about the specific regulation of generalist laws issued by the Assembly.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Ministers_(Portugal)" title="Council of Ministers (Portugal)">Council of Ministers</a> – under the presidency of the Prime Minister (or the President of Portugal at the latter's request) and the Ministers (may also include one or more Deputy Prime Ministers) – acts as the <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_(government)" title="Cabinet (government)">cabinet</a>. Each government is required to define the broad outline of its policies in a programme, and present it to the Assembly for a mandatory period of debate. The failure of the Assembly to reject the government programme by an absolute majority of deputies confirms the cabinet in office.
</p>
<div style="clear:both;"></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Parliament">Parliament</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=22" title="Edit section: Parliament">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Portuguese_Parliament_building_front_fachade.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Portuguese_Parliament_building_front_fachade.jpg/220px-Portuguese_Parliament_building_front_fachade.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Portuguese_Parliament_building_front_fachade.jpg/330px-Portuguese_Parliament_building_front_fachade.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Portuguese_Parliament_building_front_fachade.jpg/440px-Portuguese_Parliament_building_front_fachade.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2592" data-file-height="1944" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Assembly_of_the_Republic_(Portugal)" title="Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)">Assembly of the Republic</a> is housed in <a href="/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Bento_Palace" title="São Bento Palace">São Bento Palace</a> in Lisbon.</figcaption></figure>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Assembly_of_the_Republic_(Portugal)" title="Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)">Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_political_parties_in_Portugal" title="List of political parties in Portugal">List of political parties in Portugal</a></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Assembly_of_the_Republic_(Portugal)" title="Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)">Assembly of the Republic</a>, in Lisbon, is the national <a href="/wiki/Parliament" title="Parliament">parliament</a> of Portugal. It is the main legislative body, although the Government also has limited legislative powers.
</p><p>The Assembly of the Republic is a unicameral body composed of up to 230 deputies. Elected by universal suffrage according to a system of <a href="/wiki/Closed_list" title="Closed list">closed</a> <a href="/wiki/Party-list_proportional_representation" title="Party-list proportional representation">party-list proportional representation</a>, deputies serve four-year terms of office, unless the President dissolves the Assembly and calls for new elections.
</p><p>Currently the Government (<a href="/wiki/Socialist_Party_(Portugal)" title="Socialist Party (Portugal)">PS</a>) has an absolute majority of seats in Parliament. The <a href="/wiki/Social_Democratic_Party_(Portugal)" title="Social Democratic Party (Portugal)">PSD</a> is the main opposition party, alongside <a href="/wiki/Chega_(political_party)" title="Chega (political party)">Chega</a>, <a href="/wiki/Liberal_Initiative_(Portugal)" class="mw-redirect" title="Liberal Initiative (Portugal)">Liberal Initiative</a>, <a href="/wiki/Left_Bloc_(Portugal)" title="Left Bloc (Portugal)">BE</a>, <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Communist_Party" title="Portuguese Communist Party">PCP</a>, <a href="/wiki/People%E2%80%93Animals%E2%80%93Nature" class="mw-redirect" title="People–Animals–Nature">PAN</a> and <a href="/wiki/LIVRE" title="LIVRE">Livre</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_relations">Foreign relations</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=23" title="Edit section: Foreign relations">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Portugal" title="Foreign relations of Portugal">Foreign relations of Portugal</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Pal%C3%A1cio_das_Necessidades_1997.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Pal%C3%A1cio_das_Necessidades_1997.JPG/220px-Pal%C3%A1cio_das_Necessidades_1997.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Pal%C3%A1cio_das_Necessidades_1997.JPG/330px-Pal%C3%A1cio_das_Necessidades_1997.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Pal%C3%A1cio_das_Necessidades_1997.JPG/440px-Pal%C3%A1cio_das_Necessidades_1997.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2608" data-file-height="1952" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Palace_of_Necessidades" class="mw-redirect" title="Palace of Necessidades">Necessidades Palace</a> houses the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Portugal)" title="Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Portugal)">Ministry of Foreign Affairs</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres_2012.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres_2012.jpg/220px-Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres_2012.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="154" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres_2012.jpg/330px-Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres_2012.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres_2012.jpg/440px-Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres_2012.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4858" data-file-height="3396" /></a><figcaption>Current <a href="/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations" title="Secretary-General of the United Nations">Secretary-General of the United Nations</a> and former Prime Minister <a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres" title="António Guterres">António Guterres</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>A member state of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a> since 1955, Portugal is also a founding member of <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a> (1949), <a href="/wiki/OECD" title="OECD">OECD</a> (1961) and <a href="/wiki/European_Free_Trade_Association" title="European Free Trade Association">EFTA</a> (1960); it left the last in 1986 to join the <a href="/wiki/European_Economic_Community" title="European Economic Community">European Economic Community</a>, which became the European Union in 1993.
</p><p>In 1996, Portugal co-founded the <a href="/wiki/Community_of_Portuguese_Language_Countries" title="Community of Portuguese Language Countries">Community of Portuguese Language Countries</a> (CPLP), also known as the Lusophone Commonwealth, an international organization and political association of <a href="/wiki/Lusophone" class="mw-redirect" title="Lusophone">Lusophone</a> nations across four continents, where <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_language" title="Portuguese language">Portuguese</a> is an official language. The global headquarters of the CPLP is in <a href="/wiki/Penafiel_Palace" title="Penafiel Palace">Penafiel Palace</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Lisbon" title="Lisbon">Lisbon</a>.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres" title="António Guterres">António Guterres</a>, who has served as Prime Minister of Portugal from 1995 to 2002 and <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_High_Commissioner_for_Refugees" title="United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees">UN High Commissioner for Refugees</a> from 2005 to 2015, assumed the post of <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Secretary-General" class="mw-redirect" title="United Nations Secretary-General">UN Secretary-General</a> on 1 January 2017; making him the first Secretary-General from Western Europe since <a href="/wiki/Kurt_Waldheim" title="Kurt Waldheim">Kurt Waldheim</a> of Austria (1972–1981), the first former head of government to become Secretary-General and the first Secretary-General born after the establishment of the United Nations on 26 June 1945.
</p><p>In addition, Portugal was a full member of the <a href="/wiki/Latin_Union" title="Latin Union">Latin Union</a> (1983) and the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_Ibero-American_States" title="Organization of Ibero-American States">Organization of Ibero-American States</a> (1949). It has a friendship alliance and <a href="/wiki/Multiple_citizenship" title="Multiple citizenship">dual citizenship</a> treaty with its former colony, Brazil. Portugal and the United Kingdom share the world's oldest active military accord through their <a href="/wiki/Anglo-Portuguese_Alliance" title="Anglo-Portuguese Alliance">Anglo-Portuguese Alliance</a> (<a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Windsor_(1386)" title="Treaty of Windsor (1386)">Treaty of Windsor</a>), which was signed in 1373.
</p><p>There are two international territorial disputes, both with Spain:
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Olivenza" title="Olivenza">Olivenza</a>. Under Portuguese sovereignty since 1297, the municipality of Olivença was ceded to Spain under the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Badajoz_(1801)" title="Treaty of Badajoz (1801)">Treaty of Badajoz</a> in 1801, after the <a href="/wiki/War_of_the_Oranges" title="War of the Oranges">War of the Oranges</a>. Portugal claimed it back in 1815 under the <a href="/wiki/Congress_of_Vienna" title="Congress of Vienna">Treaty of Vienna</a>. However, since the 19th century, it has been continuously ruled by Spain which considers the territory theirs not only <i>de facto</i> but also <i>de jure</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-One-europe.net_2017-09-29_150-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-One-europe.net_2017-09-29-150">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li>The Ilhas Selvagens (<a href="/wiki/Savage_Islands" title="Savage Islands">Savage Islands</a>), a small group of mostly uninhabited islets which fall under Portuguese Madeira's regional autonomous jurisdiction. Found in 1364 by Italian mariners under the service of <a href="/wiki/Prince_Henry_The_Navigator" class="mw-redirect" title="Prince Henry The Navigator">Prince Henry The Navigator</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-151" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-151">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup> it was first noted by Portuguese navigator Diogo Gomes de Sintra in 1438. Historically, the islands have belonged to private Portuguese owners from the 16th century on, until 1971<sup id="cite_ref-152" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-152">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> when the government purchased them and established a natural reserve area covering the whole archipelago. The islands have been claimed by Spain since 1911,<sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153">&#91;149&#93;</a></sup> and the dispute has caused some periods of political tension between the two countries.<sup id="cite_ref-154" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-154">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup> The main problem for Spain's attempts to claim these small islands, has been not so much their intrinsic value, but the fact that they expand Portugal's <a href="/wiki/Exclusive_Economic_Zone" class="mw-redirect" title="Exclusive Economic Zone">Exclusive Economic Zone</a> considerably to the south, in detriment of Spain.<sup id="cite_ref-155" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-155">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup> The Selvagens Islands have been tentatively added to UNESCO's world heritage list in 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup></li></ul>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Military">Military</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=24" title="Edit section: Military">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Armed_Forces" title="Portuguese Armed Forces">Portuguese Armed Forces</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:224px;max-width:224px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Exercise_TRIDENT_JUNCTURE_(22791211312).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Exercise_TRIDENT_JUNCTURE_%2822791211312%29.jpg/220px-Exercise_TRIDENT_JUNCTURE_%2822791211312%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="141" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Exercise_TRIDENT_JUNCTURE_%2822791211312%29.jpg/330px-Exercise_TRIDENT_JUNCTURE_%2822791211312%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Exercise_TRIDENT_JUNCTURE_%2822791211312%29.jpg/440px-Exercise_TRIDENT_JUNCTURE_%2822791211312%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="6015" data-file-height="3867" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Army" title="Portuguese Army">Portuguese Army</a> - <a href="/wiki/Leopard_2A6" class="mw-redirect" title="Leopard 2A6">Leopard 2A6</a>.</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:POS_Corte_Real_(F_332).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/POS_Corte_Real_%28F_332%29.jpg/220px-POS_Corte_Real_%28F_332%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/POS_Corte_Real_%28F_332%29.jpg/330px-POS_Corte_Real_%28F_332%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/POS_Corte_Real_%28F_332%29.jpg/440px-POS_Corte_Real_%28F_332%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3872" data-file-height="2592" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Navy" title="Portuguese Navy">Portuguese Navy</a> - <a href="/wiki/MEKO_200" title="MEKO 200">MEKO-200 PN</a>.</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:20151026_christian.timmig_Portuguese_Aircraft_08_(22495887796).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/20151026_christian.timmig_Portuguese_Aircraft_08_%2822495887796%29.jpg/220px-20151026_christian.timmig_Portuguese_Aircraft_08_%2822495887796%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/20151026_christian.timmig_Portuguese_Aircraft_08_%2822495887796%29.jpg/330px-20151026_christian.timmig_Portuguese_Aircraft_08_%2822495887796%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/20151026_christian.timmig_Portuguese_Aircraft_08_%2822495887796%29.jpg/440px-20151026_christian.timmig_Portuguese_Aircraft_08_%2822495887796%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2200" data-file-height="1467" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Air_Force" title="Portuguese Air Force">Portuguese Air Force</a> - <a href="/wiki/General_Dynamics_F-16_Fighting_Falcon" title="General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon">F-16 Fighting Falcons</a>.</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Comandos_Portugal.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Comandos_Portugal.jpg/220px-Comandos_Portugal.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Comandos_Portugal.jpg/330px-Comandos_Portugal.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Comandos_Portugal.jpg/440px-Comandos_Portugal.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1367" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Commandos_(Portugal)" title="Commandos (Portugal)">Portuguese Army Commandos</a>.</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>The armed forces have three branches: <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Navy" title="Portuguese Navy">Navy</a>, <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Army" title="Portuguese Army">Army</a> and <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Air_Force" title="Portuguese Air Force">Air Force</a>. They serve primarily as a self-defence force whose mission is to protect the territorial integrity of the country and provide humanitarian assistance and security at home and abroad. As of 2008<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, the three branches numbered 39,200 active personnel including 7,500 women. <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_military_expenditures" title="List of countries by military expenditures">Portuguese military expenditure</a> in 2009 was 5 billion US$,<sup id="cite_ref-157" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-157">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup> representing 2.1 per cent of GDP. Military conscription was abolished in 2004. The minimum age for voluntary recruitment is 18 years.
</p><p>The Army (21,000 personnel) comprises three brigades and other small units. An <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Intervention_Brigade" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Intervention Brigade">infantry brigade</a> (mainly equipped with <a href="/wiki/Pandur_II" title="Pandur II">Pandur II</a> <a href="/wiki/Armoured_personnel_carrier" title="Armoured personnel carrier">APC</a>), a <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Mechanized_Brigade" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Mechanized Brigade">mechanized brigade</a> (mainly equipped with <a href="/wiki/Leopard_2" title="Leopard 2">Leopard 2 A6</a> tanks and <a href="/wiki/M113" class="mw-redirect" title="M113">M113</a> APC) and a <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Rapid_Reaction_Brigade" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Rapid Reaction Brigade">Rapid Reaction Brigade</a> (consisting of <a href="/wiki/Paratroopers%27_Regiment" title="Paratroopers&#39; Regiment">paratroopers</a>, <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Army_Commandos" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Army Commandos">commandos</a> and rangers). The Navy (10,700 personnel, of which 1,580 are <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Marines" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Marines">marines</a>), the world's oldest surviving naval force, has five frigates, seven corvettes, two submarines, and 28 patrol and auxiliary vessels. The Air Force (7,500 personnel) has the <a href="/wiki/Lockheed_F-16_Fighting_Falcon" class="mw-redirect" title="Lockheed F-16 Fighting Falcon">Lockheed F-16 Fighting Falcon</a> as the main combat aircraft.
</p><p>In addition to the three branches of the armed forces, there is the <a href="/wiki/National_Republican_Guard_(Portugal)" title="National Republican Guard (Portugal)">National Republican Guard</a>, a security force subject to military law and organization (<a href="/wiki/Gendarmerie" title="Gendarmerie">gendarmerie</a>) comprising 25,000 personnel. This force is under the authority of both the Defence and the Interior Ministry. It has provided detachments for participation in international operations in Iraq and East Timor.
</p><p>The United States maintains a military presence with 770 troops in the <a href="/wiki/Lajes_Air_Base" class="mw-redirect" title="Lajes Air Base">Lajes Air Base</a> at <a href="/wiki/Terceira_Island" title="Terceira Island">Terceira Island</a>, in the Azores. The <a href="/wiki/Allied_Joint_Force_Command_Lisbon" title="Allied Joint Force Command Lisbon">Allied Joint Force Command Lisbon</a> (JFC Lisbon)&#160;– one of the three main subdivisions of <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Allied_Command_Operations" title="Allied Command Operations">Allied Command Operations</a>&#160;– it is based in <a href="/wiki/Oeiras_Municipality,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Oeiras Municipality, Portugal">Oeiras</a>, near Lisbon.
</p><p>In the 20th century, Portugal engaged in two major conflicts: <a href="/wiki/Portugal_in_the_Great_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Portugal in the Great War">World War I</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Colonial_War" title="Portuguese Colonial War">Portuguese Colonial War</a> (1961–1974). After the end of the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Empire" title="Portuguese Empire">Portuguese Empire</a> in 1975, the Portuguese Armed Forces have participated in peacekeeping missions in East Timor, Bosnia, Kosovo, Afghanistan, Somalia, Iraq (<a href="/wiki/Nasiriyah" title="Nasiriyah">Nasiriyah</a>), Lebanon, <a href="/wiki/Mali" title="Mali">Mali</a><sup id="cite_ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Central_African_Republic" title="Central African Republic">Central African Republic</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup> Portugal also conducted several independent unilateral military operations abroad, as were the cases of the interventions of the Portuguese Armed Forces in Angola in 1992 and in Guinea-Bissau in 1998 with the main objectives of protecting and withdrawing of Portuguese and foreign citizens threatened by local civil conflicts.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Law">Law</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=25" title="Edit section: Law">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Campus_Justi%C3%A7a_(cropped).JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Campus_Justi%C3%A7a_%28cropped%29.JPG/220px-Campus_Justi%C3%A7a_%28cropped%29.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="158" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Campus_Justi%C3%A7a_%28cropped%29.JPG/330px-Campus_Justi%C3%A7a_%28cropped%29.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Campus_Justi%C3%A7a_%28cropped%29.JPG/440px-Campus_Justi%C3%A7a_%28cropped%29.JPG 2x" data-file-width="1305" data-file-height="940" /></a><figcaption>Lisbon's Campus of Justice</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Tribunal_Constitucional_Portugal.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Tribunal_Constitucional_Portugal.jpg/170px-Tribunal_Constitucional_Portugal.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="255" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Tribunal_Constitucional_Portugal.jpg/255px-Tribunal_Constitucional_Portugal.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Tribunal_Constitucional_Portugal.jpg/340px-Tribunal_Constitucional_Portugal.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3456" data-file-height="5184" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_Court_(Portugal)" title="Constitutional Court (Portugal)">Portuguese Constitutional Court</a></figcaption></figure>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Judiciary_of_Portugal" title="Judiciary of Portugal">Judiciary of Portugal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Law_of_Portugal" title="Law of Portugal">Law of Portugal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Drug_policy_of_Portugal" title="Drug policy of Portugal">Drug policy of Portugal</a>, and <a href="/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Portugal" title="LGBT rights in Portugal">LGBT rights in Portugal</a></div>
<p>The Portuguese legal system is part of the civil law legal system, also called the continental family legal system. The main laws include the Constitution (1976, as amended), the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Civil_Code" title="Portuguese Civil Code">Portuguese Civil Code</a> (1966, as amended) and the <a href="/wiki/Penal_Code_of_Portugal" title="Penal Code of Portugal">Penal Code of Portugal</a> (1982, as amended). Other relevant laws are the <i>Commercial Code</i> (1888, as amended) and the <i>Civil Procedure Code</i> (1961, as amended).
</p><p>The supreme national courts are the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Justice_(Portugal)" title="Supreme Court of Justice (Portugal)">Supreme Court of Justice</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Constitutional Court of Portugal">Constitutional Court</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Public_Prosecution_Service_(Portugal)" title="Public Prosecution Service (Portugal)">Public Ministry</a>, headed by the Attorney General of the Republic, constitutes the independent body of public prosecutors.
</p><p>Portuguese laws were applied in the former <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_colonies" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese colonies">colonies and territories</a> and continue to be major influences for those countries.
