</p><p>Portugal was the first country in the world to abolish <a href="/wiki/Life_imprisonment" title="Life imprisonment">life imprisonment</a> (in 1884) and was one of the first countries to <a href="/wiki/Capital_punishment_in_Portugal" title="Capital punishment in Portugal">abolish the death penalty</a>. Maximum prison sentences are limited to 25 years.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Drug" title="Drug">Drug</a> <a href="/wiki/Decriminalisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Decriminalisation">decriminalisation</a> was declared in 2001, making Portugal the first country in the world to allow usage and personal possession of all common drugs. Portugal decriminalized possession of effectively all drugs that are still illegal in other developed nations, including <a href="/wiki/Cannabis" title="Cannabis">cannabis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cocaine" title="Cocaine">cocaine</a>, <a href="/wiki/Heroin" title="Heroin">heroin</a>, and <a href="/wiki/LSD" title="LSD">LSD</a>. While possession is legal, trafficking and possession of more than "10 days worth of personal use" are still punishable by jail time and fines. People caught with small amounts of any drug are given the choice to go to a rehab facility, and may refuse treatment without consequences. Despite criticism from other European nations, who stated Portugal's drug consumption would tremendously increase, overall drug use has declined along with the number of <a href="/wiki/HIV" title="HIV">HIV</a> infection cases, which had dropped 50 percent by 2009. Drug use among 16- to 18-year-olds also declined, however the use of marijuana rose only slightly among that age group.<sup id="cite_ref-160" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-160">&#91;156&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Portugal" title="LGBT rights in Portugal">LGBTI rights</a> have increased substantially in the past years. On 27 August 2003, Portugal added the anti-discrimination employment law on the basis of sexual orientation.<sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup> At 24 July 2004, sexual orientation was added to the Constitution as part of the protected from discrimination characteristics.<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup> On 31 May 2010, Portugal became the sixth country in Europe and the eighth country in the world to legally recognize <a href="/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Portugal" title="Same-sex marriage in Portugal">same-sex marriage</a> at the national level. The law came into force on 5 June 2010.<sup id="cite_ref-autogenerated2_165-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-autogenerated2-165">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/LGBT_adoption" class="mw-redirect" title="LGBT adoption">Same-sex adoption</a> has been allowed since 1 March 2016<sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup> as is female same-sex couple access to medically assisted reproduction since 13 May 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup> This bill was adopted by the Parliament and signed by President <a href="/wiki/Marcelo_Rebelo_de_Sousa" title="Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa">Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168">&#91;164&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170">&#91;166&#93;</a></sup> As of January 2017 the New <i>Law of Gender Identity</i>,<sup id="cite_ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171">&#91;167&#93;</a></sup> simplified the legal process of <a href="/wiki/Gender" title="Gender">gender</a> and name change for <a href="/wiki/Transgender" title="Transgender">transgender</a> people, making it easier for minors to change their <a href="/wiki/Sex_marker" class="mw-redirect" title="Sex marker">sex marker</a> in legal documents.<sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172">&#91;168&#93;</a></sup> At August 2018, the right to <a href="/wiki/Gender_identity" title="Gender identity">gender identity</a> and <a href="/wiki/Gender_expression" title="Gender expression">gender expression</a> self-determination became protected, <a href="/wiki/Intersex" title="Intersex">intersex</a> minors became protected by law from unnecessary <a href="/wiki/Intersex_medical_interventions" title="Intersex medical interventions">medical procedures</a> "until the minor gender identity manifests" and the right of protection from discrimination on the basis of <a href="/wiki/Sex_characteristics_(legal_term)" title="Sex characteristics (legal term)">sex characteristics</a> also became protected by the same law.<sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Euthanasia" title="Euthanasia">Euthanasia</a> has been legalised in Portugal, after several reviews in parliament. Nationals over 18 who are terminally ill and in extreme suffering but who can still decide to, have the legal right to request for assisted dying. However, non-residents are not allowed to request for assisted euthanasia in Portugal.<sup id="cite_ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup> Only a small number of other countries like <a href="/wiki/Belgium" title="Belgium">Belgium</a>, <a href="/wiki/Colombia" title="Colombia">Colombia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Luxembourg" title="Luxembourg">Luxembourg</a>, <a href="/wiki/Netherlands" title="Netherlands">Netherlands</a>, <a href="/wiki/New_Zealand" title="New Zealand">New Zealand</a>, <a href="/wiki/Spain" title="Spain">Spain</a> currently allow for assisted dying.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Law_enforcement">Law enforcement</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=26" title="Edit section: Law enforcement">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Render_da_Guarda_no_Palacio_de_Belem_22.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Render_da_Guarda_no_Palacio_de_Belem_22.JPG/170px-Render_da_Guarda_no_Palacio_de_Belem_22.JPG" decoding="async" width="170" height="256" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Render_da_Guarda_no_Palacio_de_Belem_22.JPG/255px-Render_da_Guarda_no_Palacio_de_Belem_22.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Render_da_Guarda_no_Palacio_de_Belem_22.JPG/340px-Render_da_Guarda_no_Palacio_de_Belem_22.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2848" data-file-height="4288" /></a><figcaption>A cavalryman of the <a href="/wiki/National_Republican_Guard_(Portugal)" title="National Republican Guard (Portugal)">National Republican Guard</a>'s honour guard</figcaption></figure>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_Portugal" title="Law enforcement in Portugal">Law enforcement in Portugal</a></div>
<p>Portugal's main police organizations are the <i><a href="/wiki/Guarda_Nacional_Republicana" class="mw-redirect" title="Guarda Nacional Republicana">Guarda Nacional Republicana</a>&#160;– GNR</i> (<a href="/wiki/National_Republican_Guard_(Portugal)" title="National Republican Guard (Portugal)">National Republican Guard</a>), a <a href="/wiki/Gendarmerie" title="Gendarmerie">gendarmerie</a>; the <i><a href="/wiki/Pol%C3%ADcia_de_Seguran%C3%A7a_P%C3%BAblica" title="Polícia de Segurança Pública">Polícia de Segurança Pública</a>&#160;– PSP</i> (Public Security Police), a civilian police force who work in urban areas; and the <i><a href="/wiki/Pol%C3%ADcia_Judici%C3%A1ria" title="Polícia Judiciária">Polícia Judiciária</a>&#160;– PJ</i> (Judicial Police), a highly specialized criminal investigation police that is overseen by the Public Ministry.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Correctional_services">Correctional services</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=27" title="Edit section: Correctional services">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<p>Portugal has 49 correctional facilities in total run by the Ministry of Justice. They include seventeen central prisons, four special prisons, twenty-seven regional prisons, and one 'Cadeia de Apoio' (Support Detention Centre).<sup id="cite_ref-176" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-176">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup> As of 1&#160;January&#160;2021<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, their current prison population is about 11,234 inmates, which comes to about 0.11% of their entire population.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_177-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-177">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup> Their incarceration rate has been on the rise since 2010, with a 15% increase over the past eight years.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_177-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-177">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Administrative_divisions">Administrative divisions</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=28" title="Edit section: Administrative divisions">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Portugal" title="Administrative divisions of Portugal">Administrative divisions of Portugal</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:NUTS_PT_2013.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/NUTS_PT_2013.png/250px-NUTS_PT_2013.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="339" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/NUTS_PT_2013.png/375px-NUTS_PT_2013.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/NUTS_PT_2013.png/500px-NUTS_PT_2013.png 2x" data-file-width="1454" data-file-height="1970" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/NUTS_statistical_regions_of_Portugal" title="NUTS statistical regions of Portugal">NUTS 2 and 3 of Portugal</a> since 2013.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Administratively, Portugal is divided into 308 <a href="/wiki/Municipalities_of_Portugal" title="Municipalities of Portugal">municipalities</a> (<a href="/wiki/Portuguese_language" title="Portuguese language">Portuguese</a>: <i lang="pt">municípios or <a href="/wiki/Concelhos" class="mw-redirect" title="Concelhos">concelhos</a></i>), which after a reform in <a href="/wiki/2013_Portuguese_local_election" class="mw-redirect" title="2013 Portuguese local election">2013</a> are subdivided into 3,092 civil parishes (<a href="/wiki/Portuguese_language" title="Portuguese language">Portuguese</a>: <i lang="pt"><a href="/wiki/Freguesia" title="Freguesia">freguesia</a></i>). Operationally, the municipality and civil parish, along with the national government, are the only legally <a href="/wiki/Local_administrative_unit" class="mw-redirect" title="Local administrative unit">local administrative units</a> identified by the government of Portugal (for example, cities, towns or villages have no standing in law, although may be used as catchment for the defining services).
</p><p>For statistical purposes the Portuguese government also identifies <a href="/wiki/Nomenclature_of_Territorial_Units_for_Statistics" title="Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics">Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics</a> (NUTS), inter-municipal communities and informally, the district system, used until European integration (and being phased-out by the national government).<sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:No_original_research" title="Wikipedia:No original research"><span title="The material near this tag possibly contains original research. (February 2016)">original research?</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> Continental Portugal is agglomerated into 18 districts, while the archipelagos of the Azores and Madeira are governed as <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_area" class="mw-redirect" title="Autonomous area">autonomous regions</a>; the largest units, established since 1976, are either <a href="/wiki/Mainland_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Mainland Portugal">mainland Portugal</a> (<a href="/wiki/Portuguese_language" title="Portuguese language">Portuguese</a>: <i lang="pt">Portugal Continental</i>) and the <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_regions_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Autonomous regions of Portugal">autonomous regions of Portugal</a> (<a href="/wiki/Azores" title="Azores">Azores</a> and <a href="/wiki/Madeira" title="Madeira">Madeira</a>).
</p><p>The 18 districts of mainland Portugal are: <a href="/wiki/Aveiro_District" title="Aveiro District">Aveiro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Beja_District" title="Beja District">Beja</a>, <a href="/wiki/Braga_District" title="Braga District">Braga</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bragan%C3%A7a_District" title="Bragança District">Bragança</a>, <a href="/wiki/Castelo_Branco_District" title="Castelo Branco District">Castelo Branco</a>, <a href="/wiki/Coimbra_District" title="Coimbra District">Coimbra</a>, <a href="/wiki/%C3%89vora_District" title="Évora District">Évora</a>, <a href="/wiki/Faro_District" title="Faro District">Faro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Guarda_District" title="Guarda District">Guarda</a>, <a href="/wiki/Leiria_District" title="Leiria District">Leiria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lisbon_District" title="Lisbon District">Lisbon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Portalegre_District" title="Portalegre District">Portalegre</a>, <a href="/wiki/Porto_District" title="Porto District">Porto</a>, <a href="/wiki/Santar%C3%A9m_District" title="Santarém District">Santarém</a>, <a href="/wiki/Set%C3%BAbal_District" title="Setúbal District">Setúbal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Viana_do_Castelo_District" title="Viana do Castelo District">Viana do Castelo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vila_Real_District" title="Vila Real District">Vila Real</a> and <a href="/wiki/Viseu_District" title="Viseu District">Viseu</a>&#160;– each district takes the name of the district capital.
</p><p>Within the European Union NUTS system, Portugal is divided into seven regions: the <a href="/wiki/Azores" title="Azores">Azores</a>, <a href="/wiki/Alentejo" title="Alentejo">Alentejo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a>, <a href="/wiki/Centro,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Centro, Portugal">Centro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lisboa_Region" class="mw-redirect" title="Lisboa Region">Lisboa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Madeira" title="Madeira">Madeira</a> and <a href="/wiki/Norte,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Norte, Portugal">Norte</a>, and with the exception of the Azores and Madeira, NUTS areas are subdivided into 28 subregions.
</p>
