<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Government_finance">Government finance</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=29" title="Edit section: Government finance">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/2010%E2%80%932014_Portuguese_financial_crisis" title="2010–2014 Portuguese financial crisis">2010–2014 Portuguese financial crisis</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Portuguese_debt_and_EU_average.png" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Portuguese debt compared to Eurozone average" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Portuguese_debt_and_EU_average.png/220px-Portuguese_debt_and_EU_average.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="213" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Portuguese_debt_and_EU_average.png/330px-Portuguese_debt_and_EU_average.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Portuguese_debt_and_EU_average.png/440px-Portuguese_debt_and_EU_average.png 2x" data-file-width="703" data-file-height="681" /></a><figcaption>Debt as a percentage of the <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Portugal" title="Economy of Portugal">economy of Portugal</a>, compared to eurozone average</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Portuguese government is heavily indebted, and received a 78-billion-euro bailout from the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> and the <a href="/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund" title="International Monetary Fund">International Monetary Fund</a> in May 2011.<sup id="cite_ref-nytimes_179-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nytimes-179">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup> The ratio of Portugal's debt to its overall economy, was 107 per cent when it received the bailout.<sup id="cite_ref-nytimes_179-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nytimes-179">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup> As part of the deal, the country agreed to cut its budget deficit from 9.8 per cent of GDP in 2010 to 5.9 per cent in 2011, 4.5 per cent in 2012 and 3 per cent in 2013.<sup id="cite_ref-reuters1_180-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reuters1-180">&#91;176&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>After the bailout was announced, the Portuguese government headed by <a href="/wiki/Pedro_Passos_Coelho" title="Pedro Passos Coelho">Pedro Passos Coelho</a> managed to implement measures with the intention of improving the state's financial situation, including tax hikes, a freeze of civil service-related lower-wages and cuts of higher-wages by 14.3%, on top of the government's spending cuts. The Portuguese government also agreed to eliminate its <a href="/wiki/Golden_share" title="Golden share">golden share</a> in <a href="/wiki/Portugal_Telecom" class="mw-redirect" title="Portugal Telecom">Portugal Telecom</a> which gave it veto power over vital decisions.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup> In 2012, all public servants had already seen an average wage cut of 20% relative to their 2010 baseline, with cuts reaching 25% for those earning more than 1,500 euro per month.<sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The IMF, the <a href="/wiki/European_Commission" title="European Commission">European Commission</a> (EC) and the <a href="/wiki/European_Central_Bank" title="European Central Bank">European Central Bank</a> (ECB) said in September 2012 that Portugal's debt would peak at 124 per cent of gross domestic product in 2014.<sup id="cite_ref-October_2012_status_184-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-October_2012_status-184">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup> The IMF previously said in July 2012 that Portugal's debt would peak at about 118.5 per cent of GDP in 2013.<sup id="cite_ref-October_2012_status_184-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-October_2012_status-184">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup> In September 2013, the Portuguese Government reviewed again the public debt of Portugal for 2013 to 127.8 per cent, after a peak of 130.9 per cent in that month.<sup id="cite_ref-September_2013_status_185-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-September_2013_status-185">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>A report released in January 2011 by the <a href="/wiki/Di%C3%A1rio_de_Not%C3%ADcias" title="Diário de Notícias">Diário de Notícias</a><sup id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup> and published in Portugal by <a href="/wiki/Gradiva" title="Gradiva">Gradiva</a>, had demonstrated that in the period between the <a href="/wiki/Carnation_Revolution" title="Carnation Revolution">Carnation Revolution</a> in 1974 and 2010, the democratic <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Portugal" title="Government of Portugal">Portuguese Republic governments</a> encouraged over-expenditure and investment bubbles through unclear <a href="/wiki/Public%E2%80%93private_partnership" title="Public–private partnership">Public–private partnerships</a> and funding of numerous ineffective and unnecessary external consultancy and advisory of committees and firms.
This allowed considerable <a href="/wiki/Slippage_(finance)" title="Slippage (finance)">slippage</a> in state-managed <a href="/wiki/Public_works" title="Public works">public works</a> and inflated top management and head officer bonuses and wages. Persistent and lasting recruitment policies boosted the number of redundant public servants. Risky <a href="/wiki/Credit_(finance)" class="mw-redirect" title="Credit (finance)">credit</a>, <a href="/wiki/Public_debt" class="mw-redirect" title="Public debt">public debt</a> creation, and European <a href="/wiki/Structural_and_cohesion_funds" class="mw-redirect" title="Structural and cohesion funds">structural and cohesion funds</a> were mismanaged across almost four decades.<sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Two Portuguese banks, <a href="/wiki/Banco_Portugu%C3%AAs_de_Neg%C3%B3cios" title="Banco Português de Negócios">Banco Português de Negócios</a> (BPN) and <a href="/wiki/Banco_Privado_Portugu%C3%AAs" title="Banco Privado Português">Banco Privado Português</a> (BPP), had been accumulating losses for years due to bad investments, embezzlement and accounting fraud. The case of BPN was particularly serious because of its size, market share, and the political implications – Portugal's then President, Cavaco Silva and some of his political allies, maintained personal and business relationships with the bank and its CEO, who was eventually charged and arrested for fraud and other crimes.<sup id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-190" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-190">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup> On grounds of avoiding a potentially serious financial crisis in the Portuguese economy, the Portuguese government decided to give them a bailout, eventually at a future loss to taxpayers and to the Portuguese people in general.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Economy">Economy</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=30" title="Edit section: Economy">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Portugal" title="Economy of Portugal">Economy of Portugal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Economic_history_of_Portugal" title="Economic history of Portugal">Economic history of Portugal</a>, and <a href="/wiki/List_of_Portuguese_administrative_divisions_by_GDP" title="List of Portuguese administrative divisions by GDP">List of Portuguese administrative divisions by GDP</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Parque_das_Na%C3%A7%C3%B5es_31.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Parque_das_Na%C3%A7%C3%B5es_31.jpg/220px-Parque_das_Na%C3%A7%C3%B5es_31.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="139" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Parque_das_Na%C3%A7%C3%B5es_31.jpg/330px-Parque_das_Na%C3%A7%C3%B5es_31.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Parque_das_Na%C3%A7%C3%B5es_31.jpg/440px-Parque_das_Na%C3%A7%C3%B5es_31.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1293" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Vasco_da_Gama_Tower" title="Vasco da Gama Tower">Vasco da Gama Tower</a> in <a href="/wiki/Parque_das_Na%C3%A7%C3%B5es" title="Parque das Nações">Parque das Nações</a> with the <a href="/wiki/Vasco_da_Gama_Bridge" title="Vasco da Gama Bridge">Vasco da Gama Bridge</a> in <a href="/wiki/Lisbon" title="Lisbon">Lisbon</a></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Portugal_Product_Exports_(2019).svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Portugal_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg/220px-Portugal_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="143" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Portugal_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg/330px-Portugal_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Portugal_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg/440px-Portugal_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1100" data-file-height="715" /></a><figcaption>A proportional representation of Portugal's exports, as of 2019<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>Portugal is a <a href="/wiki/Developed_country" title="Developed country">developed</a> and a <a href="/wiki/High_income_countries" class="mw-redirect" title="High income countries">high-income country</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-191" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-191">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-192" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-192">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup> it ranks highly in <a href="/wiki/Global_Peace_Index" title="Global Peace Index">peacefulness</a>, <a href="/wiki/Democracy" title="Democracy">democracy</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-194" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-194">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Press_Freedom_Index" class="mw-redirect" title="Press Freedom Index">press freedom</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_Fragile_States_Index" title="List of countries by Fragile States Index">stability</a>, <a href="/wiki/Social_Progress_Index" title="Social Progress Index">social progress</a>, <a href="/wiki/Legatum_Prosperity_Index" title="Legatum Prosperity Index">prosperity</a> and <a href="/wiki/EF_English_Proficiency_Index" title="EF English Proficiency Index">English proficiency</a>. With a GDP per capita of 77% of the EU27 average in 2022 (an increase from 75% in 2021)<sup id="cite_ref-195" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-195">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup> and a <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_Human_Development_Index" title="List of countries by Human Development Index">HDI</a> of 0.866 (the 38th highest in the world, just behind Saudi Arabia's) in 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-196" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-196">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-197" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-197">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup> Portugal has been a net beneficiary to the <a href="/wiki/Budget_of_the_European_Union" title="Budget of the European Union">European Union budget</a> since it joined the union, then known as <a href="/wiki/European_Economic_Community" title="European Economic Community">EEC</a>, in 1986.<sup id="cite_ref-198" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-198">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-199" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-199">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-200" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-200">&#91;196&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-201" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-201">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>By the end of 2022, Portugal's GDP (PPP) was $42,341 per capita, according to OECD's report.<sup id="cite_ref-202" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-202">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup> By 2021, Portugal had the 4th lowest GDP per capita (PPP) of the eurozone out of 19 members, and the 8th lowest of the European Union out of 27 member-states.<sup id="cite_ref-203" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-203">&#91;199&#93;</a></sup> Several former economically disadvantaged <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Bloc" title="Eastern Bloc">Communist Bloc</a> countries which in the meanwhile had become Eastern European member-states of the EU, had reached or surpassed Portugal in terms of GDP (PPP) per capita around this date.<sup id="cite_ref-204" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-204">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-205" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-205">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup> In 2021, <a href="/wiki/Workforce_productivity" title="Workforce productivity">labour productivity</a> had fallen to the fifth lowest among the 27 member-states of the European Union (EU) and was 35% lower than the EU average, with only Latvia, Poland, Bulgaria, and Greece being lower to Portugal in that parameter.<sup id="cite_ref-206" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-206">&#91;202&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-207" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-207">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup> In 2022, it had fallen to the fourth lowest position.<sup id="cite_ref-208" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-208">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup> Within the EU, Portugal's economy ranks lower than most Western states.<sup id="cite_ref-209" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-209">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Portugal was one of the original <a href="/wiki/Eurozone" title="Eurozone">eurozone</a> member nations. The national currency, the <a href="/wiki/Euro" title="Euro">euro</a> (€) started transitioning from the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Escudo" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese Escudo">Portuguese Escudo</a> in 2000 and consolidated in 2002. Portugal's central bank is the <i><a href="/wiki/Banco_de_Portugal" title="Banco de Portugal">Banco de Portugal</a></i>, an integral part of the <a href="/wiki/European_System_of_Central_Banks" title="European System of Central Banks">European System of Central Banks</a>. Most industries, businesses and financial institutions are concentrated in the <a href="/wiki/Lisbon_metropolitan_area" title="Lisbon metropolitan area">Lisbon</a> and <a href="/wiki/Greater_Metropolitan_Area_of_Porto" class="mw-redirect" title="Greater Metropolitan Area of Porto">Porto</a> metropolitan areas – the <a href="/wiki/Set%C3%BAbal_District" title="Setúbal District">Setúbal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Aveiro_District" title="Aveiro District">Aveiro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Braga_District" title="Braga District">Braga</a>, <a href="/wiki/Coimbra_District" title="Coimbra District">Coimbra</a>, <a href="/wiki/Leiria_District" title="Leiria District">Leiria</a> and <a href="/wiki/Faro_District" title="Faro District">Faro</a> districts are the biggest economic centres outside these two main areas.
According to World Travel Awards, Portugal was Europe's Leading Golf Destination in 2012 and 2013.<sup id="cite_ref-210" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-210">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-211" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-211">&#91;207&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:LGPK.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/LGPK.jpg/220px-LGPK.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/LGPK.jpg/330px-LGPK.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/LGPK.jpg/440px-LGPK.jpg 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="600" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Oeiras_Municipality,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Oeiras Municipality, Portugal">Oeiras Municipality</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Lisbon_metropolitan_area" title="Lisbon metropolitan area">Lisbon metropolitan area</a>, has the headquarters of several Portuguese subsidiaries of major multinational companies.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Since the <a href="/wiki/Carnation_Revolution" title="Carnation Revolution">Carnation Revolution</a> of 1974, which culminated in the end of one of Portugal's most notable <a href="/wiki/Economic_history_of_Portugal" title="Economic history of Portugal">phases of economic expansion</a> (that started in the 1960s),<sup id="cite_ref-212" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-212">&#91;208&#93;</a></sup> a significant change has occurred in the nation's annual economic growth.<sup id="cite_ref-213" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-213">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup> After the turmoil of the 1974 revolution and the <a href="/wiki/Processo_Revolucion%C3%A1rio_Em_Curso" title="Processo Revolucionário Em Curso">PREC</a> period, Portugal tried to adapt to a changing <a href="/wiki/Globalization" title="Globalization">modern global economy</a>, a process that continues in 2013. Since the 1990s, Portugal's <a href="/wiki/Consumption_(economics)" title="Consumption (economics)">public consumption</a>-based <a href="/wiki/Economic_development" title="Economic development">economic development</a> model has been slowly changing to a system that is focused on exports, private <a href="/wiki/Investment_(macroeconomics)" title="Investment (macroeconomics)">investment</a> and the development of the <a href="/wiki/High-tech" class="mw-redirect" title="High-tech">high-tech</a> sector. Consequently, business services have overtaken more traditional industries such as textiles, clothing, footwear and <a href="/wiki/Cork_(material)" title="Cork (material)">cork</a> (Portugal is the world's leading cork producer),<sup id="cite_ref-214" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-214">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup> wood products and beverages.<sup id="cite_ref-autogenerated1_215-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-autogenerated1-215">&#91;211&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the second decade of the 21st century, the Portuguese economy suffered its most severe recession since the 1970s, resulting in the country having to be bailed out by the European Commission, European Central Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF). The bailout, agreed to in 2011, required <a href="/wiki/Portugal_and_the_IMF" class="mw-redirect" title="Portugal and the IMF">Portugal</a> to enter into a range of austerity measures in exchange for funding support of €78,000,000,000. In May 2014, the country exited the bailout but reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining its reformist momentum. At the time of exiting the bailout, the economy had contracted by 0.7% in the first quarter of 2014; however, unemployment, while still high, had fallen to 15.3%.<sup id="cite_ref-PortugalBailoutEnds_216-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-PortugalBailoutEnds-216">&#91;212&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:November_2011_Austerity_Protest_in_Lisbon,_Portugal.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/November_2011_Austerity_Protest_in_Lisbon%2C_Portugal.JPG/220px-November_2011_Austerity_Protest_in_Lisbon%2C_Portugal.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="125" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/November_2011_Austerity_Protest_in_Lisbon%2C_Portugal.JPG/330px-November_2011_Austerity_Protest_in_Lisbon%2C_Portugal.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/November_2011_Austerity_Protest_in_Lisbon%2C_Portugal.JPG/440px-November_2011_Austerity_Protest_in_Lisbon%2C_Portugal.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4592" data-file-height="2615" /></a><figcaption>November 2011 protests against austerity measures of the <a href="/wiki/Economic_Adjustment_Programme_for_Portugal" title="Economic Adjustment Programme for Portugal">Economic Adjustment Programme for Portugal</a> outside the <a href="/wiki/Assembly_of_the_Republic_(Portugal)" title="Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)">Assembly of the Republic</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The average salary in Portugal is €1,044 per month, excluding self-employed individuals<sup id="cite_ref-217" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-217">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/Minimum_wage" title="Minimum wage">minimum wage</a>, which is regulated by law, is €760 per month (paid 14 times per annum) as of 2023.<sup id="cite_ref-218" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-218">&#91;214&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Global_Competitiveness_Report" title="Global Competitiveness Report">Global Competitiveness Report</a> for 2019, published by the <a href="/wiki/World_Economic_Forum" title="World Economic Forum">World Economic Forum</a>, placed Portugal on the 34th position on the economic index.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Economist_Intelligence_Unit" title="Economist Intelligence Unit">Economist Intelligence Unit</a>'s quality of life index placed Portugal as the country with the 19th-best quality of life in the world for 2005, ahead of other economically and technologically advanced countries like <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</a>, <a href="/wiki/Germany" title="Germany">Germany</a>, the <a href="/wiki/United_Kingdom" title="United Kingdom">United Kingdom</a> and <a href="/wiki/South_Korea" title="South Korea">South Korea</a>, but nine places behind its sole neighbour, Spain.<sup id="cite_ref-219" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-219">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup> 
Major <a href="/wiki/Government-owned_corporation" class="mw-redirect" title="Government-owned corporation">state-owned companies</a> include: <a href="/wiki/%C3%81guas_de_Portugal" title="Águas de Portugal">Águas de Portugal</a> (water), <a href="/wiki/Caixa_Geral_de_Dep%C3%B3sitos" title="Caixa Geral de Depósitos">Caixa Geral de Depósitos</a> (banking), <a href="/wiki/Comboios_de_Portugal" title="Comboios de Portugal">Comboios de Portugal</a> (railways), <a href="/wiki/Companhia_das_Lez%C3%ADrias" title="Companhia das Lezírias">Companhia das Lezírias</a> (agriculture) and <a href="/wiki/R%C3%A1dio_e_Televis%C3%A3o_de_Portugal" title="Rádio e Televisão de Portugal">RTP</a> (media). Some former state-owned entities are managed by state-run <a href="/wiki/Holding_company" title="Holding company">holding company</a> <a href="/wiki/Parp%C3%BAblica" title="Parpública">Parpública</a>, which is a <a href="/wiki/Shareholder" title="Shareholder">shareholder</a> of several public and private companies.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2013)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> Among former state-owned companies recently privatized are: <a href="/wiki/CTT_Correios_de_Portugal,_S.A." title="CTT Correios de Portugal, S.A.">CTT</a> (postal service) and <a href="/wiki/ANA_Aeroportos_de_Portugal" title="ANA Aeroportos de Portugal">ANA</a> (airports).
</p><p>Companies listed on <a href="/wiki/Euronext_Lisbon" title="Euronext Lisbon">Euronext Lisbon</a> <a href="/wiki/Stock_exchange" title="Stock exchange">stock exchange</a> like <a href="/wiki/Energias_de_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Energias de Portugal">EDP</a>, <a href="/wiki/Galp_Energia" title="Galp Energia">Galp</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jer%C3%B3nimo_Martins" title="Jerónimo Martins">Jerónimo Martins</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mota-Engil" title="Mota-Engil">Mota-Engil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Novabase" title="Novabase">Novabase</a>, <a href="/wiki/Semapa" title="Semapa">Semapa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Portucel_Soporcel" class="mw-redirect" title="Portucel Soporcel">Portucel Soporcel</a>, <a href="/wiki/Portugal_Telecom" class="mw-redirect" title="Portugal Telecom">Portugal Telecom</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sonae" title="Sonae">Sonae</a>, are amongst the largest corporations of Portugal by number of employees, <a href="/wiki/Net_income" title="Net income">net income</a> or international <a href="/wiki/Market_share" title="Market share">market share</a>. The Euronext Lisbon is the major stock exchange of Portugal and is part of the pan-European group of stock exchanges <a href="/wiki/Euronext" title="Euronext">Euronext</a>. The <a href="/wiki/PSI-20" title="PSI-20">PSI-20</a> is Portugal's most selective and widely known <a href="/wiki/Stock_index" class="mw-redirect" title="Stock index">stock index</a>.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund" title="International Monetary Fund">International Monetary Fund</a> issued an update report on the economy of Portugal in late-June 2017 with a strong near-term outlook and an increase in investments and exports over previous years. Because of a surplus in 2016, the country was no longer bound by the Excessive Deficit Procedure which had been implemented during an earlier financial crisis. The banking system was more stable, although there were still non-performing loans and corporate debt. The IMF recommended working on solving these problems for Portugal to be able to attract more private investment. "Sustained strong growth, together with continued public debt reduction, would reduce vulnerabilities arising from high indebtedness, particularly when monetary accommodation is reduced."
The <a href="/wiki/OECD" title="OECD">OECD</a> economic reports since 2018 show recovery, albeit slow; and Portugal's growth prospects continue positive for 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-220" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-220">&#91;216&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-221" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-221">&#91;217&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-222" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-222">&#91;218&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In recent years, rents and house prices have skyrocketed in Portugal, particularly in Lisbon, where rents jumped 37% in 2022. Portugal's 8.3% inflation rate in the same year exacerbated the problem.<sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223">&#91;219&#93;</a></sup> 
Also according to the IMF, Portugal's economic recovery from the COVID-19 Pandemic in 2022 was substantially higher than the EU average. Although modest, economic growth is expected to proceed in 2023 while inflation is forecast to continue decreasing to 5.1%.<sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224">&#91;220&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-225" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-225">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Primary_sector">Primary sector</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=31" title="Edit section: Primary sector">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Agriculture_in_Portugal" title="Agriculture in Portugal">Agriculture in Portugal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fishing_in_Portugal" title="Fishing in Portugal">Fishing in Portugal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mining_in_Portugal" title="Mining in Portugal">Mining in Portugal</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_wine" title="Portuguese wine">Portuguese wine</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Campilhas_March_2015-1a.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Campilhas_March_2015-1a.jpg/290px-Campilhas_March_2015-1a.jpg" decoding="async" width="290" height="97" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Campilhas_March_2015-1a.jpg/435px-Campilhas_March_2015-1a.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Campilhas_March_2015-1a.jpg/580px-Campilhas_March_2015-1a.jpg 2x" data-file-width="11283" data-file-height="3766" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Alentejo" title="Alentejo">Alentejo</a> is known as the "breadbasket of Portugal", being the country's leading region in wheat and cork production.</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Agriculture_in_Portugal" title="Agriculture in Portugal">Agriculture in Portugal</a> is based on small to medium-sized family-owned dispersed units. However, the sector also includes larger scale <a href="/wiki/Intensive_farming" title="Intensive farming">intensive farming</a> export-oriented <a href="/wiki/Agrobusiness" class="mw-redirect" title="Agrobusiness">agrobusinesses</a> backed by companies (like <a href="/wiki/Grupo_RAR" title="Grupo RAR">Grupo RAR</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Vitacress" title="Vitacress">Vitacress</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sovena" class="mw-redirect" title="Sovena">Sovena</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lactogal" title="Lactogal">Lactogal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vale_da_Rosa" title="Vale da Rosa">Vale da Rosa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Companhia_das_Lez%C3%ADrias" title="Companhia das Lezírias">Companhia das Lezírias</a> and <a href="/wiki/Valouro" title="Valouro">Valouro</a>). The country produces a wide variety of crops and livestock products, including: <a href="/wiki/Tomato" title="Tomato">tomatoes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Citrus" title="Citrus">citrus</a>, <a href="/wiki/Green_vegetables" class="mw-redirect" title="Green vegetables">green vegetables</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a>, <a href="/wiki/Wheat" title="Wheat">wheat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Barley" title="Barley">barley</a>, <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">maize</a>, <a href="/wiki/Olive" title="Olive">olives</a>, <a href="/wiki/Oilseed" class="mw-redirect" title="Oilseed">oilseeds</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nut_(fruit)" title="Nut (fruit)">nuts</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cherry" title="Cherry">cherries</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bilberry" title="Bilberry">bilberry</a>, <a href="/wiki/Table_grapes" class="mw-redirect" title="Table grapes">table grapes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Edible_mushroom" title="Edible mushroom">edible mushrooms</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dairy_products" class="mw-redirect" title="Dairy products">dairy products</a>, <a href="/wiki/Poultry" title="Poultry">poultry</a> and <a href="/wiki/Beef" title="Beef">beef</a>. According to <a href="/wiki/FAO" class="mw-redirect" title="FAO">FAO</a>, Portugal is the top producer of <a href="/wiki/Cork_(material)" title="Cork (material)">cork</a> and <a href="/wiki/Carob" title="Carob">carob</a> in the world, accounting to about 50% and 30% of world production, respectively.<sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226">&#91;222&#93;</a></sup> It is also the third largest exporter of <a href="/wiki/Chestnut" title="Chestnut">chestnuts</a> and the third largest European producer of <a href="/wiki/Pulp_(paper)" title="Pulp (paper)">pulp</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227">&#91;223&#93;</a></sup> Portugal is among the top ten largest <a href="/wiki/Olive_oil" title="Olive oil">olive oil</a> producers in the world and is the fourth largest exporter.<sup id="cite_ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup> The country is also one of the world's largest exporters of <a href="/wiki/Wine" title="Wine">wine</a>, being reputed for its <a href="/wiki/Fine_wine" class="mw-redirect" title="Fine wine">fine wines</a>.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Forestry" title="Forestry">Forestry</a> has also played an important economic role among the rural communities and industry (namely <a href="/wiki/Paper_industry" class="mw-redirect" title="Paper industry">paper industry</a> that includes <a href="/wiki/Portucel_Soporcel_Group" class="mw-redirect" title="Portucel Soporcel Group">Portucel Soporcel Group</a>, <a href="/wiki/Engineered_wood" title="Engineered wood">engineered wood</a> that includes <a href="/wiki/Sonae_Ind%C3%BAstria" title="Sonae Indústria">Sonae Indústria</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Furniture" title="Furniture">furniture</a> that includes several manufacturing plants in and around <a href="/wiki/Pa%C3%A7os_de_Ferreira" title="Paços de Ferreira">Paços de Ferreira</a>, the core of Portugal's major industrial operations of <a href="/wiki/IKEA" title="IKEA">IKEA</a>). In 2001, the gross agricultural product accounted for 4% of the national GDP.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Valen%C3%A7a_do_Douro_edited.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Valen%C3%A7a_do_Douro_edited.jpg/220px-Valen%C3%A7a_do_Douro_edited.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Valen%C3%A7a_do_Douro_edited.jpg/330px-Valen%C3%A7a_do_Douro_edited.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Valen%C3%A7a_do_Douro_edited.jpg/440px-Valen%C3%A7a_do_Douro_edited.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4288" data-file-height="2848" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Douro_river" class="mw-redirect" title="Douro river">Douro valley</a> vineyards which produce the worldwide known <a href="/wiki/Port_wine" title="Port wine">Port wine</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Traditionally a sea power, Portugal has had a strong tradition in <a href="/wiki/Fishing_in_Portugal" title="Fishing in Portugal">the Portuguese fishing sector</a> and is one of the countries with the highest fish consumption per capita.<sup id="cite_ref-229" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-229">&#91;225&#93;</a></sup> The main landing sites in Portugal (including Azores and Madeira), according to total landings in weight by year, are the harbours of <a href="/wiki/Matosinhos" title="Matosinhos">Matosinhos</a>, <a href="/wiki/Peniche,_Portugal" title="Peniche, Portugal">Peniche</a>, <a href="/wiki/Olh%C3%A3o" title="Olhão">Olhão</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sesimbra" title="Sesimbra">Sesimbra</a>, <a href="/wiki/Figueira_da_Foz" title="Figueira da Foz">Figueira da Foz</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sines,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Sines, Portugal">Sines</a>, <a href="/wiki/Portim%C3%A3o" title="Portimão">Portimão</a> and <a href="/wiki/Madeira" title="Madeira">Madeira</a>. Portuguese-processed fish products are exported through several companies, under a number of different brands and registered trademarks, such as <a href="/wiki/Conservas_Ramirez" title="Conservas Ramirez">Ramirez</a>, the world's oldest active canned fish producer.
</p><p>Portugal is a significant European <a href="/wiki/Minerals" class="mw-redirect" title="Minerals">minerals</a> producer and is ranked among Europe's leading <a href="/wiki/Copper" title="Copper">copper</a> producers. The nation is also a notable producer of <a href="/wiki/Tin" title="Tin">tin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tungsten" title="Tungsten">tungsten</a> and <a href="/wiki/Uranium" title="Uranium">uranium</a>. However, the country lacks the potential to conduct <a href="/wiki/Hydrocarbon_exploration" title="Hydrocarbon exploration">hydrocarbon exploration</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aluminium" title="Aluminium">aluminium</a>, a limitation that has hindered the development of Portugal's <a href="/wiki/Mining_in_Portugal" title="Mining in Portugal">mining</a> and <a href="/wiki/Metallurgy" title="Metallurgy">metallurgy</a> sectors. Although the country has vast iron and coal reserves – mainly in the north – after the 1974 revolution and the consequent <a href="/wiki/Economic_globalization" title="Economic globalization">economic globalization</a>, low competitiveness forced a decrease in the extraction activity for these minerals. The <a href="/wiki/Panasqueira" title="Panasqueira">Panasqueira</a> and <a href="/wiki/Neves-Corvo_mine" title="Neves-Corvo mine">Neves-Corvo mines</a> are among the most recognized Portuguese mines that are still in operation.<sup id="cite_ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230">&#91;226&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Portugal is rich in its <a href="/wiki/Lithium" title="Lithium">lithium</a> subsoil, which is especially concentrated in the districts of <a href="/wiki/Guarda_District" title="Guarda District">Guarda</a>, <a href="/wiki/Viseu" title="Viseu">Viseu</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vila_Real" title="Vila Real">Vila Real</a> and <a href="/wiki/Viana_do_Castelo" title="Viana do Castelo">Viana do Castelo</a>, while most of the country's lithium comes from the Gonçalo aplite-pegmatite field. The largest <a href="/wiki/Lithium" title="Lithium">lithium</a> mine in Europe is operated by Grupo Mota, Felmica, in the Guarda region, which is estimated to have reserves for 30 years of production. It has five more deposits in its possession.<sup id="cite_ref-231" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-231">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-232" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-232">&#91;228&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-233" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-233">&#91;229&#93;</a></sup> Savannah Resources in May 2018 announced a 52% increase in the estimated lithium resources at the Mina do Barroso Lithium Project in northern Portugal, saying the country could become the first European supplier of <a href="/wiki/Spodumene" title="Spodumene">spodumene</a>, a lithium-bearing mineral.<sup id="cite_ref-234" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-234">&#91;230&#93;</a></sup> The company said the estimated mineral resources at the mine now stood at 14 million tonnes. Lithium prices have risen in expectation of growing demand for the mineral, which is used in batteries for electric vehicles and for storing electricity from the power grid. Europe consumes more than 20 per cent of the global supply of battery-grade lithium but currently has to import all its supplies of the mineral.<sup id="cite_ref-235" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-235">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>W Resources stated in 2018 that it had started a new drilling campaign at its São Martinho <a href="/wiki/Gold" title="Gold">gold</a> project in Portugal. The so-called <a href="/wiki/Reverse_circulation_drilling" class="mw-redirect" title="Reverse circulation drilling">reverse circulation drilling</a> programme included 15 holes with around 2,000 metres (6,600&#160;ft) of total drilling. The objective is to extend resources by integrating the data from 2016 drilling results with the expansion expected with the ongoing campaign.<sup id="cite_ref-236" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-236">&#91;232&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-237" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-237">&#91;233&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-238" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-238">&#91;234&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Secondary_sector">Secondary sector</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=32" title="Edit section: Secondary sector">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Veh%C3%ADculos_en_el_puerto_de_Set%C3%BAbal,_Portugal,_2019-05-24,_DD_01.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Veh%C3%ADculos_en_el_puerto_de_Set%C3%BAbal%2C_Portugal%2C_2019-05-24%2C_DD_01.jpg/220px-Veh%C3%ADculos_en_el_puerto_de_Set%C3%BAbal%2C_Portugal%2C_2019-05-24%2C_DD_01.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="121" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Veh%C3%ADculos_en_el_puerto_de_Set%C3%BAbal%2C_Portugal%2C_2019-05-24%2C_DD_01.jpg/330px-Veh%C3%ADculos_en_el_puerto_de_Set%C3%BAbal%2C_Portugal%2C_2019-05-24%2C_DD_01.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Veh%C3%ADculos_en_el_puerto_de_Set%C3%BAbal%2C_Portugal%2C_2019-05-24%2C_DD_01.jpg/440px-Veh%C3%ADculos_en_el_puerto_de_Set%C3%BAbal%2C_Portugal%2C_2019-05-24%2C_DD_01.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5633" data-file-height="3109" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Volkswagen_Autoeuropa" title="Volkswagen Autoeuropa">Volkswagen Autoeuropa</a> cars in the Port of Setúbal.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Industry is diversified, ranging from <a href="/wiki/Automotive_industry" title="Automotive industry">automotive</a> (<a href="/wiki/Volkswagen_Autoeuropa" title="Volkswagen Autoeuropa">Volkswagen Autoeuropa</a> and <a href="/wiki/Peugeot_Citro%C3%ABn" class="mw-redirect" title="Peugeot Citroën">Peugeot Citroën</a>) and <a href="/wiki/Bicycle" title="Bicycle">bicycles</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239">&#91;235&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Aerospace_industry" class="mw-redirect" title="Aerospace industry">aerospace</a> (<a href="/wiki/Embraer" title="Embraer">Embraer</a> and <a href="/wiki/OGMA" title="OGMA">OGMA</a>), <a href="/wiki/Electronics_industry" title="Electronics industry">electronics</a> and <a href="/wiki/Textile_industry" title="Textile industry">textiles</a>, to <a href="/wiki/Food_industry" title="Food industry">food</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chemical_industry" title="Chemical industry">chemicals</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cement" title="Cement">cement</a> and <a href="/wiki/Wood_pulp" class="mw-redirect" title="Wood pulp">wood pulp</a>. Volkswagen Group's <a href="/wiki/AutoEuropa" class="mw-redirect" title="AutoEuropa">AutoEuropa</a> motor vehicle assembly plant in <a href="/wiki/Palmela" title="Palmela">Palmela</a> is among the largest <a href="/wiki/Foreign_direct_investment" title="Foreign direct investment">foreign direct investment</a> projects in Portugal.
Modern non-traditional technology-based industries, such as <a href="/wiki/Aerospace" title="Aerospace">aerospace</a>, <a href="/wiki/Biotechnology" title="Biotechnology">biotechnology</a> and <a href="/wiki/Information_technology" title="Information technology">information technology</a>, have been developed in several locations across the country. <a href="/wiki/Alverca" class="mw-redirect" title="Alverca">Alverca</a>, <a href="/wiki/%C3%89vora" title="Évora">Évora</a><sup id="cite_ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240">&#91;236&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Ponte_de_Sor" title="Ponte de Sor">Ponte de Sor</a> are the main centres of the Portuguese aerospace industry, which is led by Brazil-based company Embraer and the Portuguese company OGMA. Following the turn of the 21st century, many major biotechnology and information technology industries have been founded, and are concentrated in the metropolitan areas of <a href="/wiki/Lisbon_metropolitan_area" title="Lisbon metropolitan area">Lisbon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Porto_Metropolitan_Area" class="mw-redirect" title="Porto Metropolitan Area">Porto</a>, <a href="/wiki/Braga" title="Braga">Braga</a>, <a href="/wiki/Coimbra" title="Coimbra">Coimbra</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aveiro,_Portugal" title="Aveiro, Portugal">Aveiro</a>.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2013)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Tertiary_sector">Tertiary sector</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=33" title="Edit section: Tertiary sector">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Tourism_in_Portugal" title="Tourism in Portugal">Tourism in Portugal</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tleft"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:224px;max-width:224px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:DSC_3294_(3784718431).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/DSC_3294_%283784718431%29.jpg/220px-DSC_3294_%283784718431%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/DSC_3294_%283784718431%29.jpg/330px-DSC_3294_%283784718431%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/DSC_3294_%283784718431%29.jpg/440px-DSC_3294_%283784718431%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="849" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption">A view of <a href="/wiki/Nazar%C3%A9,_Portugal" title="Nazaré, Portugal">Nazaré</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Estremadura_Province_(historical)" title="Estremadura Province (historical)">Estremadura</a>.</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Praia_da_Marinha_(35518737040).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Praia_da_Marinha_%2835518737040%29.jpg/220px-Praia_da_Marinha_%2835518737040%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Praia_da_Marinha_%2835518737040%29.jpg/330px-Praia_da_Marinha_%2835518737040%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Praia_da_Marinha_%2835518737040%29.jpg/440px-Praia_da_Marinha_%2835518737040%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1920" data-file-height="1280" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption">Portuguese coast in <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a>.</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>The banking and insurance sectors performed well until the <a href="/wiki/Financial_crisis_of_2007%E2%80%932008" class="mw-redirect" title="Financial crisis of 2007–2008">financial crisis of 2007–2008</a>, and this partly reflected a rapid deepening of the market in Portugal. While sensitive to various types of market and underwriting <a href="/wiki/Risk" title="Risk">risks</a>, it has been estimated that overall both the life and non-life sectors will be able to withstand a number of severe shocks, even though the impact on individual insurers varies widely.<sup id="cite_ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Travel and <a href="/wiki/Tourism_in_Portugal" title="Tourism in Portugal">tourism</a> continue to be extremely important for Portugal. It has been necessary for the country to focus upon its niche attractions, such as health, nature and rural tourism, to stay ahead of its competitors.<sup id="cite_ref-242" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-242">&#91;238&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Portugal is among the top 20 most-visited countries in the world, receiving an average of 20,000,000 foreign tourists each year.<sup id="cite_ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup> In 2014, Portugal was elected <i>The Best European Country</i> by <a href="/wiki/USA_Today" title="USA Today">USA Today</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2017, Portugal was elected both <i>Europe's Leading Destination</i><sup id="cite_ref-245" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-245">&#91;241&#93;</a></sup> and in 2018 and 2019, <i>World's Leading Destination</i><sup id="cite_ref-246" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-246">&#91;242&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Tourist hotspots in Portugal are: <a href="/wiki/Lisbon" title="Lisbon">Lisbon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cascais" title="Cascais">Cascais</a>, <a href="/wiki/F%C3%A1tima,_Portugal" title="Fátima, Portugal">Fatima</a>, <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a>, <a href="/wiki/Madeira" title="Madeira">Madeira</a>, <a href="/wiki/Porto" title="Porto">Porto</a> and <a href="/wiki/Coimbra" title="Coimbra">Coimbra</a>. Lisbon attracts the sixteenth-most tourists among European cities<sup id="cite_ref-247" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-247">&#91;243&#93;</a></sup> (with seven million tourists occupying the city's hotels in 2006).<sup id="cite_ref-248" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-248">&#91;244&#93;</a></sup> Notable luxury destinations include the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Riviera" title="Portuguese Riviera">Portuguese Riviera</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Comporta" title="Comporta">Comporta Coast</a>.
</p><p>Also, between 5–6 million religious pilgrims visit <a href="/wiki/F%C3%A1tima,_Portugal" title="Fátima, Portugal">Fatima</a> each year, where apparitions of the Virgin Mary to three shepherd children allegedly took place in 1917. The <a href="/wiki/Sanctuary_of_F%C3%A1tima" title="Sanctuary of Fátima">Sanctuary of Our Lady of Fatima</a> is one of the largest Roman Catholic shrines in the world. The Portuguese government continues to promote and develop new tourist destinations, such as the <a href="/wiki/Douro" title="Douro">Douro Valley</a>, the island of <a href="/wiki/Porto_Santo_Island" title="Porto Santo Island">Porto Santo</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Alentejo" title="Alentejo">Alentejo</a>. The legend of the <a href="/wiki/Rooster_of_Barcelos" title="Rooster of Barcelos">Rooster of Barcelos</a> tells the story of a dead rooster's miraculous intervention in proving the innocence of a man who had been falsely accused and sentenced to death. The story is associated with the 17th-century <a href="/wiki/Calvary_(sculpture)" class="mw-redirect" title="Calvary (sculpture)">calvary</a> that is part of the collection of the Archaeological Museum located in Paço dos Condes, a gothic-style palace in <a href="/wiki/Barcelos,_Portugal" title="Barcelos, Portugal">Barcelos</a>, a city in northwest Portugal. The <a href="/wiki/Rooster_of_Barcelos" title="Rooster of Barcelos">Rooster of Barcelos</a> is bought by thousands of tourists as a national <a href="/wiki/Souvenir" title="Souvenir">souvenir</a>. On 30 November 2016, the United Nations added the Portuguese <span title="Portuguese-language text"><i lang="pt">Bisalhães</i></span> tradition of making black pottery to the UNESCO Heritage Protection List.<sup id="cite_ref-249" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-249">&#91;245&#93;</a></sup>
On 7 December 2017, the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a> added the <i>Bonecos de Estremoz</i> – <i>Toys of <a href="/wiki/Estremoz" title="Estremoz">Estremoz</a></i> tradition as an <a href="/wiki/UNESCO_Intangible_Cultural_Heritage_Lists" title="UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists">UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage</a> of Humankind.<sup id="cite_ref-250" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-250">&#91;246&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Quaternary_sector">Quaternary sector</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=34" title="Edit section: Quaternary sector">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Science_and_technology_in_Portugal" title="Science and technology in Portugal">Science and technology in Portugal</a></div>
<p>Scientific and technological research activities in Portugal are mainly conducted within a network of <a href="/wiki/R%26D" class="mw-redirect" title="R&amp;D">R&amp;D</a> units belonging to <a href="/wiki/List_of_universities_in_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="List of universities in Portugal">public universities</a> and state-managed autonomous research institutions like the <a href="/wiki/Instituto_Nacional_de_Engenharia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o" title="Instituto Nacional de Engenharia, Tecnologia e Inovação">INETI&#160;– Instituto Nacional de Engenharia, Tecnologia e Inovação</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Instituto_Nacional_dos_Recursos_Biol%C3%B3gicos" title="Instituto Nacional dos Recursos Biológicos">INRB&#160;– Instituto Nacional dos Recursos Biológicos</a>. The funding and management of this research system is mainly conducted under the authority of the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Science,_Technology_and_Higher_Education" title="Ministry of Science, Technology and Higher Education">Ministry of Science, Technology and Higher Education</a> (MCTES) and the MCTES's <a href="/wiki/Funda%C3%A7%C3%A3o_para_a_Ci%C3%AAncia_e_Tecnologia" title="Fundação para a Ciência e Tecnologia">Fundação para a Ciência e Tecnologia</a> (FCT).
</p>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:224px;max-width:224px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Fotooal.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Fotooal.jpg/220px-Fotooal.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Fotooal.jpg/330px-Fotooal.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Fotooal.jpg/440px-Fotooal.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3442" data-file-height="2592" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption">The <i><a href="/wiki/Lisbon_Astronomical_Observatory" title="Lisbon Astronomical Observatory">Observatório Astronómico de Lisboa</a></i> is Portugal's oldest (1878) astronomical observatory.</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Cultural_Center_Lisbon_Portugal_(52073738550).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Cultural_Center_Lisbon_Portugal_%2852073738550%29.jpg/220px-Cultural_Center_Lisbon_Portugal_%2852073738550%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Cultural_Center_Lisbon_Portugal_%2852073738550%29.jpg/330px-Cultural_Center_Lisbon_Portugal_%2852073738550%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Cultural_Center_Lisbon_Portugal_%2852073738550%29.jpg/440px-Cultural_Center_Lisbon_Portugal_%2852073738550%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5184" data-file-height="3888" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Champalimaud_Foundation" title="Champalimaud Foundation">Champalimaud Foundation</a>, one of the leading research centers for <a href="/wiki/Neuroscience" title="Neuroscience">neuroscience</a> and <a href="/wiki/Oncology" title="Oncology">oncology</a> in the world.</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:TagusPark.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/TagusPark.JPG/220px-TagusPark.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/TagusPark.JPG/330px-TagusPark.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/TagusPark.JPG/440px-TagusPark.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2272" data-file-height="1704" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption">View of <a href="/wiki/Science_and_technology_park" class="mw-redirect" title="Science and technology park">science and technology park</a> <a href="/wiki/Taguspark" title="Taguspark">Taguspark</a>.</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>The largest R&amp;D units of the public universities by volume of research grants and peer-reviewed publications, include <a href="/wiki/Biosciences" class="mw-redirect" title="Biosciences">biosciences</a> research institutions like the <a href="/wiki/Instituto_de_Medicina_Molecular" title="Instituto de Medicina Molecular">Instituto de Medicina Molecular</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Centre_for_Neuroscience_and_Cell_Biology" title="Centre for Neuroscience and Cell Biology">Centre for Neuroscience and Cell Biology</a>, the <a href="/wiki/IPATIMUP" class="mw-redirect" title="IPATIMUP">IPATIMUP</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Instituto_de_Biologia_Molecular_e_Celular" title="Instituto de Biologia Molecular e Celular">Instituto de Biologia Molecular e Celular</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Abel_Salazar_Biomedical_Sciences_Institute" title="Abel Salazar Biomedical Sciences Institute">Abel Salazar Biomedical Sciences Institute</a>.
</p><p>Among the largest non-state-run research institutions in Portugal are the <a href="/wiki/Instituto_Gulbenkian_de_Ci%C3%AAncia" title="Instituto Gulbenkian de Ciência">Instituto Gulbenkian de Ciência</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Champalimaud_Foundation" title="Champalimaud Foundation">Champalimaud Foundation</a>, a neuroscience and oncology research centre which awards every year one of the highest monetary prizes of any science prize in the world. A number of both national and multinational high-tech and industrial companies, are also responsible for research and development projects. One of the oldest learned societies of Portugal is the <a href="/wiki/Sciences_Academy_of_Lisbon" class="mw-redirect" title="Sciences Academy of Lisbon">Sciences Academy of Lisbon</a>, founded in 1779.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Iberian_peninsula" class="mw-redirect" title="Iberian peninsula">Iberian</a> bilateral state-supported research efforts include the <a href="/wiki/International_Iberian_Nanotechnology_Laboratory" title="International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory">International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Ibercivis" title="Ibercivis">Ibercivis</a> <a href="/wiki/Distributed_computing" title="Distributed computing">distributed computing</a> platform, which are joint research programmes of both Portugal and Spain. Portugal is a member of several pan-European scientific organizations. These include the <a href="/wiki/European_Space_Agency" title="European Space Agency">European Space Agency</a> (ESA), the <a href="/wiki/European_Laboratory_for_Particle_Physics" class="mw-redirect" title="European Laboratory for Particle Physics">European Laboratory for Particle Physics</a> (CERN), <a href="/wiki/ITER" title="ITER">ITER</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/European_Southern_Observatory" title="European Southern Observatory">European Southern Observatory</a> (ESO).
</p><p>Portugal has the largest <a href="/wiki/Aquarium" title="Aquarium">aquarium</a> in Europe, the <a href="/wiki/Lisbon_Oceanarium" title="Lisbon Oceanarium">Lisbon Oceanarium</a>, and the Portuguese have several other notable organizations focused on science-related exhibits and divulgation, like the state agency <i>Ciência Viva</i>, a programme of the Portuguese Ministry of Science and Technology to the promotion of a scientific and technological culture among the Portuguese population,<sup id="cite_ref-251" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-251">&#91;247&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Science_Museum_of_the_University_of_Coimbra" title="Science Museum of the University of Coimbra">Science Museum of the University of Coimbra</a>, the <a href="/wiki/List_of_natural_history_museums#Portugal" title="List of natural history museums">National Museum of Natural History</a> at the University of Lisbon, and the <a href="/wiki/Visionarium_(Portugal)" title="Visionarium (Portugal)">Visionarium</a>.
</p><p>With the emergence and growth of several <a href="/wiki/Science_park" title="Science park">science parks</a> throughout the world that helped create many thousands of scientific, technological and knowledge-based businesses, Portugal started to develop several<sup id="cite_ref-252" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-252">&#91;248&#93;</a></sup> science parks across the country. These include the <a href="/wiki/Taguspark" title="Taguspark">Taguspark</a> (in <a href="/wiki/Oeiras_Municipality,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Oeiras Municipality, Portugal">Oeiras</a>), the <a href="/wiki/Coimbra_iParque" title="Coimbra iParque">Coimbra iParque</a> (in <a href="/wiki/Coimbra" title="Coimbra">Coimbra</a>), the <a href="/wiki/Biocant" title="Biocant">biocant</a> (in <a href="/wiki/Cantanhede_Municipality" class="mw-redirect" title="Cantanhede Municipality">Cantanhede</a>), the <a href="/wiki/Madeira_Tecnopolo" title="Madeira Tecnopolo">Madeira Tecnopolo</a><sup id="cite_ref-253" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-253">&#91;249&#93;</a></sup> (in <a href="/wiki/Funchal" title="Funchal">Funchal</a>), <a href="/wiki/Sines_Tecnopolo" title="Sines Tecnopolo">Sines Tecnopolo</a><sup id="cite_ref-254" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-254">&#91;250&#93;</a></sup> (in <a href="/wiki/Sines,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Sines, Portugal">Sines</a>), Tecmaia<sup id="cite_ref-255" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-255">&#91;251&#93;</a></sup> (in <a href="/wiki/Maia_Municipality" class="mw-redirect" title="Maia Municipality">Maia</a>) and <a href="/wiki/Parkurbis" title="Parkurbis">Parkurbis</a><sup id="cite_ref-256" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-256">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup> (in <a href="/wiki/Covilh%C3%A3" title="Covilhã">Covilhã</a>). Companies locate in the Portuguese science parks to take advantage of a variety of services ranging from financial and legal advice through to marketing and technological support.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Egas_Moniz" class="mw-redirect" title="Egas Moniz">Egas Moniz</a>, a Portuguese physician who developed the <a href="/wiki/Cerebral_angiography" title="Cerebral angiography">cerebral angiography</a> and <a href="/wiki/Leucotomy" class="mw-redirect" title="Leucotomy">leucotomy</a>, received in 1949 the <a href="/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine" title="Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine">Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine</a>&#160;– he is the first Portuguese recipient of a <a href="/wiki/Nobel_Prize" title="Nobel Prize">Nobel Prize</a> and the only in the sciences.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/European_Innovation_Scoreboard" class="mw-redirect" title="European Innovation Scoreboard">European Innovation Scoreboard</a> 2011, placed Portugal-based innovation in the 15th position, with an impressive increase in innovation expenditure and output.<sup id="cite_ref-257" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-257">&#91;253&#93;</a></sup> Portugal was ranked 32nd in the <a href="/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index" title="Global Innovation Index">Global Innovation Index</a> in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-258" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-258">&#91;254&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Transport">Transport</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=35" title="Edit section: Transport">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Transport_in_Portugal" title="Transport in Portugal">Transport in Portugal</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:224px;max-width:224px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Vasco_da_Gama_Bridge_03.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Vasco_da_Gama_Bridge_03.JPG/220px-Vasco_da_Gama_Bridge_03.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Vasco_da_Gama_Bridge_03.JPG/330px-Vasco_da_Gama_Bridge_03.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Vasco_da_Gama_Bridge_03.JPG/440px-Vasco_da_Gama_Bridge_03.JPG 2x" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="683" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Vasco_da_Gama_Bridge" title="Vasco da Gama Bridge">Vasco da Gama Bridge</a> is the longest bridge in the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">EU</a>.</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Lisbon_Oriente_Station_(42264380264).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt=""
