class="trow" style="display:flex"><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Jer%C3%B3nimos_Monastery" title="Jerónimos Monastery">Jerónimos Monastery</a> (top) and <a href="/wiki/Bel%C3%A9m_Tower" title="Belém Tower">Belém Tower</a> (middle) are <a href="/wiki/Masterpiece" title="Masterpiece">magna opera</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Manueline_style" class="mw-redirect" title="Manueline style">Manueline style</a> and symbols of Portuguese nationhood. <a href="/wiki/Casa_da_M%C3%BAsica" title="Casa da Música">Casa da Música</a> (bottom) is an example of post-Millennium architecture.</div></div></div></div>
<p>Traditional architecture is distinctive and include the <a href="/wiki/Manueline" title="Manueline">Manueline</a>, also known as Portuguese late <a href="/wiki/Gothic_architecture" title="Gothic architecture">Gothic</a> a sumptuous, composite Portuguese style of architectural ornamentation of the first decades of the 16th century, followed by <a href="/wiki/Pombaline_style" title="Pombaline style">Pombaline style</a> of the 18th century. A 20th-century interpretation of traditional architecture, <a href="/wiki/Soft_Portuguese_style" class="mw-redirect" title="Soft Portuguese style">Soft Portuguese style</a>, appears extensively in major cities, especially Lisbon. Modern Portugal has given the world renowned architects like <a href="/wiki/Eduardo_Souto_de_Moura" title="Eduardo Souto de Moura">Eduardo Souto de Moura</a>, <a href="/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Siza_Vieira" title="Álvaro Siza Vieira">Álvaro Siza Vieira</a> (both <a href="/wiki/Pritzker_Prize" class="mw-redirect" title="Pritzker Prize">Pritzker Prize</a> winners) and <a href="/wiki/Gon%C3%A7alo_Byrne" title="Gonçalo Byrne">Gonçalo Byrne</a>. In Portugal <a href="/wiki/Tom%C3%A1s_Taveira" title="Tomás Taveira">Tomás Taveira</a> is also noteworthy, particularly for stadium design.<sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-324" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-324">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Azulejo" title="Azulejo">azulejo</a> is a mainstream, typical element among Portugal's traditional building materials and construction techniques.<sup id="cite_ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-326" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-326">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cinema">Cinema</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=46" title="Edit section: Cinema">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Portugal" title="Cinema of Portugal">Cinema of Portugal</a></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Portugal" title="Cinema of Portugal">Portuguese cinema</a> has a long tradition, reaching back to the birth of the medium in the late 19th century.
<a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Lopes_Ribeiro" title="António Lopes Ribeiro">António Lopes Ribeiro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Reis" title="António Reis">António Reis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pedro_Costa" title="Pedro Costa">Pedro Costa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Manoel_de_Oliveira" title="Manoel de Oliveira">Manoel de Oliveira</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jo%C3%A3o_C%C3%A9sar_Monteiro" title="João César Monteiro">João César Monteiro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Fonseca_e_Costa" title="José Fonseca e Costa">José Fonseca e Costa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Edgar_P%C3%AAra" title="Edgar Pêra">Edgar Pêra</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio-Pedro_Vasconcelos" title="António-Pedro Vasconcelos">António-Pedro Vasconcelos</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fernando_Lopes_(filmmaker)" title="Fernando Lopes (filmmaker)">Fernando Lopes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jo%C3%A3o_Botelho" title="João Botelho">João Botelho</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jo%C3%A3o_M%C3%A1rio_Grilo" title="João Mário Grilo">João Mário Grilo</a> and <a href="/wiki/Leonel_Vieira" title="Leonel Vieira">Leonel Vieira</a>, are among those that gained notability. Noted Portuguese film actors include <a href="/wiki/Joaquim_de_Almeida" title="Joaquim de Almeida">Joaquim de Almeida</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nuno_Lopes" title="Nuno Lopes">Nuno Lopes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Daniela_Ruah" title="Daniela Ruah">Daniela Ruah</a>, <a href="/wiki/Maria_de_Medeiros" title="Maria de Medeiros">Maria de Medeiros</a>, <a href="/wiki/Diogo_Infante" title="Diogo Infante">Diogo Infante</a>, <a href="/wiki/Soraia_Chaves" title="Soraia Chaves">Soraia Chaves</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ribeirinho" title="Ribeirinho">Ribeirinho</a>, <a href="/wiki/L%C3%BAcia_Moniz" title="Lúcia Moniz">Lúcia Moniz</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Diogo_Morgado" title="Diogo Morgado">Diogo Morgado</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cuisine">Cuisine</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=47" title="Edit section: Cuisine">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_cuisine" title="Portuguese cuisine">Portuguese cuisine</a> and <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_wine" title="Portuguese wine">Portuguese wine</a></div>
<p>Portuguese cuisine is very diverse. Different regions have their own traditional dishes. The Portuguese have a culture of good food, and throughout the country there are myriad good restaurants and typical small tasquinhas. The Portuguese consume a lot of dry <a href="/wiki/Cod" title="Cod">cod</a> (<i><a href="/wiki/Bacalhau" title="Bacalhau">bacalhau</a></i> in Portuguese), for which there are hundreds of <a href="/wiki/Bacalhau#Bacalhau_dishes" title="Bacalhau">recipes</a> ranging from <a href="/wiki/Bacalhau_%C3%A0_Br%C3%A1s" title="Bacalhau à Brás">bacalhau à Brás</a> to <a href="/wiki/Bacalhau_%C3%A0_Gomes_de_S%C3%A1" title="Bacalhau à Gomes de Sá">bacalhau à Gomes de Sá</a> among many other popular examples such as <a href="/wiki/Bacalhau_com_natas" title="Bacalhau com natas">bacalhau com natas</a>. Two other popular fish recipes are grilled <a href="/wiki/Sardines" class="mw-redirect" title="Sardines">sardines</a> and <a href="/wiki/Caldeirada" title="Caldeirada">caldeirada</a>, a tomato-based <a href="/wiki/Stew" title="Stew">stew</a> that can be made from several types of fish or molluscs with a mix of onion, garlic, bay leaf, potatoes, tomatoes, peppers, parsley or coriander. 
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cozidoaportuguesa2.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Cozidoaportuguesa2.JPG/220px-Cozidoaportuguesa2.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="174" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Cozidoaportuguesa2.JPG/330px-Cozidoaportuguesa2.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Cozidoaportuguesa2.JPG/440px-Cozidoaportuguesa2.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2888" data-file-height="2287" /></a><figcaption>The stewed meats and vegetables of <a href="/wiki/Cozido_%C3%A0_portuguesa" title="Cozido à portuguesa">cozido à portuguesa</a> and its accompanying rice and beans.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Typical Portuguese meat recipes made out of the customary beef, pork, chicken, goat, lamb or duck meat, include <i><a href="/wiki/Cozido_%C3%A0_portuguesa" title="Cozido à portuguesa">cozido à portuguesa</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Feijoada" title="Feijoada">feijoada</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Frango_de_churrasco" class="mw-redirect" title="Frango de churrasco">frango de churrasco</a></i>, <i>leitão</i> (roast <a href="/wiki/Suckling_pig" title="Suckling pig">suckling pig</a>), <i><a href="/wiki/Chanfana" title="Chanfana">chanfana</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Carne_de_porco_%C3%A0_alentejana" title="Carne de porco à alentejana">carne de porco à alentejana</a></i>. A very popular northern dish is <a href="/wiki/Dobrada_(food)" title="Dobrada (food)">dobrada</a>, a tripe with white beans and carrots stew, often served with steamed white rice, and the related <a href="/wiki/Tripas_%C3%A0_moda_do_Porto" title="Tripas à moda do Porto">tripas à moda do Porto</a> which is a traditional dish from Porto. <a href="/wiki/Peri-peri" title="Peri-peri">Peri-peri</a> chicken is a spicy charcoal chicken dish served with fries or rice and vegetables, a favourite throughout Portugal, but most common in the <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a> region.
</p><p>Typical fast food dishes include the <a href="/wiki/Francesinha" title="Francesinha">Francesinha</a> (Frenchie) from Porto and <i>bifanas</i> (grilled pork) or <i>prego</i> (grilled beef) <a href="/wiki/Sandwich" title="Sandwich">sandwiches</a>, which are well known around the country.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:MargaretCafe_PasteisDeNata.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/MargaretCafe_PasteisDeNata.JPG/220px-MargaretCafe_PasteisDeNata.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/MargaretCafe_PasteisDeNata.JPG/330px-MargaretCafe_PasteisDeNata.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/MargaretCafe_PasteisDeNata.JPG/440px-MargaretCafe_PasteisDeNata.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2400" data-file-height="1600" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Pastel_de_nata" title="Pastel de nata">Pastéis de Nata</a> in Lisbon</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Portuguese art of <a href="/wiki/Pastry" title="Pastry">pastry</a> has its origins in the many <a href="/wiki/Medieval" class="mw-redirect" title="Medieval">medieval</a> Catholic monasteries spread widely across the country. These monasteries, using very few ingredients (mostly eggs, <a href="/wiki/Vanilla" title="Vanilla">vanilla</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cinnamon" title="Cinnamon">cinnamon</a>, flour, almonds and some liqueurs), managed to create a spectacular wide range of different pastries, of which <a href="/wiki/Past%C3%A9is_de_Bel%C3%A9m" class="mw-redirect" title="Pastéis de Belém">pastéis de Belém</a> (or <i>pastéis de nata</i>) originally from Lisbon, <a href="/wiki/Pastel_de_Tent%C3%BAgal" title="Pastel de Tentúgal">pastéis de Tentúgal</a> from the <a href="/wiki/Baixo_Mondego" title="Baixo Mondego">Baixo Mondego valley</a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Ovos_moles" title="Ovos moles">ovos moles</a></i> from <a href="/wiki/Aveiro,_Portugal" title="Aveiro, Portugal">Aveiro</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tigelada" title="Tigelada">tigeladas</a> from <a href="/wiki/Abrantes" title="Abrantes">Abrantes</a>, are examples.
</p><p>Portuguese wines have enjoyed international recognition since the times of the Romans, who associated Portugal with their god <a href="/wiki/Dionysus" title="Dionysus">Bacchus</a>. Today, the country is known by wine lovers and its wines have won several international prizes. Some of the best Portuguese wines are <a href="/wiki/Vinho_Verde" title="Vinho Verde">Vinho Verde</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vinho_Alvarinho" class="mw-redirect" title="Vinho Alvarinho">Vinho Alvarinho</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vinho_do_Douro" class="mw-redirect" title="Vinho do Douro">Vinho do Douro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vinho_do_Alentejo" class="mw-redirect" title="Vinho do Alentejo">Vinho do Alentejo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vinho_do_D%C3%A3o" class="mw-redirect" title="Vinho do Dão">Vinho do Dão</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vinho_da_Bairrada" class="mw-redirect" title="Vinho da Bairrada">Vinho da Bairrada</a> and the sweet <a href="/wiki/Port_Wine" class="mw-redirect" title="Port Wine">Port Wine</a>, <a href="/wiki/Madeira_Wine" class="mw-redirect" title="Madeira Wine">Madeira Wine</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Moscatel" class="mw-redirect" title="Moscatel">Moscatel</a> from <a href="/wiki/Set%C3%BAbal" title="Setúbal">Setúbal</a> and <a href="/wiki/Favaios" title="Favaios">Favaios</a>. Port and Madeira are particularly appreciated in a wide range of places around the world.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Fashion_and_design">Fashion and design</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=48" title="Edit section: Fashion and design">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:They_can_make_anything_out_of_cork_in_Portugal!_(33974132358).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/They_can_make_anything_out_of_cork_in_Portugal%21_%2833974132358%29.jpg/220px-They_can_make_anything_out_of_cork_in_Portugal%21_%2833974132358%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="138" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/They_can_make_anything_out_of_cork_in_Portugal%21_%2833974132358%29.jpg/330px-They_can_make_anything_out_of_cork_in_Portugal%21_%2833974132358%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/They_can_make_anything_out_of_cork_in_Portugal%21_%2833974132358%29.jpg/440px-They_can_make_anything_out_of_cork_in_Portugal%21_%2833974132358%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="2535" /></a><figcaption>Natural cork bags.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Industrialized, export-oriented <a href="/wiki/Fashion" title="Fashion">fashion</a> and <a href="/wiki/Design" title="Design">design</a> in <a href="/wiki/Clothing" title="Clothing">clothing</a>, <a href="/wiki/Footwear" title="Footwear">footwear</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kitchenware" title="Kitchenware">kitchenware</a> and <a href="/wiki/Furniture" title="Furniture">furniture</a> industries, was pioneered by fashion designers like Eduarda Abbondanza, Mário Matos Ribeiro, Ana Salazar, José António Tenente, João Tomé, Francisco Pontes or Manuela Gonçalves, as well as textile industry industrialists established in places like <a href="/wiki/Ave_(intermunicipal_community)" title="Ave (intermunicipal community)">Vale do Ave</a>, in clothing;<sup id="cite_ref-327" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-327">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup> several entrepreneurs of the Portuguese footwear industry;<sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Vista_Alegre_Atlantis" class="mw-redirect" title="Vista Alegre Atlantis">Vista Alegre Atlantis</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rafael_Bordalo_Pinheiro" title="Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro">Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Tableware" title="Tableware">tableware</a> and kitchenwear;<sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup> and businesspersons of the old-established furniture industry heavily concentrated in and around places such as <a href="/wiki/Pa%C3%A7os_de_Ferreira" title="Paços de Ferreira">Paços de Ferreira</a> and <a href="/wiki/Paredes,_Portugal" title="Paredes, Portugal">Paredes</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-331" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-331">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-332" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-332">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup> Corkware and other <a href="/wiki/Cork_(material)" title="Cork (material)">cork</a>-based products such as furniture, decorative items and floor and wall coatings, are also distinctive products found among typical designer creations of Portuguese origin.<sup id="cite_ref-333" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-333">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-335" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-335">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Filigree-portugal-deusa_ii-0000634.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Filigree-portugal-deusa_ii-0000634.jpg/220px-Filigree-portugal-deusa_ii-0000634.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Filigree-portugal-deusa_ii-0000634.jpg/330px-Filigree-portugal-deusa_ii-0000634.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Filigree-portugal-deusa_ii-0000634.jpg/440px-Filigree-portugal-deusa_ii-0000634.jpg 2x" data-file-width="645" data-file-height="430" /></a><figcaption>Typical Portuguese filigree heart shaped pendant, an iconic item in Portuguese fashion and design.</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Filigree" title="Filigree">Filigree</a> began to be produced in Portugal in the 8th century with the arrival of Arab migrants after the <a href="/wiki/Muslim_conquest_of_Iberia" class="mw-redirect" title="Muslim conquest of Iberia">Umayyad invasion of Iberian Peninsula</a>, who brought new patterns with them. With time, the peninsula began to produce different filigree patterns, but while in Spain the filigree jewellery-making tradition became less relevant, in Portugal it was perfected. After the 18th century, Portuguese Filigree already had its own distinctive imagery, motifs and shapes. Filigree from the 17th and 18th centuries became famous for their extraordinary complexity. Gold and silver filigree jewellery of delicate and artistic design is still made in considerable quantities throughout the country, particularly filigree hearts, which are iconic symbols of Portuguese jewellery-making.<sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-339" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-339">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Literature">Literature</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=49" title="Edit section: Literature">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_literature" title="Portuguese literature">Portuguese literature</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:312px;max-width:312px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:171px;max-width:171px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:188px;overflow:hidden"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Cam%C3%B5es,_por_Fern%C3%A3o_Gomes.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Cam%C3%B5es%2C_por_Fern%C3%A3o_Gomes.jpg/169px-Cam%C3%B5es%2C_por_Fern%C3%A3o_Gomes.jpg" decoding="async" width="169" height="189" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Cam%C3%B5es%2C_por_Fern%C3%A3o_Gomes.jpg/254px-Cam%C3%B5es%2C_por_Fern%C3%A3o_Gomes.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Cam%C3%B5es%2C_por_Fern%C3%A3o_Gomes.jpg/338px-Cam%C3%B5es%2C_por_Fern%C3%A3o_Gomes.jpg 2x" data-file-width="640" data-file-height="714" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Lu%C3%ADs_Vaz_de_Cam%C3%B5es" class="mw-redirect" title="Luís Vaz de Camões">Luís Vaz de Camões</a>, legendary poet of the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Renaissance" title="Portuguese Renaissance">Portuguese Renaissance</a></div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:137px;max-width:137px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:188px;overflow:hidden"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Pessoa_chapeu.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Pessoa_chapeu.jpg/135px-Pessoa_chapeu.jpg" decoding="async" width="135" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Pessoa_chapeu.jpg/203px-Pessoa_chapeu.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Pessoa_chapeu.jpg/270px-Pessoa_chapeu.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1084" data-file-height="1513" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Fernando_Pessoa" title="Fernando Pessoa">Fernando Pessoa</a>, prolific writer of 20th-century <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_language" title="Portuguese language">Portuguese</a> literature</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>Portuguese literature, one of the earliest Western literatures, developed through text as well as song. Until 1350, the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese-Galician" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese-Galician">Portuguese-Galician</a> <a href="/wiki/Troubadour" title="Troubadour">troubadours</a> spread their literary influence to most of the Iberian Peninsula,<sup id="cite_ref-340" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-340">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup> like King <a href="/wiki/Denis_of_Portugal" title="Denis of Portugal">D. Dinis</a> (1261–1325) who became famous for his poetry. Other kings would write and sponsor works of literature across Portuguese history, like <a href="/wiki/Ferdinand_I_of_Portugal" title="Ferdinand I of Portugal">D. Fernando</a> (1367–1383) who supported Pêro Menino in writing o <i>Livro da Falcoaria</i><sup id="cite_ref-:2_85-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-85">&#91;81&#93;</a></sup><i>.</i> Another notable name in Portuguese literature is <a href="/wiki/Gil_Vicente" title="Gil Vicente">Gil Vicente</a> (c. 1465–c. 1536), one of the founders of Portuguese dramatic traditions.
</p><p>Adventurer and poet <a href="/wiki/Lu%C3%ADs_de_Cam%C3%B5es" title="Luís de Camões">Luís de Camões</a> (c. 1524–1580) wrote the epic poem <i><a href="/wiki/Os_Lus%C3%ADadas" title="Os Lusíadas">Os Lusíadas</a></i> (<i>The Lusiads</i>), with <a href="/wiki/Virgil" title="Virgil">Virgil</a>'s <i><a href="/wiki/Aeneid" title="Aeneid">Aeneid</a></i> as his main influence.<sup id="cite_ref-WDL_341-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WDL-341">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup> Modern Portuguese poetry is rooted in neoclassic and contemporary styles, as exemplified by <a href="/wiki/Manuel_Maria_Barbosa_du_Bocage" title="Manuel Maria Barbosa du Bocage">Bocage</a> (1765–1805), <a href="/wiki/Antero_de_Quental" title="Antero de Quental">Antero de Quental</a> (1842–1891) and <a href="/wiki/Fernando_Pessoa" title="Fernando Pessoa">Fernando Pessoa</a> (1888–1935). Modern Portuguese literature is represented by authors such as <a href="/wiki/Almeida_Garrett" title="Almeida Garrett">Almeida Garrett</a>, <a href="/wiki/Camilo_Castelo_Branco" title="Camilo Castelo Branco">Camilo Castelo Branco</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Maria_de_E%C3%A7a_de_Queir%C3%B3s" class="mw-redirect" title="José Maria de Eça de Queirós">Eça de Queirós</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fernando_Pessoa" title="Fernando Pessoa">Fernando Pessoa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sophia_de_Mello_Breyner_Andresen" title="Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen">Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Lobo_Antunes" title="António Lobo Antunes">António Lobo Antunes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Miguel_Torga" title="Miguel Torga">Miguel Torga</a> and <a href="/wiki/Agustina_Bessa-Lu%C3%ADs" title="Agustina Bessa-Luís">Agustina Bessa-Luís</a>. Particularly popular and distinguished is <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Saramago" title="José Saramago">José Saramago</a>, recipient of the 1998 <a href="/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature" title="Nobel Prize in Literature">Nobel Prize in Literature</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Music">Music</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=50" title="Edit section: Music">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Music_of_Portugal" title="Music of Portugal">Music of Portugal</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Jose_malhoa_fado.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Jose_malhoa_fado.jpg/220px-Jose_malhoa_fado.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Jose_malhoa_fado.jpg/330px-Jose_malhoa_fado.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Jose_malhoa_fado.jpg/440px-Jose_malhoa_fado.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1116" data-file-height="952" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Fado" title="Fado">Fado</a>, depicted in this famous painting (c. 1910) by <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Malhoa" title="José Malhoa">José Malhoa</a>, is Portugal's traditional music.</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Music_of_Portugal" title="Music of Portugal">Portuguese music</a> encompasses a wide variety of genres. The traditional one is the Portuguese folk music which has deep roots in local customs, utilising instruments such as <a href="/wiki/Bagpipes" title="Bagpipes">bagpipes</a> (<i><a href="/wiki/Gaita_(bagpipe)" class="mw-redirect" title="Gaita (bagpipe)">gaita</a></i>), drums, flutes, tambourines, accordions and ukuleles (<i><a href="/wiki/Cavaquinho" title="Cavaquinho">cavaquinho</a></i>). Within Portuguese folk music is the renowned genre of <a href="/wiki/Fado" title="Fado">Fado</a>, a melancholic urban music originated in <a href="/wiki/Lisbon" title="Lisbon">Lisbon</a> in the 19th century, probably inside bohemian environments, usually associated with the <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_guitar" title="Portuguese guitar">Portuguese guitar</a> and <i>saudade</i>, or longing. <a href="/wiki/Coimbra_fado" class="mw-redirect" title="Coimbra fado">Coimbra fado</a>, a unique type of "<a href="/wiki/Troubadour" title="Troubadour">troubadour</a> serenading" fado, is also noteworthy. Internationally notable performers include <a href="/wiki/Am%C3%A1lia_Rodrigues" title="Amália Rodrigues">Amália Rodrigues</a>, <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Paredes" title="Carlos Paredes">Carlos Paredes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Afonso" title="José Afonso">José Afonso</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mariza" title="Mariza">Mariza</a>, <a href="/wiki/Carlos_do_Carmo" title="Carlos do Carmo">Carlos do Carmo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Chainho" title="António Chainho">António Chainho</a>, <a href="/wiki/M%C3%ADsia" title="Mísia">Mísia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dulce_Pontes" title="Dulce Pontes">Dulce Pontes</a> and <a href="/wiki/Madredeus" title="Madredeus">Madredeus</a>.
</p><p>In the classical music domain, Portugal is represented by names as the pianists <a href="/wiki/Artur_Pizarro" title="Artur Pizarro">Artur Pizarro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Maria_Jo%C3%A3o_Pires" title="Maria João Pires">Maria João Pires</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sequeira_Costa" title="Sequeira Costa">Sequeira Costa</a>, the violinists <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Damas" title="Carlos Damas">Carlos Damas</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gerardo_Ribeiro" title="Gerardo Ribeiro">Gerardo Ribeiro</a> and in the past by the great cellist <a href="/wiki/Guilhermina_Suggia" title="Guilhermina Suggia">Guilhermina Suggia</a>. Notable composers include <a href="/wiki/Marcos_Portugal" title="Marcos Portugal">Marcos Portugal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Vianna_da_Motta" title="José Vianna da Motta">José Vianna da Motta</a>, <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Seixas" title="Carlos Seixas">Carlos Seixas</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jo%C3%A3o_Domingos_Bomtempo" title="João Domingos Bomtempo">João Domingos Bomtempo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jo%C3%A3o_de_Sousa_Carvalho" title="João de Sousa Carvalho">João de Sousa Carvalho</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lu%C3%ADs_de_Freitas_Branco" title="Luís de Freitas Branco">Luís de Freitas Branco</a> and his student <a href="/wiki/Joly_Braga_Santos" title="Joly Braga Santos">Joly Braga Santos</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fernando_Lopes-Gra%C3%A7a" title="Fernando Lopes-Graça">Fernando Lopes-Graça</a>, <a href="/wiki/Emmanuel_Nunes" title="Emmanuel Nunes">Emmanuel Nunes</a> and <a href="/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9rgio_Azevedo&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Sérgio Azevedo (page does not exist)">Sérgio Azevedo</a>. Similarly, contemporary composers such as Nuno Malo and Miguel d'Oliveira have achieved some international success writing.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:AmaliaRodrigues1969_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/AmaliaRodrigues1969_%28cropped%29.jpg/220px-AmaliaRodrigues1969_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="180" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/AmaliaRodrigues1969_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-AmaliaRodrigues1969_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/AmaliaRodrigues1969_%28cropped%29.jpg/440px-AmaliaRodrigues1969_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2363" data-file-height="1930" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Am%C3%A1lia_Rodrigues" title="Amália Rodrigues">Amália Rodrigues</a>, known as the <i>Queen of <a href="/wiki/Fado" title="Fado">Fado</a></i>, performing in 1969</figcaption></figure>
<p>In addition to <a href="/wiki/Folk_music" title="Folk music">Folk</a>, Fado and Classical music, other genres are present at Portugal like pop and other types of modern music, particularly from North America and the United Kingdom, as well as a wide range of Portuguese, Caribbean, Lusophone African and Brazilian artists and bands. Artists with international recognition include <a href="/wiki/Dulce_Pontes" title="Dulce Pontes">Dulce Pontes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Moonspell" title="Moonspell">Moonspell</a>, <a href="/wiki/Buraka_Som_Sistema" title="Buraka Som Sistema">Buraka Som Sistema</a>, <a href="/wiki/Blasted_Mechanism" title="Blasted Mechanism">Blasted Mechanism</a>, <a href="/wiki/David_Carreira" title="David Carreira">David Carreira</a> and <a href="/wiki/The_Gift_(band)" title="The Gift (band)">The Gift</a>, with the three latter being nominees for a <a href="/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award" class="mw-redirect" title="MTV Europe Music Award">MTV Europe Music Award</a>.
</p><p>Portugal has several summer music festivals, such as <i><a href="/wiki/Festival_Sudoeste" class="mw-redirect" title="Festival Sudoeste">Festival Sudoeste</a></i> in <a href="/wiki/Zambujeira_do_Mar" title="Zambujeira do Mar">Zambujeira do Mar</a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Festival_de_Paredes_de_Coura" class="mw-redirect" title="Festival de Paredes de Coura">Festival de Paredes de Coura</a></i> in <a href="/wiki/Paredes_de_Coura" title="Paredes de Coura">Paredes de Coura</a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Festival_Vilar_de_Mouros" class="mw-redirect" title="Festival Vilar de Mouros">Festival Vilar de Mouros</a></i> near <a href="/wiki/Caminha" title="Caminha">Caminha</a>, <a href="/wiki/Boom_Festival" title="Boom Festival">Boom Festival</a> in <a href="/wiki/Idanha-a-Nova_Municipality" class="mw-redirect" title="Idanha-a-Nova Municipality">Idanha-a-Nova Municipality</a>, <i><a href="/wiki/NOS_Alive" title="NOS Alive">NOS Alive</a></i>, <i>Sumol Summer Fest</i> in <a href="/wiki/Ericeira" title="Ericeira">Ericeira</a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Rock_in_Rio#Lisboa,_Portugal,_and_Madrid,_Spain" title="Rock in Rio">Rock in Rio Lisboa</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Super_Bock_Super_Rock" title="Super Bock Super Rock">Super Bock Super Rock</a></i> in <a href="/wiki/Greater_Lisbon" class="mw-redirect" title="Greater Lisbon">Greater Lisbon</a>. Out of the summer season, Portugal has a large number of festivals, designed more to an urban audience, like Flowfest or Hip Hop Porto. One of the largest international <a href="/wiki/Goa_trance" title="Goa trance">Goa trance</a> festivals takes place in central Portugal every two years, the Boom Festival, that is also the only festival in Portugal to win international awards: <a href="/wiki/European_Festival_Awards" title="European Festival Awards">European Festival Award</a> 2010 – Green'n'Clean Festival of the Year and the Greener Festival Award Outstanding 2008 and 2010. 
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Hives_Queima_Das_Fitas_Coimbra_2012_(23514791).jpeg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/The_Hives_Queima_Das_Fitas_Coimbra_2012_%2823514791%29.jpeg/220px-The_Hives_Queima_Das_Fitas_Coimbra_2012_%2823514791%29.jpeg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/The_Hives_Queima_Das_Fitas_Coimbra_2012_%2823514791%29.jpeg/330px-The_Hives_Queima_Das_Fitas_Coimbra_2012_%2823514791%29.jpeg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/The_Hives_Queima_Das_Fitas_Coimbra_2012_%2823514791%29.jpeg/440px-The_Hives_Queima_Das_Fitas_Coimbra_2012_%2823514791%29.jpeg 2x" data-file-width="1152" data-file-height="768" /></a><figcaption>Swedish rock band <a href="/wiki/The_Hives" title="The Hives">The Hives</a> at <a href="/wiki/Queima_das_Fitas" title="Queima das Fitas">Queima das Fitas Festival</a> of Coimbra in 2012.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The student festivals of <i><a href="/wiki/Queima_das_Fitas" title="Queima das Fitas">Queima das Fitas</a>,</i> which are major events in a number of cities across Portugal, show every year a selection of well-established, high-profile musicians and bands to the public as well as newer, on the rise, upcoming success artists seeking definite recognition.<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2005, Portugal held the <a href="/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Awards" title="MTV Europe Music Awards">MTV Europe Music Awards</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Pavilh%C3%A3o_Atl%C3%A2ntico" class="mw-redirect" title="Pavilhão Atlântico">Pavilhão Atlântico</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lisbon" title="Lisbon">Lisbon</a>. Furthermore, Portugal won the <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2017" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2017">Eurovision Song Contest 2017</a> in <a href="/wiki/Kyiv" title="Kyiv">Kyiv</a> with the song "<a href="/wiki/Amar_pelos_dois" title="Amar pelos dois">Amar pelos dois</a>" presented by <a href="/wiki/Salvador_Sobral" title="Salvador Sobral">Salvador Sobral</a>, and subsequently hosted the <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2018" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2018">2018 contest</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Altice_Arena" title="Altice Arena">Altice Arena</a> in <a href="/wiki/Lisbon" title="Lisbon">Lisbon</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Sport">Sport</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=51" title="Edit section: Sport">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Sport_in_Portugal" title="Sport in Portugal">Sport in Portugal</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:IRNPOR_match_2018_FIFA_World_Cup_11_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/IRNPOR_match_2018_FIFA_World_Cup_11_%28cropped%29.jpg/170px-IRNPOR_match_2018_FIFA_World_Cup_11_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="213" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/IRNPOR_match_2018_FIFA_World_Cup_11_%28cropped%29.jpg/255px-IRNPOR_match_2018_FIFA_World_Cup_11_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/IRNPOR_match_2018_FIFA_World_Cup_11_%28cropped%29.jpg/340px-IRNPOR_match_2018_FIFA_World_Cup_11_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="638" data-file-height="800" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo" title="Cristiano Ronaldo">Cristiano Ronaldo</a> is considered to be one of the greatest football players of all time.<sup id="cite_ref-345" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-345">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Association_football" title="Association football">Football</a> is the most popular sport in Portugal. There are several football competitions ranging from local amateur to world-class professional level. The legendary <a href="/wiki/Eus%C3%A9bio" title="Eusébio">Eusébio</a> is still a major symbol of <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_football" class="mw-redirect" title="Portuguese football">Portuguese football</a> history. <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Player_of_the_Year" title="FIFA World Player of the Year">FIFA World Player of the Year</a> winners <a href="/wiki/Lu%C3%ADs_Figo" title="Luís Figo">Luís Figo</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo" title="Cristiano Ronaldo">Cristiano Ronaldo</a>, who won the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Ballon_d%27Or" title="FIFA Ballon d&#39;Or">FIFA Ballon d'Or</a>, are two world-class Portuguese football players. Portuguese football managers are also noteworthy, with <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho" title="José Mourinho">José Mourinho</a><sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Abel_Ferreira" title="Abel Ferreira">Abel Ferreira</a><sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup> being among the most renowned.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team" title="Portugal national football team">Portugal national football team</a>&#160;– <i>Seleção Nacional</i>&#160;– have won one <a href="/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship" title="UEFA European Championship">UEFA European Championship</a> title: the <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016" title="UEFA Euro 2016">UEFA Euro 2016</a>, with a 1–0 victory in the <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016_Final" class="mw-redirect" title="UEFA Euro 2016 Final">final</a> over <a href="/wiki/France_national_football_team" title="France national football team">France</a>, the tournament hosts. In addition, Portugal finished first in the <a href="/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Nations_League" title="2018–19 UEFA Nations League">2018–19 UEFA Nations League</a> with a 1–0 win over the <a href="/wiki/Netherlands_national_football_team" title="Netherlands national football team">Netherlands</a> in the <a href="/wiki/2019_UEFA_Nations_League_Final" class="mw-redirect" title="2019 UEFA Nations League Final">final</a> (held in Portugal), second in the <a href="/wiki/2004_European_Football_Championship" class="mw-redirect" title="2004 European Football Championship">Euro 2004</a> (also held in Portugal), third in the <a href="/wiki/1966_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1966 FIFA World Cup">1966 FIFA World Cup</a> and <a href="/wiki/2017_FIFA_Confederations_Cup" title="2017 FIFA Confederations Cup">2017 FIFA Confederations Cup</a>, and fourth in the <a href="/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2006 FIFA World Cup">2006 FIFA World Cup</a>. At youth level, Portugal have won two <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Youth_Championship" class="mw-redirect" title="FIFA World Youth Championship">FIFA World Youth Championships</a> (in <a href="/wiki/1989_FIFA_World_Youth_Championship" title="1989 FIFA World Youth Championship">1989</a> and <a href="/wiki/1991_FIFA_World_Youth_Championship" title="1991 FIFA World Youth Championship">1991</a>) and several <a href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">UEFA</a> European Youth Championships.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Sele%C3%A7%C3%A3o_Portuguesa_de_H%C3%B3quei_em_Patins_-_01.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Sele%C3%A7%C3%A3o_Portuguesa_de_H%C3%B3quei_em_Patins_-_01.jpg/220px-Sele%C3%A7%C3%A3o_Portuguesa_de_H%C3%B3quei_em_Patins_-_01.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="132" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Sele%C3%A7%C3%A3o_Portuguesa_de_H%C3%B3quei_em_Patins_-_01.jpg/330px-Sele%C3%A7%C3%A3o_Portuguesa_de_H%C3%B3quei_em_Patins_-_01.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Sele%C3%A7%C3%A3o_Portuguesa_de_H%C3%B3quei_em_Patins_-_01.jpg/440px-Sele%C3%A7%C3%A3o_Portuguesa_de_H%C3%B3quei_em_Patins_-_01.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3000" data-file-height="1800" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Portugal_national_roller_hockey_team" title="Portugal national roller hockey team">Portugal national roller hockey</a> team, 2014. Historically, roller hockey is popular in Portugal and its national team has won several major competitions.</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/S.L._Benfica" title="S.L. Benfica">S.L. Benfica</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sporting_CP" title="Sporting CP">Sporting CP</a> and <a href="/wiki/FC_Porto" title="FC Porto">FC Porto</a> are the largest <a href="/wiki/Sports_clubs" class="mw-redirect" title="Sports clubs">sports clubs</a> by popularity and by number of trophies won, often known as "<i>os três grandes</i>" (<a href="/wiki/Big_Three_(Portugal)" title="Big Three (Portugal)">"the big three"</a>). They have won eight titles in the European <a href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">UEFA</a> club competitions, were present in 21 finals and have been regular contenders in the last stages almost every season. Other than football, many Portuguese sports clubs, including the "big three", compete in several other sports events with a varying level of success and popularity, these may include <a href="/wiki/Roller_hockey_(quad)" title="Roller hockey (quad)">roller hockey</a>, <a href="/wiki/Basketball" title="Basketball">basketball</a>, <a href="/wiki/Futsal" title="Futsal">futsal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Team_handball" class="mw-redirect" title="Team handball">handball</a>, <a href="/wiki/Volleyball" title="Volleyball">volleyball</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sport_of_athletics" title="Sport of athletics">athletics</a>.
The <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Football_Federation" title="Portuguese Football Federation">Portuguese Football Federation</a> (FPF) &#160;– <i>Federação Portuguesa de Futebol</i>&#160;– annually hosts the <a href="/wiki/Algarve_Cup" title="Algarve Cup">Algarve Cup</a>, a prestigious <a href="/wiki/Women%27s_association_football" title="Women&#39;s association football">women's football</a> tournament that has been celebrated in the Portuguese region of <a href="/wiki/Algarve" title="Algarve">Algarve</a>.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Portugal_national_rugby_union_team" title="Portugal national rugby union team">Portuguese national rugby union team</a> qualified for the <a href="/wiki/2007_Rugby_World_Cup" title="2007 Rugby World Cup">2007 Rugby World Cup</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Portugal_national_rugby_sevens_team" title="Portugal national rugby sevens team">Portuguese national rugby sevens team</a> has played in the <a href="/wiki/World_Rugby_Sevens_Series" class="mw-redirect" title="World Rugby Sevens Series">World Rugby Sevens Series</a>.
</p>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tleft"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:352px;max-width:352px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:122px;max-width:122px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:187px;overflow:hidden"><span typeof="mw:File"><a class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Nelson_%C3%89vora" title="Nelson Évora">Nelson Évora</a> won gold in triple jump at the Olympics among other major competitions.</div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:226px;max-width:226px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:187px;overflow:hidden"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:814_mamona_hinkstapkampioene_(28463062821).jpg" //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/814_mamona_hinkstapkampioene_%2828463062821%29.jpg/448px-814_mamona_hinkstapkampioene_%2828463062821%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1258" data-file-height="1050" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Patr%C3%ADcia_Mamona" title="Patrícia Mamona">Patrícia Mamona</a> won gold at European athletics and indoor championships as well as silver at the Olympics.</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Athletics_(sport)" class="mw-redirect" title="Athletics (sport)">athletics</a>, the Portuguese have won a number of gold, silver and bronze medals in the European, World and Olympic Games competitions. <a href="/wiki/Road_bicycle_racing" title="Road bicycle racing">Road cycling</a>, with <a href="/wiki/Volta_a_Portugal" title="Volta a Portugal">Volta a Portugal</a> being the most important race, is also a popular sports event and includes professional cycling teams such as <a href="/wiki/Sporting_CP" title="Sporting CP">Sporting CP</a>, <a href="/wiki/Boavista_(cycling_team)" class="mw-redirect" title="Boavista (cycling team)">Boavista</a>, <a href="/wiki/Clube_de_Ciclismo_de_Tavira" class="mw-redirect" title="Clube de Ciclismo de Tavira">Clube de Ciclismo de Tavira</a> and <a href="/wiki/Uni%C3%A3o_Ciclista_da_Maia" title="União Ciclista da Maia">União Ciclista da Maia</a>. At international level, Portuguese cyclists have already achieved good results. <a href="/wiki/Joaquim_Agostinho" title="Joaquim Agostinho">Joaquim Agostinho</a> finished on the podium in 1978 and 1979 <a href="/wiki/Tour_de_France" title="Tour de France">Tour de France</a>, and 1974 <a href="/wiki/Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a" title="Vuelta a España">Vuelta a España</a>. <a href="/wiki/Rui_Costa_(cyclist)" title="Rui Costa (cyclist)">Rui Costa</a> has won the <a href="/wiki/UCI_Road_World_Championships" title="UCI Road World Championships">world title</a> in the men's road race.
</p><p>The country has also achieved notable performances in sports including <a href="/wiki/Fencing" title="Fencing">fencing</a>, <a href="/wiki/Judo" title="Judo">judo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kitesurf" class="mw-redirect" title="Kitesurf">kitesurf</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rowing_(sport)" title="Rowing (sport)">rowing</a>, sailing, <a href="/wiki/Surfing" title="Surfing">surfing</a>, shooting, <a href="/wiki/Taekwondo" title="Taekwondo">taekwondo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Triathlon" title="Triathlon">triathlon</a> and <a href="/wiki/Windsurfing" title="Windsurfing">windsurfing</a>, winning several European and world titles. Portugal's <a href="/wiki/Paralympic" class="mw-redirect" title="Paralympic">paralympic</a> athletes have also won many medals in sports including <a href="/wiki/Swimming_(sport)" title="Swimming (sport)">swimming</a>, <a href="/wiki/Boccia" title="Boccia">boccia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sport_of_athletics" title="Sport of athletics">athletics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts" title="Mixed martial arts">mixed martial arts</a> and <a href="/wiki/Wrestling" title="Wrestling">wrestling</a>.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Sepang_Victory_(2017)_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Sepang_Victory_%282017%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/170px-Sepang_Victory_%282017%29_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="205" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Sepang_Victory_%282017%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/255px-Sepang_Victory_%282017%29_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Sepang_Victory_%282017%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/340px-Sepang_Victory_%282017%29_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="667" data-file-height="805" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Miguel_Oliveira" title="Miguel Oliveira">Miguel Oliveira</a>, Portuguese professional motorcycle racer</figcaption></figure>
<p>In motorsport, Portugal is internationally noted for the <a href="/wiki/Rally_of_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Rally of Portugal">Rally of Portugal</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Estoril_Circuit" class="mw-redirect" title="Estoril Circuit">Estoril</a> and <a href="/wiki/Algarve_Circuit" class="mw-redirect" title="Algarve Circuit">Algarve Circuits</a> as well as the revived <a href="/wiki/Porto_Street_Circuit" class="mw-redirect" title="Porto Street Circuit">Porto Street Circuit</a> which holds a stage of the WTCC every two years, as well as for a number of internationally noted pilots and racers such as <a href="/wiki/Miguel_Oliveira" title="Miguel Oliveira">Miguel Oliveira</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tiago_Monteiro" title="Tiago Monteiro">Tiago Monteiro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_F%C3%A9lix_da_Costa" title="António Félix da Costa">António Félix da Costa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Filipe_Albuquerque" title="Filipe Albuquerque">Filipe Albuquerque</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pedro_Lamy" title="Pedro Lamy">Pedro Lamy</a>, <a href="/wiki/Armindo_Ara%C3%BAjo" title="Armindo Araújo">Armindo Araújo</a> and others in a wide range of varied <a href="/wiki/Motorsports" class="mw-redirect" title="Motorsports">motorsports</a>.
</p><p>In equestrian sports, Portugal won the only Horseball-Pato World Championship in 2006 achieved the third position in the First <a href="/wiki/Horseball" title="Horseball">Horseball</a> World Cup and has achieved several victories in the European <a href="/wiki/Working_Equitation" class="mw-redirect" title="Working Equitation">Working Equitation</a> Championship.
</p><p>In water sports, Portugal has three major sports: <a href="/wiki/Swimming_(sport)" title="Swimming (sport)">swimming</a>, <a href="/wiki/Water_polo" title="Water polo">water polo</a> and <a href="/wiki/Surfing" title="Surfing">surfing</a>. Most recently, Portugal had success in <a href="/wiki/Canoeing" title="Canoeing">canoeing</a> with several world and European champions, such as olympic medalists. Annually, the country also hosts one of the stages of the <a href="/wiki/World_Surf_League" title="World Surf League">World Surf League</a> men's and women's <i>Championship Tour</i>, the <a href="/wiki/MEO_Rip_Curl_Pro_Portugal" title="MEO Rip Curl Pro Portugal">MEO Rip Curl Pro Portugal</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Supertubos" title="Supertubos">Supertubos</a> in <a href="/wiki/Peniche,_Portugal" title="Peniche, Portugal">Peniche</a>.
</p><p>Northern Portugal has its own original <a href="/wiki/Martial_art" class="mw-redirect" title="Martial art">martial art</a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Jogo_do_Pau" class="mw-redirect" title="Jogo do Pau">Jogo do Pau</a></i>, in which the fighters use staffs to confront one or several opponents. Other popular sport-related recreational outdoor activities with thousands of enthusiasts nationwide include <a href="/wiki/Airsoft" title="Airsoft">airsoft</a>, fishing, <a href="/wiki/Golf" title="Golf">golf</a>, hiking, hunting and <a href="/wiki/Orienteering" title="Orienteering">orienteering</a>.
</p><p>Portugal is one of the world's best <a href="/wiki/Golf" title="Golf">golf</a> destinations.<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup> It has received several awards by the World Golf Awards.<sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>High-profile, successful competitive athleticism and sportsmanship in Portugal can be traced back to the time of <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Rome" title="Ancient Rome">Ancient Rome</a>. <a href="/wiki/Gaius_Appuleius_Diocles" title="Gaius Appuleius Diocles">Gaius Appuleius Diocles</a> (104&#160;&#8211;&#32;after 146 AD) was a noteworthy <a href="/wiki/Chariot_racing" title="Chariot racing">charioteer</a> born in <a href="/wiki/Lamego,_Portugal" class="mw-redirect" title="Lamego, Portugal">Lamego</a> who became one of the most celebrated athletes in <a href="/wiki/Ancient_history" title="Ancient history">ancient history</a>. He is often cited as the <a href="/wiki/Forbes%27_list_of_the_world%27s_highest-paid_athletes" class="mw-redirect" title="Forbes&#39; list of the world&#39;s highest-paid athletes">highest-paid athlete of all time</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-laphamsquarterly.org_350-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-laphamsquarterly.org-350">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Struck_351-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Struck-351">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Visual_arts">Visual arts</span><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Portugal&amp;action=edit&amp;section=52" title="Edit section: Visual arts">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_art" title="Portuguese art">Portuguese art</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:A_Adora%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_Magos_(1828)_-_Domingos_Sequeira.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/A_Adora%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_Magos_%281828%29_-_Domingos_Sequeira.png/220px-A_Adora%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_Magos_%281828%29_-_Domingos_Sequeira.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="159" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/A_Adora%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_Magos_%281828%29_-_Domingos_Sequeira.png/330px-A_Adora%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_Magos_%281828%29_-_Domingos_Sequeira.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/A_Adora%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_Magos_%281828%29_-_Domingos_Sequeira.png/440px-A_Adora%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_Magos_%281828%29_-_Domingos_Sequeira.png 2x" data-file-width="2210" data-file-height="1599" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Domingos_Sequeira" title="Domingos Sequeira">Domingos Sequeira</a> was one of the most prolific <a href="/wiki/Neoclassicism" title="Neoclassicism">neoclassical</a> painters. (<a href="/wiki/Adoration_of_the_Magi_(Sequeira)" title="Adoration of the Magi (Sequeira)"><i>Adoration of the Magi</i>; 1828</a>).</figcaption></figure>
<p>Portugal has a <a href="/wiki/List_of_Portuguese_artists" title="List of Portuguese artists">rich history in painting</a>. The first well-known painters dating back to the 15th century&#160;– like <a href="/wiki/Nuno_Gon%C3%A7alves" title="Nuno Gonçalves">Nuno Gonçalves</a> and <a href="/wiki/Gr%C3%A3o_Vasco" class="mw-redirect" title="Grão Vasco">Vasco Fernandes</a>&#160;– were part of the late Gothic painting period. During the Renaissance, Portuguese painting was highly influenced by Northern European painting. In the Baroque period <a href="/wiki/Josefa_de_%C3%93bidos" title="Josefa de Óbidos">Josefa de Óbidos</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vieira_Lusitano" title="Vieira Lusitano">Vieira Lusitano</a> were the most prolific painters.
<a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Malhoa" title="José Malhoa">José Malhoa</a>, known for his work <i>Fado</i>, and <a href="/wiki/Columbano_Bordalo_Pinheiro" title="Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro">Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro</a> (who painted the portraits of <a href="/wiki/Te%C3%B3filo_Braga" title="Teófilo Braga">Teófilo Braga</a> and <a href="/wiki/Antero_de_Quental" title="Antero de Quental">Antero de Quental</a>) were both references in <a href="/wiki/Naturalist_school_of_painting" class="mw-redirect" title="Naturalist school of painting">naturalist painting</a>.
</p><p>The 20th century saw the arrival of <a href="/wiki/Modernism" title="Modernism">Modernism</a>, and along with it came the most prominent Portuguese painters: <a href="/wiki/Amadeo_de_Souza-Cardoso" class="mw-redirect" title="Amadeo de Souza-Cardoso">Amadeo de Souza-Cardoso</a>, who was heavily influenced by French painters, particularly the Delaunays (<a href="/wiki/Robert_Delaunay" title="Robert Delaunay">Robert</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sonia_Delaunay" title="Sonia Delaunay">Sonia</a>). Among his best-known works is <i>Canção Popular a Russa e o Fígaro</i>. Other great modernist painters/writers include <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Botelho" title="Carlos Botelho">Carlos Botelho</a> and <a href="/wiki/Almada_Negreiros" title="Almada Negreiros">Almada Negreiros</a>, friend to the poet <a href="/wiki/Fernando_Pessoa" title="Fernando Pessoa">Fernando Pessoa</a>, who painted Pessoa's portrait. He was deeply influenced by both <a href="/wiki/Cubist" class="mw-redirect" title="Cubist">Cubist</a> and <a href="/wiki/Futurism_(art)" class="mw-redirect" title="Futurism (art)">Futurist</a> trends.
</p><p>Prominent international figures in visual arts nowadays include painters <a href="/wiki/Vieira_da_Silva" class="mw-redirect" title="Vieira da Silva">Vieira da Silva</a>, <a href="/wiki/J%C3%BAlio_Pomar" title="Júlio Pomar">Júlio Pomar</a>, Helena Almeida, <a href="/wiki/Joana_Vasconcelos" title="Joana Vasconcelos">Joana Vasconcelos</a>, <a href="/wiki/Juli%C3%A3o_Sarmento" title="Julião Sarmento">Julião Sarmento</a> and <a href="/wiki/Paula_Rego" title="Paula Rego">Paula Rego</a>.
</p>
